articleTitle: HVDC insulation systems: effect of voltage polarity inversion slew rate on partial discharge phenomenology and harmfulness
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The design of HVDC insulation systems has to take into account various factors which can be neglected under AC, especially the dependence of conductivity on temperature and field and the issue of electric field transient during energization and polarity inversion. The electric field transient in the presence of temperature gradients and/or inhomogeneities, as cavities, can take significantly long times to go from the initial permittivity-driven distribution to that pertinent to DC-steady state, where conductivity rules the field profile in insulation and its maximum value. If conditions occur that can incept partial discharges, in steady state and/or during transient, they can cause considerable damage to insulation. When the mean voltage transient rate during operation is significant, aging can be locally accelerated, and the overall insulation life and reliability reduced. This paper focuses on possible remedy actions, which are related to the amount of damage as a function of voltage slew rate and of rest time between opposite-polarity voltage steps. The impact of voltage rise time during voltage polarity inversion on PD magnitude and repetition rate, and relevant damage, is analyzed based on experimental measurements and an aging model. It is shown that lower voltage slew rate and shorter rest time at a constant voltage slew rate can be beneficial to reduce the damage associate to PD incepted during voltage transients.

articleTitle: Lightning impulse performance of natural ester oil based nanofluid with magnesium oxide nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Using natural oils as a substitute for mineral oils has drawn the attention of researchers with respect to environmental regulations. In addition, the usage of natural ester based nanofluids helps in enhancing their properties. In this study, natural ester oil based nanofluids are prepared by employing magnesium oxide nanoparticles due to their excellent physical and thermal properties. Nanofluids with different nanoparticles concentration have been subjected to lightning impulse voltage to investigate their electrical performance. A one-stage impulse generator has been used to produce lightning impulse voltage of 1.2/50μs; the impulse dielectric strength of liquid insulation is investigated by using needle to plane configuration. The impulse voltage and the transient current are measured, while the time to breakdown is recorded, in order to investigate the lightning performance of the nanofluid in various concentrations by following step up method. In addition, 20 shots are performed at each level to help in obtaining the probability of the lightning breakdown voltage. The prepared natural ester oil based nanofluids show better performance, by means of increased U<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50%</sub> than the base oil.

articleTitle: Grounding system of medium voltage network with integrated distributed generation: short-circuit analysis and calculation of the developed potentials
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In modern overhead Medium Voltage power networks, with high RES penetration, remote-controlled coupling and protection systems (Load Breakers, Reclosers and Sectionalizers) are increasingly being installed in order to control network's bi-directional power flow and to protect personnel and equipment against short-circuits. Most of those systems consist of a control panel on a metal enclosure that is accessible either by qualified personnel or by passers-by. For this reason, it is necessary to study the adequacy of the grounding system, in order to ensure the reduction of the developed touch and step voltages in case of a short-circuit on the network. In this paper, the performance of a grounding system is being evaluated, considering various scenarios, by using appropriate software tools. Purpose of the present work is to perform risk analysis and identify the worst-case scenario that should be considered during the design of grounding grids on distribution networks as well as to spotlight critical design parameters, taking into account techno-economical criteria. Finally, the results to be extracted from this paper are expected to be a guide for the optimal design of the grounding system of distribution networks.

articleTitle: SOC estimation for lithium-ion batteries based on electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and equivalent circuit model
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: As the main energy storage device of battery electric vehicles (BEV), the safety, reliability and useful life of lithium-ion batteries have been paid much attention by the industry and researchers. The state of charge (SOC) of a battery is a physical quantity representing the remaining battery power. If SOC is obtained accurately, it can not only provide reasonable operation suggestions for users and greatly improve the battery life, but also serve as the basis for estimating the state of health (SOH), thus improving the safety and reliability of the battery. In this paper, based on the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) characteristics, a fractional-order circuit model (FOECM) of the battery was established. Based on parameters of the FOECM, SOC of the battery could be estimated. This method was used to estimate another battery at 60% SOC and achieved a good estimation accuracy.

articleTitle: Beneficial electrode arrangement for electroaerodynamic propulsion
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: A pair of asymmetrical electrodes under high voltage can produce an ionic wind and thrust. This has been proposed as an alternative method to the standard airplane engines of today. The main advantages of the ionic wind propulsion are no moving parts, near silent operation, and no combustion emissions. The first prototype airplane with solid-state propulsion based on the ionic wind flew in 2018. This paper reports on experiments with different electrode configurations and designs (aluminum tubes and an airfoil NACA 0021) for the generation of thrust by corona discharges. Some beneficial electrode arrangements are identified and a configuration with two grounded collector electrodes shows a maximum thrust of 820 mN/m and a thrust-topower ratio of 14.1 N/kW for a thrust of 100 mN/m. An EAD aircraft design for a flying wing UAV is discussed.

articleTitle: Estimation of state of charge of lithium battery based on electrochemical impedance spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The electrochemical reaction of lithium-ion power batteries is easily affected by temperature, which leads to changes in battery capacity. In order to accurately predict the battery states of charge(SOC) and provide a basis for battery management strategies, this paper measures and studies lithium-ion batteries with different SOC in a wide temperature range based on electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. An online estimation method of battery SOC based on electrochemical impedance spectroscopy is proposed.The experimental results show that, within the normal operating temperature (15-45°C) of the lithium battery, the SOC hardly has any effect on the battery impedance phase. We compared the impedance amplitude changes under different SOCs and choose 100 Hz as the characteristic frequency. The 100HZ impedance amplitude is used to estimate the battery SOC. Finally, the experimental results show that the SOC estimation model established in this paper can control the estimation error within 4%. This article proves that the impedance spectrum amplitude has a good characterization ability for battery SOC, which can provide a reference for accurate estimation of battery SOC and improve battery safety.

articleTitle: The influence of degassing time and curing time on insulation behaviours of silicone gel in IGBT modules
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The silicone gel is used to encapsulate insulated gate bipolar transistor (IGBT) modules. It can prevent electrical discharges and protect semiconductors against humidity, dust, and vibration. The silicone gel has to be processed through mixing, degassing and curing. These procedures will affect the insulation behaviours of silicone gel, including the degassing time and curing time. Partial discharge (PD) and electrical tree, which are warning signals of insulation failure, appear at different voltages when processing conditions are changed. However, the way how these conditions affect phenomena is not clear. Therefore, this paper investigates the influence of processing conditions on partial discharge and electrical tree. The experimental study is conducted by needle-plate electrodes under AC voltage. The results demonstrate that the degassing time has a positive influence on the insulation performance, while the curing time makes a little positive effect on insulation behaviours. And the article also suggests a suitable operating procedure which insulation behaviours need.

articleTitle: Influence of thermal aging on the physical characteristics of liquid silicone rubber
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Composite insulators with silicone rubber sheds are becoming more and more popular in the past few decades due to their excellent properties, especially hydrophobic transfer ability. Compared to traditional high temperature vulcanized silicone rubber, liquid silicone rubber shows great advantage for good fluidity and simple moulding process, making it perfect for the manufacture of insulators with large diameters. Considering the operation conditions, thermal aging of insulating materials is of great significance for power transmission. In this paper, aging of silicone rubber composites under different temperatures are conducted for 2000 h. Influence of thermal aging on the basic characteristics of sample is investigated, including hardness, hydrophobicity and mechanical strength. The results indicate that the performance of liquid silicone rubber used in this paper meet well the requirements for composite insulators.

articleTitle: Surface charge inversion algorithm of non-invasive surface potential measurement
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The inversion algorithm attracts much attention since it converts surface potential to the distribution of surface charges on solid insulation. The surface charge inversion algorithm for surface potential measurement was affected by both the shape of the testing sample and the experimental methods. This paper proposes a surface charge inversion algorithm for a non-invasive surface potential measurement, which was previously reported to investigate the surface charge distribution during highvoltage application. As for the non-invasive surface potential measurement, the high voltage is applied to one side of the solid dielectric film (charged surface) and the surface potential of the other side (measured surface) is measured. The inversion algorithm based on electrostatic simulation converts the surface potential of the measured surface to the surface charge density of the charged surface. The proposed algorithm is used to restore the surface charge distribution between two finger electrodes. The inversion matrix is a diagonal-like matrix, and the unit surface charge on the charged surface affects the potential of the measured surface on a large area. The inversion algorithm is verified through a reconstruction of a pre-set surface charge distribution with voltage application. The maximum relative error of the inversion algorithm was 10% of the minimum applied charge. The algorithm is applicable to surface charge inversion for non-invasive surface potential measurement under high voltage application and provides references for surface charge investigations.

articleTitle: Flashover voltage estimation of cone-type GIS spacer with permittivity graded materials (ε-FGM) by volume-time theory in consideration with conductor surface roughness in SF6 GAS
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Toward the compact gas insulated switchgears (GIS) and transmission lines (GIL), we have been investigating a novel electric field grading technique around the GIS spacer by ``functionally graded materials (FGM)'' with spatial distribution of permittivity (ε-FGM). We have already designed and fabricated the cone-type ε-FGM spacer samples with the relative permittivity distribution between 10 and 4 for 245 kV class GIS and obtained the higher flashover voltage (FOV) than that of the spacer samples with uniform permittivity. In this paper, in order to verify the estimated FOV of the ε-FGM spacer samples, we estimated the theoretical discharge inception voltage (TDIV<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</sub>) by the analytical approach with the extended Volume-Time theory in consideration with the conductor surface roughness. The estimated TDIV50 of the ε-FGM spacer sample was verified to be consistent with the measured FOV and higher by 28 % in SF6 gas at 0.6 MPa-abs than that of the conventional spacer sample.

articleTitle: Data reliability of rfid temperature sensor applied to switchgear
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: This paper uses multi-physical field coupling finite element model to study the temperature distribution of the distribution switchgear and the influence of different arrangement and encapsulation on heat transfer efficiency. The temperature distribution and different sensor encapsulation of low voltage switchgear is simulated. The results show the temperature distribution inside the switchgear, especially the position of the hot spot is beneficial to the arrangement of the sensor. The temperature sensor arranged in the plum contact encapsulation is improved, and the improved temperature sensor encapsulation has a certain increase in data reliability and operating life.

articleTitle: Experimental practice implemented to improve meaningfulness of prequalification tests for extruded HVDC 525kV land and submarine cables
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The paper describes the extra tests practiced in prequalification (PQ) tests on extruded HVDC 525kV land and submarine cables to help understand the possible changes of insulation properties. The success criteria defined by CIGRE TB.496 for the current PQ tests are the results of insulation without breakdown during all performed tests and the pass of dissection examination. However, it is lack of insight information of cable insulation property changes caused by long term load cycles (LC) and test voltage applications, To overcome these drawbacks, the reported work firstly developed full-size cable space charge measuring technology by pulsed electro-acoustic method (PEA) and conducted reference measurement before PQ tests on a section of outer sheath removed cable under different voltages and polarities.This section of cable for PEA measurement was replaced by pre-modelled joint and the similar tests will be carried out after designed LC tests. This practice is expected to evaluate space charge performance both in terms of its profile and accumulation. Secondly, the leakage current in the cable insulation are continuously monitored during HVDC 525kV cable load cycle test to obtain the electrical performance changes which could be introduced to cable insulation under electrical and thermal stress. Moreover, the partial discharge test under AC voltage was carried out on the PQ tests setups as well to ensure the testing loops without any defects which could jeopardise this costly and time consuming tests. The results partial discharge under AC 420kV has approved the electrical performance and installation quality of PQ testing loops.

articleTitle: Impulse overvoltage on stator winding of direct-drive wind turbine generators
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Analysing the impulse overvoltage along stator wingdings are quite significant for the optimization of insulation design in direct-drive wind turbine generators. In this paper, the accurate repetitive impulse overvoltage and its distribution characteristic along the stator windings of 2.5MW direct-drive generator are analysed by means of simulation combined with experiment. The equivalent circuit model of three-phase stator windings with the basic unit of turn conductors is established based on the PSCAD/EMTDC software, considering the frequency-dependent parameters such as inductance and resistance. A laboratory experiment platform with the 2.5MW turbine generator under the excitation of three-phase PWM converter is set up. The obtained results indicate that the simulation and experiment are in good agreement. The characteristics of repetitive overvoltage along stator windings under three-phase excitation are of great significance to improve the quality and insulation design of wind turbine generator. The coil-to-ground and coil-to-coil peak voltages slightly decreased from the terminal to the neutral point of a phase winding. Moreover, the voltage drop cross the first coil is mainly concentrated on the first inter-turn.

articleTitle: Basic behaviour of FRA measurements on rotating machines
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Mechanical stresses in the operation of rotating machines can cause faults. Especially the detection of rod ruptures in the squirrel cage of induction machines or in the damper winding of synchronous machines is time-consuming, as these have been so far found mainly via visual inspection. To overcome this issue, this paper focuses on the applicability of Frequency Response Analysis (FRA) for rotating machines as a reliable and reproducible method for condition assessment and fault diagnosis. The basics of FRA are described and the fundamental trace for rotating machines is shown and explained. The good reproducibility of the method is shown by defining influencing factors and their effects on the frequency response. A new visualization approach is used, allowing to outline the impacts based on the rotor angle, which might also help for the later identification of even small faults. Furthermore, the frequency response for various machine types and power classes is discussed. It is shown, that a general trace exists, even if there are shifts in frequency ranges and deviations due to design dissimilarities. In order to verify the findings regarding the fundamental behaviour of the frequency response, an approach for an electrical model is made using the grey box modelling method.

articleTitle: Current field distribution calculation for water-blocking cushion layer of HV XLPE cable
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In order to explore the root cause of the erosion phenomenon of the water-blocking cushion layer in the high-voltage cable, reproduce the whole process of its occurrence and development, and determine the relevant influencing factors and damage mechanism, a simulation model is established and the current field distribution is studied in this paper, taking 110kV XLPE cable as an example. Through simulation, this paper obtains the cloud diagram of the potential, electric field, and current density distribution in the cable model, considering the number of layers around the cushion layer, Cable conductor cross-sectional area, the amount of interference fit between the aluminum sheath and the cushion layer, and esistivity of aluminum sheath (simulating white powder generation). Increasing the number of wrapping layers of the cushion layer and increasing the interference fit between the cushion layer and the aluminum sheath can reduce the concentration of current density distribution in the cable. Among them, increasing the number of wrapping layers of the cushion layer improves the current in the insulation shielding layer. The distribution effect is obvious, and increasing the interference fit is more effective in reducing the current density at the interface between the aluminum sheath and the cushion layer.

articleTitle: Influence of the blocking element on the front of a HVDC-lightning impulse composite voltage
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The decarbonisation of the electrical power system makes the expansion and conversion of the existing electrical energy networks unavoidable. In some cases, for example the connection of offshore wind-farms to the existing grids, the high voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission proves to be advantageous. Nevertheless, the integration of new transmission technologies has to continue to provide the high security of electrical power supply. Therefore, all electrical components have to withstand several tests. In addition to the high voltage test with pure loads, such as DC and impulse voltages, testing with composite voltages, e.g. DC and lightning impulse (LI) voltage, is state-of-the-art for HVDC components. Special test circuits with blocking and coupling elements for the different voltage sources are used to generate these composite voltages. The blocking and coupling elements influence the shape of the composite voltage, thus affecting the reproducibility of the voltage waveform, which is necessary for standardised tests. This study presents the results from measurements of composite voltages consisting of DC and LI voltages with different blocking and coupling elements. The influence of the elements on the front and on the shape of the composite voltage is examined. Derived from the results, recommendations for the test execution are given.

articleTitle: Moisture assessment of oil-impregnated pressboard by switching impulse application
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: This paper discusses about an advanced technique for assessing the condition of oil-paper insulation by switching impulse application. For this purpose, an experimental setup has been developed in the laboratory which can generate impulse voltage with varying peak and front time. A module has been made in the laboratory which can measure both impulse voltage and corresponding dielectric response current. Using the setup, switching impulse voltage has been applied to the oil impregnated pressboards with different moisture content. Based on the measured voltage and current data, tanδ of the pressboard has been evaluated over the frequency range of 100Hz to 5 kHz. The tanδ profile calculated under switching impulse has been compared with the tanδ values obtained from DIRANA measurement over the mentioned frequency range. Comparison results show that, both the tanδ values hold good agreement with each other. The front time and peak of the applied switching impulse has been varied to investigate their effect on tanδ profile. Furthermore, the effect of temperature on the oil impregnated pressboard has been studied under switching impulse voltage. Finally, the proposed technique has been applied to a distribution transformer for investigating its insulation condition.

articleTitle: Research on linearity measurement method of impulse current measuring devices
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Linearity is a key technical parameter of the impulse current converting devices which directly affects the measurement accuracy of the impulse current measuring system. The factors affecting the linearity of different types of impulse current converting devices have been studied. Standard devices for on-site calibration of the linearity of industrial-grade impulse current measuring devices have been developed, including multilayer PCB-type Rogowski coils and magnetic field sensors based on Archimedes coil modules. Different linearity evaluation methods such as temperature rise calculation method, equivalent energy method, compared with Rogowski coil, compared with magnetic field sensor have been studied and tested. For a 100kA shunt-based impulse current measuring system, the test methods, applicable conditions and measurement levels of different methods are compared. The test results show that the linearity measurement results of several methods differ by about 0.7%, and it is more practical to compare with the linearity standard device under the condition of not knowing the material characteristics of the shunt.

articleTitle: Combined kerr-effect and polarization current measurements in oil-pressboard barrier systems
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: This paper focuses on Kerr-effect and simultaneous polarization current measurements in a laboratory-scale mineral oil/pressboard arrangement in which one electrode is covered with pressboard in order to simulate real HVDC transformer insulation systems. On those arrangements, the influence of different electrical DC field stresses and oil gap widths on the transient charge carrier transport processes and the corresponding space charge phenomena is investigated. The measurement results are compared with measurements in a bare electrode arrangement with a mineral oil gap in order to examine the impact of an inserted pressboard barrier. The objective of the research is to describe the transient charge carrier transport processes and space charge phenomena in oil and oil-impregnated pressboard insulation systems. Hence, information about both, the electric field distribution and the transient conduction processes within the oil gap can be obtained. With the results, common theories about the field distribution within the insulation system can be verified and the understanding of the transient and steady state behaviour of oil-board layered insulation systems of converter transformers can be increased.

articleTitle: Discharge characteristics of actual winding turn-to-turn structure inside transformers under oscillating switching impulse voltage
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In this work a real winding turn-to-turn model is designed and manufactured and the discharge characteristics of the model is studied. Both the standard switching impulse wave and the oscillating switching impulse wave are considered in the impulse withstand test, and the selected waves are in line with IEC 60060-3 standard. During the experiment, the partial discharge pulse sequence, breakdown voltage, and discharge time lag are obtained. The results show that as the voltage amplitude increases, the number of partial discharge pulses increases significantly. The partial discharge pulses are concentrated on the peak of the oscillation period under the oscillating switching impulse voltage. And the waveform oscillation has little effect on the breakdown characteristics of the winding, and the breakdown often occurs at the peak of the first cycle. This paper provides experimental support for studying the influence of oscillating waves and double-exponential waves on the insulation characteristics of transformers.

articleTitle: Analysis of lightning protection performance of 110 kV transmission line canceling lightning wire
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The 110 kV transmission line is an essential part of high-voltage transmission lines. However, some 110 kV lines have severe icing problems and plan to use the mode of operation without the lightning wire. In this paper, the ATP software simulates the transmission line with the lightning wire canceled. Then the lightning withstanding level of the line after the lightning wire is canceled is studied. The simulation obtains the lightning withstanding level under different grounding resistance of the tower. The results show that the lightning withstanding level of the transmission line after the lightning wire is canceled lower than that of the standard transmission line. Based on the simulation results, this paper proposes using the anti-lightning and antiicing composite insulator to improve the lightning protection performance of transmission line without the lightning wire. Through simulation calculations, it finds that the lightning withstanding level of the transmission line has been dramatically improved after applying the anti-lightning and anti-icing composite insulator. It indicates that installing the anti-lightning and anti-icing composite insulator is a feasible solution on the transmission line without lightning wire.

articleTitle: Inverse analysis of optimum permittivity distribution for FGM spacer in consideration with multiple objective functions in gaseous insulation systems
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: For relaxation of electric field (E-field) stress around solid insulation spacer in HV-GIS (Gas Insulated Switchgears), we have proved the effectiveness of an application of functionally graded materials (FGM) with spatial distribution of permittivity (ε-FGM). For this purpose, we have proposed a technique for inverse analysis of the permittivity distribution in an ε-FGM spacer. The technique can provide us optimum permittivity distribution with the maximum E-field stress relaxation with less computation time. In this paper, we developed the new technique of the inverse analysis under the consideration of multiple objective functions on the insulation performances. In our study, we focus on three kinds of functions: (a) dielectric strength in SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas gap, (b) dielectric strength on the spacer surface, and (c) dielectric strength on the embedded electrode/epoxy spacer interface. Under the consideration of three objective functions, the optimum permittivity distribution in ε-FGM spacer are modified full-automatically. Through the application results to GIS spacer, we obtain the inverse analysis of optimum permittivity distribution by only 11 times of iterations. As a result, we obtained 25% improvement of insulation performance around ε-FGM spacer compared with the conventional spacer with uniform permittivity distribution.

articleTitle: DC air humidity correction factor for air external insulation revisited
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The dielectric strength of external insulation depends on atmospheric conditions such as humidity, pressure and temperature, among other parameters. For the sake of achieving proper design and/or testing of high voltage apparatus, atmospheric corrections procedures are used to translate specific site conditions or laboratory conditions to standard atmosphere conditions. IEC standards recommend atmospheric correction procedures for humidity and relative air density based on semi-empirical or empirical approaches. The recommendation provided in the standard for humidity correction was validated with experiments performed to different electrode arrangements. However, the experiments could not cover all possible configurations existing in high voltage application and inaccuracies in the application of corrections under positive switching impulses have been reported. This paper is dedicated to study the humidity correction factor used in external air insulation subject to direct voltage stress (DC). The tests were performed for quasi-uniform and non-uniform gaps. The data of the tests is compared with the recommendations of IEC standard 60060-1. The test results indicate that the humidity correction proposed in the standard is not capable to reproduce the results in a wide range of humidity and for diverse type of electrode arrangements. Moreover, the paper concludes that to avoid significant overvoltage corrections, humidity corrections shall not be applied, and new approaches shall be done in order to provide a correction in function of gap uniformity, humidity ranges and type of voltage stress.

articleTitle: Effect of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons on excitation and growth characteristics of electrical tree in polyethylene-based insulation for high voltage cables
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: High voltage cable is a considerable way for large-capacity power transmission and power grid interconnection. The deterioration of electrical trees is the main reason for the failure of polyethylene-based insulation for high voltage cables. The key to ensuring the reliability of high voltage cables is to restrain the deterioration of electrical trees in polymer insulation materials. To investigate the inhibition methods of electrical tree in polyethylene-based insulation, the effects of different photo-crosslinkers and photo-initiators of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons on the excitation and growth characteristics of electrical treeing in polyethylene-based insulation were studied. The results show that the electrical tree phenomenon occurs in polyethylene-based insulation with polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon additives under AC voltage. And the electrical tree within polyethylene-based insulation containing 1wt% photo-crosslinker triallyl cyanurate and 1wt% photo-initiator 4,4'-dichlorobenzophenone has the most diminutive length, width, and area. It is conducted that the photo-crosslinker triallyl cyanurate and photo-initiator 4,4'-dichlorobenzophenone as polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon additives inhibit the electrical tree deterioration within polyethylene-based insulation.

articleTitle: A wavelet de-noising method for partial discharge based on wavelet entropy and sparsity
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Distributed partial discharge detection is an effective tool for evaluating the insulation status of long power cables. However, on-site detection signals are often hampered by several noise sources. In this study, we developed a new wavelet-based PD de-noising method that is adaptive and scale-dependent. The new method adopts the wavelet that can minimise the value of the wavelet entropy of the approximation coefficients as the optimal wavelet at each decomposition scale. The decomposition scale that can minimise the SCR value of the detail coefficients is selected as the optimal decomposition scale. The de-noising results of the proposed method were compared with those of the method using db8 wavelet and the maximum decomposition scale. Concerning the simulated PD signal with interference, this method showed better performance in four performance evaluation parameters. Regarding the real signals obtained from a 597 m long 10-kV cable in the laboratory and a 330-kV cable on commissioning test site, the results showed that the proposed method reduces the magnitude error by 27.9% and 21.5%, respectively, and that it results in better de-noising with regard to the minimisation of pulse distortions. As such, it can be a promising approach when applied to on-site cable PD detection

articleTitle: Evaluation of transformer insulation with different PD methods using a synchronous multi-channel technique
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In the paper, an effective diagnosis of transformer winding insulation with a versatile PD measuring system is described. The system is used for the conventional (IEC 60270) and non-conventional PD measurements performed during routine tests in the factory. The PD acquisition unit is connected to different types of PD sensors: coupling capacitors, as well as inductive and transient earth voltage sensors for contemporary measurements to benefit from the advantage of each measurement method. The noise is effectively distinguished from the internal PD activity and PD sources are defined and separated by the synchronous multi-channel evaluation technique. The sensitivity of different types of PD measurements is directly compared, which is beneficial for establishing a reference for the onsite PD measurements.

articleTitle: Research on the temperature rise characteristics of converter transformer valve-side bushing and the prediction model of full state index
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The valve-side bushing of UHV converter transformer carries a large multi-frequency superimposed current, and it is prone to local overheating faults such as the copper-aluminum transition zone and the contact finger ablation of the strap. In order to verify the temperature rise characteristics of the valve-side bushing of the converter transformer, the thermal performance test system of UHV DC bushing is established in this paper. The thermal performance test method of UHV DC bushing with high ambient temperatures and multi-frequency current was put forward, and the temperature rise test was carried out. The results show that the axial and radial temperatures inside the valve-side bushing core of the converter transformer are unevenly distributed, and the temperature distribution of two types of paper-impregnated capacitive DC bushings has the characteristics of a typical first-order exponential function under the conditions of high ambient temperature and multi-frequency current. Based on the experimental results, this paper establishes a model of the axial and radial heat balance characteristics of the inner core of the bushing capacitor under multi-frequency current. The model can be used as the steady-state temperature criterion of the bushing, which has important guiding significance for the operating state monitoring of the bushing.

articleTitle: Failure diagnosis in rotating machines using fra involving the rotation angle of the rotor
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Several studies have shown, that the SFRA method is not only suitable for transformers but also for rotating machines as a tool for reliable condition diagnosis. Is has the ability to sensitively detect diverse faults, which influence the frequency response in different frequency ranges. Therefore, a condition assessment of a machine is possible. Even faults that are not directly in the electrical measuring circuit of the SFRA have an effect on the frequency response and are therefore detectable. Examples are rod ruptures in the damper cage of synchronous machines or broken rods in squirrel cages of induction machines. Conventional methods are often unable to detect this types of fault, and new, alternative methods are also often very complex and in some cases not practical. This paper focuses on the SFRA method for the detection of different failure modes involving the rotation angle of the rotor. The rotor position is altered, allowing the detection of failures without comparison to a fingerprint. This is a general and transferable approach, which might provide new possibilities for failure diagnosis in rotating machines, even if no previous SFRA measurement is available.

articleTitle: Survey on asset management strategies of electric grid operators
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The asset management enables the electric grid operators to achieve its organisational objectives. Since a characteristic feature of asset management is individuality, this study identifies similarities and differences between electric grid operators and derives which characteristics of asset management appear to be effective under which circumstances. Therefore, a questionnaire was designed to access the four topics asset management, asset strategies, health index and online monitoring systems. The answers of the participants (n = 18) were classified by the kind of system operator, the number of managed assets, the number of cost-intensive assets, and the circuit length of cables and overhead lines. The study finds cost-intensive assets and a high number of assets correlate with a higher probability of triggering maintenance measures by intervals and replacements by condition. It is also more likely that replacements have been prioritised, a health index developed, and monitoring systems installed.

articleTitle: Service experience with a novel DC current injection generator for HVDC long-term tests – 3150 a at 422 kv DC potential
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The concept of the capacitive direct current injection was presented in previous papers. The aim is to test HVDC equipment simultaneously with e.g. ±422 kV DC and 3150 A DC. First prototypes based on the concept showed good service experience, so that a generator with rated values 660 kV and 5000 A was built. This contribution presents the final overall assembly of this generator and its technical details. First long-term service experience with this concept was gained during a trial run of the test equipment with ±422 kV and 3150 A. This generally proves that such generators can be implemented for high equipment ratings and that reliable operation is possible. Further commissioning of the generator to its rated values of 660 kV and 5000 A is planned for the future.

articleTitle: Diagnostic method for partial discharge in transformer based on multiple information and application analysis
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Partial discharge (PD) may cause power transformer fault and defect, there are many methods developed to detect, diagnose and locate the PD defect. However, every method has advantages and disadvantages, there is still no a method that can solve all the problems. In this paper, detection and diagnostic technology for PD defect in a 220kV transformer based on multiple methods is introduced. Firstly, for the abnormal oil chromatography data found in the routine test, dissolved gas analysis (DGA) method is adopted, and a discharge defect is found inside the transformer. Secondly, ultra-high frequency (UHF) method, high frequency (HF) method and ultrasonic method are used to detect and diagnose the PD defect, a suspension discharge is found, consistent with the results of DGA method. Thirdly, the PD defect is located near the shielding part of phase B bushing outlet based on ultrasonic-electrical combination method, which is consistent with the actual defect position. Test results show that multiple detection methods are useful for diagnosis and location of PD defect, it provides a reference for the processing and analysis of similar anomalies in transformer.

articleTitle: Lifetime estimation of operational aged transformers with new fuzzy logic algorithms
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The ongoing aging of transformers in the power supply networks represents an increasing technical and financial risk for operators. Therefore, the knowledge of the aging condition of the asset is of elementary interest in order to be able to plan replacement and exchange measures in a time- and cost-optimized manner. Since the end of life of transformers is determined by the aging of the solid insulation, the DP value is considered to be an indicator of the aging of the entire asset. However, this can only be determined directly by paper sampling with the active part accessible, which limits its practicality. Therefore, in the past, the paper condition was estimated by means of furan derivatives. Another approach is to estimate the DP value using computer-aided methods based on other insulating oil characteristics. In this paper, the results of both estimation methods are compared with the actual DP values of real transformers to investigate the validity of this new approach. Additionally the measured furan concentration will be compared to the measured DP value from more than 50 operationally aged transformers.

articleTitle: Research on detection technology of bubble size distribution in transformer oil based on MIE scattering theeory
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The existence of bubbles in oil paper insulation will seriously reduce its insulation strength, and the particle size of bubbles is one of the key parameters affecting its insulation performance. In the field of electrical engineering, there is no method to detect the particle size of bubbles in transformer oil. In this paper, a method for detecting bubble size in oil is proposed based on Mie scattering theory. The spatial distribution of scattered light intensity contains the particle size information of bubbles, and then the particle size distribution law of bubbles is deduced. Firstly, an experimental platform for bubble detection was built, and then the inversion algorithm was written by using relevant theoretical calculation. Silicon carbide particles with known particle size were used as calibration samples, and the particle size distribution of cavitation bubbles due to vibration was also detected. The calibration and actual detection results show that this method can be used to detect bubbles in transformer oil.

articleTitle: The influence of dielectric constant characteristics of AC high gradient resistor on potential distribution
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In order to realize the miniaturization of gas-insulated metal-enclosed arresters (GIS arresters) for GIS power stations, GIS lightning arrester manufacturers usually use high gradient resistors. Due to the change in the formulation process of the high gradient resistor, the relative dielectric constant characteristics change. The relative dielectric constant of the resistor has a significant impact on the potential distribution of the GIS arrester. Therefore, this paper takes 220kV GIS lightning arrester as an example, through experiments and simulations, the relative dielectric constant characteristics of high gradient resistors under different chargeability and the influence on the potential distribution of GIS arresters are studied. The research results show that: the relative dielectric constant of resistors varies greatly with the change of chargeability, which has a great influence on the potential distribution. A measure to optimize the potential distribution of the arrester by using the relative dielectric constant of the resistor is proposed. The research results provide an important reference for the design and parameter selection of GIS arresters.

articleTitle: DC electric fields in HVDC stations
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The paper considers aspects related to DC electric fields and their limitation as a part of measures towards safety in HVDC converter stations. It is shown that the existing traditional approach based on DC electric field limitation on DC transmission lines crossing open public areas where human beings can be affected by long term exposure to electric fields is not applied to HVDC converter stations where only occupational personnel has limited access to and no public is permitted. Given that, it is recommended that assessment of risks (if any) associated with electromagnetic field exposure to occupational personnel involved in operational and maintenance activities shall be based on assessment of the assigned works and tasks according to recommendations of HVDC manufacturer and world-recognized best practices of safe maintenance in HVDC converter stations. Instead of introducing of exposure limits for DC electric fields making the compact design solutions complicated, the alternative ways and work methods for providing occupational safety are proposed together with the advances in the safe maintenance approaches as well as the latest achievements in digital maintenance and diagnostic technologies. Implementation of the available safe maintenance techniques makes possible to completely avoid the DC electric field exposure from consideration.

articleTitle: HVDC GIS/GIL – classification of PD defects using NoDi* pattern and machine learning
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Partial discharge measurement is one of the most important diagnosis methods for high voltage equipment. For equipment under AC voltage exists reliable interpretation tools such as the PRPD pattern. Due to the lack of phase information at DC voltage, many of the established methods for interpreting PD cannot be used. At DC voltage, the classification of PD defects can be realised with NoDi* pattern or automatically with machine learning algorithms. For this purpose, features are extracted from the measured PD data and provided to the trained algorithm. Five typical PD defects of HVDC GIS/GIL were investigated – bouncing particles, particles in firefly effect, floating electrodes, and chamber and busbar corona. New aspects of floating electrode with respect to the dynamic range of the input amplifier of the PD measurement system were investigated. For this purpose, two measurement systems in parallel with different gain settings were used. Furthermore, the possibility to distinguish between busbar and chamber corona at DC voltage was examined. The extracted features for the machine learning algorithms were analysed and both manual and automatic feature selection were performed and compared to verify the manual feature selection. The results were in good agreement. In a next step, the necessary number of PD pulses was investigated to obtain the same seperability between the PD defects, whereas a number of 500 PD pulses seems sufficient for a PDM system.

articleTitle: Line selection strategy for a beneficial DLR system based on international project experience
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: System operators have to face several technical, economic, and system-level control challenges during the operation of high voltage distribution- and transmission lines. The progressively increasing energy demand, the spread of distributed generation, aspiration for an integrated energy market (IEM) formation, intermittent generation of renewable energy sources, continuous supply constraint of the consumers or the capital-intensive and prolonged investments in case of new infrastructure constructions also belong to this challenging problem area. Dynamic line rating (DLR) is a state-of-the-art methodology for uprating power lines, as this technique monitors the thermal behaviour of the overhead lines' phase conductors. On the other hand, a complex line monitoring expert system can be established based on the infrastructural and computational background required for the implementation of a DLR system. In this way, not only the real-time ampacity of the power lines can be calculated, but a DLR-based expert system also provides an opportunity for predetermined transmission capacity calculation, tracking of conductor temperature, monitoring of sag-clearance variation of the conductors, or forecast icing events with the determination of anti-icing current. Implementing a DLR-based expert system is preceded by different preparatory processes, which are essential during the system-level approach. The first phase of any internal or international DLR project is selecting power lines, on whose line monitoring system can be applied effectively. One purpose of this article is to present a complex line selection strategy including the specialties of the investigated network such as historical load duration curves, load limiting machinery in the substations, archive icing events, or different strategic aspects that highly affect the economic return, efficiency and operational safety of such a system. Another important aspect in the preparatory process of a DLR system implementation is the so-called critical span analysis. In this step, the required number and installation place of the sensor system is determined, in order that the measurement results adequately represent the prevailing thermal conditions along the entire route of the power line. As the results of the preparatory actions, the implementation of the line monitoring system can be performed both from an infrastructural and IT solutions point of view. Another aspiration of this paper to provide case studies via the experiences earned in the framework of European Commission supported FARCROSS project. In the Work Package 5 demonstration stage of the FARCROSS project, a complex grid management technology for handling cross-border transmission line capacity-related issues have been implemented at four transmission system operators' grids. The lessons learned during the selection of transmission lines for demonstration purposes are presented in detail. Furthermore, the experiences gained during critical span analysis, field installation of measuring devices and integration of system components at the already closed phase of the demo are also discussed in this article.

articleTitle: Effect of epoxy material itself on characteristics and properties of its fluorinated surface layer
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In order to investigate a possible effect of the epoxy material itself on physicochemical characteristics and electrical properties of the fluorinated surface layer, in this report, three kinds of anhydride cured epoxy samples were prepared using different raw materials and formulations and. Their surface fluorination was performed in a laboratory stainless vessel under the same conditions. ATR-IR analysis shows a stronger C=O absorption for the sample with a higher crosslink density, and also indicates that fluorine atoms are incorporated into the surface layers. SEM cross-section images show a thicker fluorinated layer for the sample with a lower crosslink density. SEM surface images indicate that the fluorination led to the formation of many surface cracks and/or pits, and surface cracks are much deeper for the sample with a higher crosslinking density. The measurements of surface conductivity and surface potential decay reveal a significant increase in surface conductivity or the potential decay rate for these epoxy samples by the fluorination. The measurements also show a significant dependence of the increase in surface conduction on the resin raw materials and formulation, and the higher the epoxy value or crosslinking density, the more the increase in surface conduction.

articleTitle: Application of finite element method to compare the installation requirements in a buried cable according to IEC60287 standards
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In this paper, the thermal analysis of an installed underground XLPE- insulated single core power cable with flat formation, is presented. Quickfield© is the software used to simulate and evaluate the current rating in the buried cable, using specific boundary conditions. Quickfield© is a Finite Element Method CAD modeling software that supports a variety of electromagnetic, thermal and stress analysis problems that have either two-dimensional x-y symmetry or axial symmetry. IEC 60287 standards are applicable to the conditions of the steady-state operation of cables, at all alternating voltages and direct voltages up to 5 kV, buried directly into the ground without partial drying-out of the soil. The current rating calculations (IEC60287.1-1) and thermal rating calculations (IEC60287.2-1) were used for calculation purposes. A system of three single core power cables arranged in flat formation is buried in multi-layered soil. The cable line burial depth used is 1000mm, the thermal resistivity of the soil is 1.2K.m/W and the temperature of the soil used is 30˚C. These boundary conditions were used to simulate and evaluate the current rating of the cable. The purpose of this study is to compare the current rating of an underground XLPE-insulated single core power cable calculated according to IEC60287 from a manufacturer to the simulation results. The results were obtained using the finite element software Quickfield© to show the impact on the outcome on real life installation conditions. The results obtained with the software, when the assumption is made that the soil is radial and also isotherm, correlates with the calculated results obtained using the analytical method based on the analogy between an electrical circuit and a heat flow circuit. The analogy used when calculating the current rating was that the heat flow in the circuit corresponds to the current rating in a buried cable. The simulation results were analysed and compared with the manufacturer's data and calculated according to IEC60287 standards.

articleTitle: Volume effect on AC dielectric breakdown strength of ester oil compared with that of mineral oil
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: This study deals with the stressed oil volume (SOV) volume dependence of dielectric breakdown strength Eb in natural ester oil (EO) as compared with that of mineral oil (MO). The SOV was varied in the range from 0.1mm3 to 4000mm3 for both oils in various electrode systems. As a result, similar SOV dependence of Eb was found to be obtained in both oils. This suggests that when EO is used as insulating oil in transformers, the same insulation design as MO can be applicable. The ratio (Rm) of the shape parameter m-value of the EO to that of the MO at each SOV was calculated by making a Weibull distribution of breakdown voltage Vb at the electrodes used in the experiment. It was found that the SOV dependence of Rm showed an increasing trend. It was also found that the relative water content of EO was about 2.9 to 9.1 %, while that of MO was about 12.8 to 27.3 %, and comparing the relative water content of the two oils. The higher relative water content of the MO caused more free water in the MO and more weaknesses, which contributes to the larger scattering of the breakdown voltage.

articleTitle: Reproducibility of partial discharge measurements on surface discharges according to iec 60270 at dc and ac voltages
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Partial discharge measurement at AC voltage is one of the most important diagnostic tools for testing and evaluating the condition of high-voltage equipment. The requirements for the measuring system, the test setup and the test procedure as well as the evaluation methods are defined in IEC 60270. Acceptance criteria and measurement procedures are defined in the corresponding standards of the different equipment. For partial discharge measurements at DC voltage stress, the requirements have to be questioned, due to the different partial discharge behaviour of some defects and the lack of experience at DC voltage. Due to the increasing use of HVDC transmission systems in the future transmission grid, partial discharge measurement at DC voltage is becoming more and more important. For this reason, the applicability of IEC 60270 for partial discharge measurements at DC voltage was examined in different round robin tests. After the already published measurement results on epoxy insulators and measurements on a needle-plate arrangement, this paper presents investigations on surface discharge arrangements and analyses, compares and discusses the results of the different laboratories.

articleTitle: Dielectric frequency response of oil-paper insulation under uneven damp
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: On account of good electrical and mechanical properties, oil-paper bushing is widely used in power systems. Due to the influence of temperature gradient and gravity, the distribution of moisture in the bushing is uneven. In order to use frequency domain spectroscopy (FDS) to evaluate the moisture content of the bushing more accurately, the FDS curves of oil-paper insulation under the condition of uneven damp were studied. According to the dielectric response test principle, the relationship between the complex conductivity and the complex permittivity was deduced, which is the basis of constructing a numerical model under the condition of uneven damp. At the same time, a variety of uneven damp physical models were constructed to study the influence of moisture content, temperature and uneven distribution on the dielectric response characteristics of the oil-paper insulation model. The results show that when the oil-paper insulation is not affected by moisture uniformly, the dielectric loss curves show obvious loss peaks and curve fluctuation. When the oil-paper insulation combination is more uneven, the curve fluctuation is greater, and the corresponding frequency of the loss peak increases. The FDS curves obtained from the experiment and numerical model are in good agreement, which verifies the correctness of the model.

articleTitle: Novel approach for insulation condition assessment of high voltage substation equipment at 1 Hz
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In the field, it is common practice to evaluate the average condition of high voltage substation equipment by measurement of dielectric losses. This practice involves applying an AC signal to an insulation system (capacitor) at a frequency close to the line-frequency (60 or 50 Hz) and measure the current and the angle between current and applied voltage to determine the insulation dissipation factor or power factor (also known by the term of tan delta). Line-frequency insulation dissipation factor (DF) or power factor (PF) depends on the frequency of the applied signal, dielectric properties of the insulation material, insulation temperature, geometrical design, as well as aging and contamination that might be present within the insulating medium. The field experience suggests that the use of table correction factors for temperature correction does not reflect the true thermal behavior of the insulation system and any trending analysis turns out sometimes misleading due to incorrect temperature correction. Throughout the service life of an electrical asset, line-frequency DF may not change, may increase or sometimes it may even decrease, but the reason for these changes is not always clear. The research work carried out by the authors shows that even a “good” line-frequency DF is not always “good” and that assessment of insulation should consider one more DF value obtained at a different frequency to properly and reliably determine the condition of the insulation system. This document provides a clear understanding of the benefit of testing for insulation DF at line-frequency (50 or 60 Hz) and 1 Hz. A simple procedure carried out at the same time and with the same test set provides a more reliable and more efficient way to evaluate the condition of critical high voltage substation equipment including power transformers, bushings, and instrument transformers.

articleTitle: Research on mechanical properties of cable terminals for high speed trains at extreme temperature
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The rapid development of high-speed railway makes the number of cables and terminals running in extreme temperature environments gradually increase. Under extreme temperature conditions, the mechanical reliability of the interface of cable terminal will be severely challenged. In this paper, the mechanical properties of rubber insulation materials, used for highspeed train cable and terminal, were researched in a wide temperature range. A typical cable terminal model was established to simulate the interface pressure reliability of insulation materials under extreme temperature conditions. The results show that the elastic modulus of the selected silicone rubber and ethylene-propylene rubber materials increase significantly at low temperature. And simulation results show that the SiR/EPR interface pressure can meet the requirement of cable terminals under extreme temperature conditions. This paper is expected to be used in the structural optimization of cables and terminals for high-speed trains and can help to realize the localization of high-speed train cable terminals.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic-thermal coupled analysis of a 10 kV silicone rubber cast dry-type transformer
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Epoxy resin is often used as insulating material to cast dry-type transformers, but its heat dissipation and overload capacity is relatively weak. Silicone rubber material has better thermal conductivity, insulation and mechanical properties, and has been widely used in composite insulators, lightning arrester and other external insulation equipment. In this paper, silicone rubber is used as insulating material to cast the dry-type transformer, and the improvement of heat dissipation performance of the transformer is analysed. Taking a 10 kV epoxy resin dry-type transformer as an example, the three-dimensional model of the transformer was established, and the finite volume method was used to analyse the thermal field. By comparing the simulation results with the actual temperature rise data of the transformer, the error is less than 2.8 °C, which verify the accuracy of the calculation method. The casting area of epoxy resin in the transformer is replaced by a new type of silicone rubber material to calculate the temperature field. The results show that the hot spot temperature rise of the transformer with silicone rubber as insulating material decreases by about 3 °C at the rated load, which improves the heat dissipation capacity of the transformer.

articleTitle: Simulation on weibull-distribution of PP nanocomposites modulated by carrier transport and molecular displacement
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Polypropylene is widely used in thin-film capacitors for its excellent electrical and chemical properties, while electric breakdown is the key factor restricting the improvement of energy storage density of capacitors. Nanodoping is an effective way to improve the matrix breakdown performance, but the effects of aggregate structure, charge transport and molecular displacement of polymers on the distribution shape parameter of breakdown fields of nanocomposites are still unclear. In this paper, the parameters of charge transport and molecular displacement affected by the aggregate structure of polymers are extracted, and the carrier transport and molecular displacement modulated electrical breakdown (CTMD) model considering the random variables are established to simulate the breakdown strength of PP/Al2O3 nanocomposites. The DC breakdown strengths obey the Weibull-distribution when the random variables follow the Gaussian distribution. It is found that with the increase in variance of random variables, the characteristic breakdown strength is in good agreement with experimental results, while the distribution shape parameter decreases. Specifically, the distribution shape parameter decreases fastest with the rise of the standard deviation of the energy of deep traps and much slower with increasing the standard deviation of the attempt-to-escape frequency, carrier mobility and trapping coefficient. The results show that the simulated Weibulldistribution can be consistent with the experimental results by adjusting the variance of random variables, and the effect of each parameter on the distribution shape parameter is diverse.

articleTitle: Study on fitting and prediction of metallized film capacitor's voltage drop
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Metallized film capacitors (MFC) are important devices in many industries, while its voltage drop obstacles the exertion of its energy storage characteristics. Therefore, it has become an important research topic to clarify the voltage drop law of MFC and predict the voltage drop of MFC. At first, this paper gives the voltage drop test circuit of MFC. Then, the classical voltage drop model, power function, 9-order polynomial and smoothing spline are used to fit the voltage drop data, and the voltage drop values are predicted based on the fitting results. At final, fitting and prediction performance of these methods are compared, and the research direction of how to improve the prediction accuracy is pointed out.

articleTitle: Simulation of the electric field of human body surface when the ±1100 kV line is installed in parallel with the 1000 kV AC line
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In this paper, the finite element simulation models of tower, line, insulator and human body of UHV AC / DC parallel line are established, the distribution characteristics of human surface electric field of ±1100 kV DC line live working when erected in parallel with 1000 kV AC are obtained, and the distribution of human surface electric field at five typical working locations commonly used for live maintenance are calculated. The influence of the parallel distance between the two lines in the range of 28-70 m on the electric field level is studied. We also calculated and compared the average body surface maximum electric field of two equipotential entry paths for live maintenance of DC lines when the nearest parallel distance between the two lines is 28 m, which provides a reference basis for electromagnetic shielding protection measures for live operation of ±1100 kV DC lines.

articleTitle: Propagation properties of PD-Emitted electromagnetic wave in three phase encapsulated type GIS with series arrangement and relation between defect position and sensor output
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: As partial discharge (PD) diagnostic for GIS, the UHF method to detect PD-emitted electromagnetic (EM) wave in the UHF band has been applied due to several advantages like sensitivity and safety as a non-contact method. So far, there were researches on the UHF method, it has not been clear for propagation properties of PD-emitted EM wave in the GIS, especially for the three-phase encapsulated type GIS due to the difficulty to evaluate influence of high voltage conductor arrangement like triangle or straight arrangement. In this paper, focusing on the straight type arrangement of the three-phase encapsulated type GIS, the authors investigated propagation properties of EM wave experimentally with a model tank and simulated PD signal and numerically with FD-TD analysis, and then compared both results. As a result, good agreement on the amplitude of detected signal between them was found, so further discussion was performed using the FD-TD analysis with changing the defect position. The simulation results showed that amplitude of the sensor output depends on the defect position, which means that one can identify the defect position based on the relation of the sensor output among the sensors.

articleTitle: Simulation analysis of electric field changes during low temperature start-up of converter transformer
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In this paper, based on the non-linear influence law of temperature and field strength on the dielectric parameters of transformer oil and oil-impregnated pressboard, a simplified model of the winding end on the valve side of the converter transformer is established, and the finite element method is used to study the electric field distribution on the valve side of the converter transformer during low temperature start-up process at -40°C. The research results show that: under AC voltage, the highest field strength on the valve side is located near the oil gap of the high voltage end winding except 80°C, and is transferred to the outside of the capacitor ring at 80°C. The highest field strength value increases slightly with temperature rise. Under DC and AC-DC superimposed voltage, the highest field strength position on the valve side is located at the overlap between the corner ring and the pressboard near the high voltage end except 80°C, and is transferred to the inside of the capacitor ring at 80°C. With the increase of temperature, the highest field strength firstly increases and then decreases, reaching the peak value at -20°C and the lowest value at 80°C. And the higher the DC component, the greater the variation of the highest field strength with the temperature rise. At the same time, the lower the temperature, the deeper the influence of the DC component on the highest field strength.

articleTitle: Study on the self-sensing partial discharge detection method for power transformers adopting its component as ultra-high frequency sensor
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Power transformer is one of the most important equipment in power system. Its reliability directly affects the safe operation of power network. A partial discharge (PD) detection method for transformers adopting the end shield of the bushing as ultra-high frequency (UHF) sensor is developed in this paper. The transformer can be used as the internal UHF sensor to measure the PD UHF signals. The experiments are carried out on a 220kV transformer with suspension discharge defect models set inside. The validity and sensitivity of this method are proved by experiments with AC voltage. The results show that the proposed method has high detection sensitivity and it can measure the PD signals without additional sensor. The UHF method has good anti-interference performance and is not affected by corona discharge outside the transformer. This PD detection method solves the problem that the internal UHF sensor inconvenient while the external sensor is susceptible to interference. It provides a new method for PD detection of transformers in field.

articleTitle: Arc interruption performance of C4F7NCO2 and dielectric recovery in disconnecting switch
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas is widely used in high voltage power switchgear. However, SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> is a gas with strong greenhouse effect. Therefore, the study of new environment-friendly gases represented by perfluoronitrile (C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N) gas as a substitute gas for SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> has become a hot issue in the field of high-voltage electrical appliances. In this paper, the magneto-hydro-dynamic (MHD) model of arc burning process was established for the structure of 126kV isolation switch. The results about the post arc breakdown voltage and electrical field distribution was calculated for the evaluation of the performance of arc interruption. The established model in this thesis is valid and can be widely used in arc simulation and the evaluation of dielectric recovery. The results of this paper are significant for the application of new environmental gases in isolating switchgear and optimization design.

articleTitle: DC flashover performance of surface fluorinated alumina/epoxy resin composite with real spacer formulation
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The surface of spacers in GIS or GIL used for fixing and supporting high voltage conductors is known to be the most vulnerable area since flashovers easily occur along the surface. In this report, the alumina-filled epoxy composite samples prepared using the same formulation and technology as those for real spacers were surface fluorinated in a laboratory stainless vessel using a F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>/N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> mixture with 12.5% F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> by volume at 0.1 MPa and 55 °C for 30 min. The dc flashover performance of the surface fluorinated epoxy composite sample was evaluated using the finger electrode/sheet sample configuration in 0.1 MPa SF6 gas. The flashover tests indicate that the fluorination led to an increase in the dc flashover voltage at 63.2% probability by 8.46%. The results also show that the fluorination simultaneously reduced the dispersion of the flashover performance. The increase in dc flashover voltage is mainly attributed to an increase in surface conduction or the suppression of surface charge accumulation by the fluorination, as indicated by measurements of surface potential decay and surface conductivity. The increase in surface conduction is due to changes in composition and structure of the surface layer, as shown by ATR-IR analysis and SEM observation.

articleTitle: Comparative study of partial discharge detection with multi-band helical antenna and silicon photomultiplier
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The stable operation of gas-insulated switchgear (GIS) directly affects the reliability of the power grid. Partial discharge may occur when GIS has internal defects, resulting in insulation deterioration and even surface flashover. The partial discharge induces electromagnetic signals and optical signals. A kind of three-band helical antenna is designed to detect the electromagnetic signals in ultra-high frequency (UHF) band caused by corona discharge and surface discharge in this paper. The center frequencies of the helical antenna are 715MHz, 970MHz, and 1.5GHz, respectively, distributing in the main frequency spectra of partial discharge caused by the typical defects. Furthermore, silicon photomultiplier (SiPM) is taken to detect optical signals, and the optical signals are used to compare with the UHF signals.
