publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The study of absorption spectrum characteristics of transformer oil is helpful to evaluate the state of transformer oil and to lay a foundation for the selection of optical parameters in related optical experiments. Based on the absorption spectrum test platform, this paper systematically studied the influence law of transformer oil state, namely gas content, mositure content and aging degree on its absorption spectrum. It was found that the gas content mainly affects the occurrence of the saturation absorption peak, when the water content is 10ppm and the gas content is greater than 1%, the saturation absorption peak appears, but does not appear when the gas content is less than 1%; Moisture content mainly affects absorbance through the presence of water in oil, the absorbance of suspended water is the largest while that of dissolved water is the smallest. The larger the moisture content is, the more the number of saturated absorption peaks will increase; Aging degree mainly affects the number of saturated absorption peaks. The more serious the aging degree, the more the number of saturated absorption peaks and the wider the band range of saturated absorption peaks.

articleTitle: Evaluation method of cable dielectric loss under oscillating wave voltage
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Dielectric loss test can be used as a diagnostic test method for cable insulation condition evaluation. Because the power cable is generally long and its equivalent capacitance is large, it is inconvenient to measure its tan δ at high voltage. Using damped oscillation wave instead of power frequency sine wave as test voltage excitation source makes it possible to test power cable dielectric loss on site. The evaluation method of cable dielectric loss under oscillating voltage is discussed, and the reference data of different dielectric cables are given.

articleTitle: Simulation of electric field and space charge of typical particle defects of HVDC cable
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The increasing demand for the HVDC power cable has greatly emphasized the space charge and electric field distribution within the polymeric cable insulation. One of the critical aspects of cable is the space charge, and it is a unique challenge in the production of HVDC cable insulation. The electric field distribution inside the cable insulation has become a significant challenge, especially in solid insulation material. The main purpose of this paper is to determine the space charge and the electric field distribution between the XLPE and EPDM insulation materials, with the existence of void and without void, which has been located at the centre between the two insulation. The Finite Element Method (FEM) technique is utilized based on COMSOL Simulation software to observe the electric field distribution and the space charge density. To analyze the behavior between the two insulation of cable, a two-dimensional (2D) model was built. First, an equivalent model of 11kV cable with XLPE and EPDM insulation material along with high voltage electrode and ground electrode were built. Second, to examine the electric field and the space charge, a typical void defect was added between the two insulation. Third, the simulation was carried out to determine the electrical potential, electric field behaviour, and the space charge density with and without the existence of the void defect. The simulation result describes that the electric field at the air void defect of the cable insulation layer is relatively strong. As the voltage increases, a higher electric field was generated. The electric field at the edges of high voltage and ground electrode is relatively high. When a high voltage was applied, a positive charge was developed between the two insulation layers. The lower surface of the EPDM insulation layer generates a negative charge.

articleTitle: Micromagnetic investigation on vortex motion of nanocrystalline alloy under kHz level magnetization
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The dominant mechanism of magnetization in magnetic materials is the deflection of magnetic moment and the displacement of magnetic domain wall. There are relatively few researches on the magnetization mechanism of nanocrystalline soft magnetic alloy at mesoscopic level. In this paper, the influence mechanism of the high frequency magnetization process of nanocrystalline soft magnetic alloy under different external factors was investigated according the mechanism of displacement of magnetic domain walls by Micromagnetic Simulation. The results show that in the process of repeated magnetization, the two vortices are symmetrically distributed with the central axis as the dividing line, which can be regarded as moving from one side of the material to the other. At the same time, the increase of amplitude and frequency of the alternating magnetic field can accelerate the process of magnetization, while the acceleration degrees of the two vortices are different with the effect of increasing amplitude more significant.

articleTitle: Electric field prediction and optimization of 12 kV switchgear contact box
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The concentrated electric field of the contact box will lead to the aging of the insulator, which is easy to cause accidents such as breakdown. Therefore, this paper considers KYN-28A switchgear as the object of study and comes up with a three-dimensional electric field prediction and optimization method based on SVM-PSO hybrid algorithm for contact box of switchgear. Firstly, this paper establishes the three-dimensional model of switchgear by SolidWorks and the model is imported into COMSOL for electric field calculation. Then, the maximum of electric field strength of switchgear contact box can be obtained through the simulation. Next, a set of simulation data is obtained by enumeration of phase spacing, cross section area and corner radius of bus bar. This group of data is applied to SVM, and then the electric field prediction model of switchgear contact box under different bus phase spacing, cross-sectional area and chamfer radius is established. Last, the optimization results of the minimum field strength of the contact box are obtained by using the PSO optimization algorithm. The research results of this paper provide a theoretical basis for the design and optimization of switchgear.

articleTitle: On-line monitoring and characteristic analysis of converter transformer vibration
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The vibration signal of the converter transformer contains abundant internal mechanical conditions, but the current vibration detection methods in a short time cannot comprehensively and concretely study the variation law of vibration characteristics of the converter transformer during the entire operation period. Based on the above reasons, we have developed an on-line vibration monitoring system to implement 24-hour on-line vibration monitoring on the converter transformer; then, we extracted vibration characteristic parameters from a large number of vibration signals collected, and analyzed the variation law of vibration characteristic parameters of different measuring points under different operation modes. As a result, the vibration of the converter transformer varies greatly with the operating condition, and the vibration monitoring analysis should try to select the measuring points which are less affected by the operating condition. The research results provide an effective basis and data support for a comprehensive understanding of the vibration characteristics and maintenance and repair of the converter transformer during operation.

articleTitle: Optimisation of built-in UHF conical monopole antenna sensors for partial discharge detection in high voltage switchgear
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In this paper, a built-in antenna sensor for wide-band based on a classic conical monopole antenna is proposed to detect partial discharge(PD) in 600MHz-1.2GHz. The antenna is modeled by CST Microwave Studio to yield good performance in the frequency range of interest. The large ground plate of the classic conical monopole antenna is replaced by a concentric cylindrical block, which reduces the area of the cross-section of the ground plate and realizes the miniaturization of antenna. By appropriately choosing the gap distance between the cone and cylindrical block, cone length and the diameter of the concentric cylindrical block, the performance of wide bandwidth, omnidirectional radiation patterns and good gain are acquired. A vector network analyzer(VNA) is used to test the return loss of the conical antenna, and the test results are consistent with the simulation results (standing wave ratio of less than 2.5). Finally, an experimental platform is set up in the laboratory and typical partial discharge defects are set. The proposed UHF monopole antenna is fabricated and tested. Detection impedance, transient earth voltages(TEV) and UHF are used for PD detection simultaneously with the aim to validate the effectiveness of the antenna and the experimental results demonstrate that the proposed UHF antenna appeared to be suitable for PD detection.

articleTitle: Analysis and study on withstand voltage characteristic of the arrester of DC transfer switch
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The DC transfer switch is the key equipment when system operation mode changed. After the DC transfer switch is turned off, the residual energy on the auxiliary circuit and the system must be absorbed through the arrester. The arrester would be destroyed by huge amounts of energy in process of the state of DC transfer switch changed. In recent years, during the commissioning and operation of DC transmission project, there have been many cases of failures in the operation mode conversion due to the damaged arrester. According to the actual configuration of the DC transfer switch, generation mechanism and withstand characteristic of voltage was analyzed by circuit theory and simulation calculation. A test device for withstanding characteristic of the arrester had been built, and the test for withstand voltage versus time characteristic was carried out. Test results can be used as a reference for the design and selection of the arrester of DC transfer switch for other engineering.

articleTitle: Investigation of electrical and thermal behavior of modified epoxy structures for DC and high frequency applications
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Epoxy resin insulations are considered as a potential candidate for various applications like transformers, cable terminations, power electronic device packaging, and bushings. This has promoted a great interest in their use as high voltage insulation materials for high frequency applications. This work presents the effect of different curing agent concentrations on the electrical and thermal properties of epoxy resin for DC and high frequency applications. Differential scanning calorimetry is used to characterize the thermal performance of the materials. The insulation properties such as breakdown measurements under DC and high frequency stress, DC resistivity, and space charge distributions at different temperatures, and dielectric spectroscopy at different frequencies and temperatures are performed. Results reveal that high curing agent concentrations optimize the thermal and electrical performance of epoxy resin insulation. However, high frequency stress severely degrades the breakdown and dielectric properties of all the prepared materials. By the control of resin stoichiometry, epoxy resin with suitable electrical and thermal properties can be realized for high frequency applications.

articleTitle: Effect of hydrolyzable chlorine content on dielectric properties of epoxy/Al2O3 composite hygrothermal aging
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The electrical insulation performance of epoxy composites decreases seriously after hygrothermal aging, which threatens the safe operation of electrical equipment. In order to explore the effect of hydrolyzable chlorine content on dielectric properties of epoxy/Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> composite hygrothermal aging, the breakdown strength, volume resistivity, relative permittivity and dielectric loss factor of four kinds of epoxy/Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> composites with different hydrolyzable chlorine content were tested after the hygrothermal aging. The changes of these dielectric properties before and after hygrothermal aging were analyzed and explained from the perspective of hydrolyzable chlorine. The results show that after hygrothermal aging, the breakdown strength of epoxy/Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> composite increases at first and then decreases with increase of hydrolyzable chlorine content, the volume resistivity of epoxy/Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> composite decreases continuously with the increase of hydrolyzable chlorine content, the relative permittivity and dielectric loss factor of epoxy/Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> composite both increase with the increase of hydrolyzable chlorine content. These changes in dielectric properties are related to the electron-absorbing properties of hydrolyzable chlorine atom and hydroxyl group formed after hydrolysis.

articleTitle: Simulation and design of new DCCB test circuit
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: It is necessary to ensure the equivalence of the recovery voltage and its rising rate during the breaking test of mechanical HVDC circuit breaker. In this paper, a test circuit topology is proposed, which is composed of current source, commutation source and recovery voltage source. Both current source and commutation source are oscillation circuits composed of L and C, which use low-voltage capacitor to provide fault current and current zero-crossing point for DCCB. Recovery voltage source uses high-voltage capacitor, which mainly provides recovery voltage for DCCB. The design of the test circuit realizes the isolation of the recovery voltage source from the current source and the commutation source, ensuring that the recovery voltage can rise rapidly after the successful breaking of DCCB. The advantage of this topology is that the test circuit ensures the equivalence of di/dt and du/dt in the breaking test, and the consumption of capacitance is smaller and the cost is low. Finally, the effectiveness of the test circuit is verified by simulation software, the simulation results show that the test circuit can not only fully simulate the recovery voltage and its rising rate, but also ensure the equivalence of current process.

articleTitle: A cable hybrid type defect localization method based on frequency domain reflectometry
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Early detection and elimination of cable defects is very important to improve the reliability of cable operation. Traditional time-domain reflection (TDR) localization method unable to locate latent defects due to the rising edge of the pulse signal. In recent years, some scholars have started local defect localization research based on frequency domain reflectometry (FDR). This paper proposes a method for diagnosing hybrid type cable defects based on frequency domain reflectometry. Simulation and field test were carried out to analyse the aging and abrasion defects on the same cable to illustrate the reliability of the positioning algorithm when mixed types of defects occur. The simulation and experimental results correspond well, which illustrates that when hybrid type of defects occur in the same cable, FDR can locate the defects and the location accuracy of simulation is within 0.5%, and the experimental test is within 0.3%.

articleTitle: Stability study of wind and de-icing resistant anti-icing coatings
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: With the development of the power system, the problem of ice cover on transmission lines is a serious threat to the stable transmission of electricity, making it impossible to guarantee national economic security. Insulator over-icing reduces insulator flashover voltage, line over-icing increases transmission line and tower loading, and de-icing can also trigger line dancing leading to serious problems such as line breakage and tower collapse. This paper introduces the principle of superhydrophobic coating anti-icing, and prepares a nano-superhydrophobic coating and micro-nano co-doped two superhydrophobic coating. The wind tunnel test and repeated de-icing test are designed for both coatings. The results show that the micro-nano co-doped superhydrophobic coating is better than the pure nano-doped superhydrophobic coating in terms of hydrophobic performance due to its dual-scale roughness, and still has superhydrophobic performance after wind tunnel tests and repeated de-icing tests. The stability is much better than that of the pure nano-doped superhydrophobic coating, which provides a new idea for the application of anti-icing coatings in the field of power systems.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation on charge transport and analysis of its relationship with DC electric breakdown
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Electric field distortion caused by charge transport is an important factor resulting in breakdown. Based on bipolar charge transport model, the dynamic process of space charge distribution and electric field distortion varied with voltage is simulated. The results show that the electric field distortion caused by charge accumulation in the shallow region of material is a key factor that affects the breakdown process. Due to the homo space charges accumulation, the reverse electric field formed at sample edge, which makes the electric field weakened in the region, while the electric field inside the sample is strengthened, thus inducing the maximum E. The PEA result verifies the relationship between charge distribution and electric field distortion. Besides, seen from the view of impact ionization and free volume breakdown theory, the charge energy affected by distorted electric field and free volume should be jointly considered to interpret the breakdown process.

articleTitle: Dielectric strength and conductivity improvements of voltage-stabilizer modified EPDM materials used for cable accessory insulation
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In order to achieve high quality electrical materials for cable terminals, the crosslinked ethylene-propylene-diene monomer (EPDM) materials with significant improvements in both conductivity and electric strength are developed by employing a specific voltage stabilizer and thermal-chemistry grafting/crosslinking technique. The characteristic aromatic compounds with polar-group coupled benzene are selected as voltage stabilizers to introduce charge traps in deep levels and nomadic electronic-states at band-edge, which account for promoting dielectric breakdown strength and electric conductivity respectively. Infrared spectroscopy characterizations indicate that the voltage-stabilizer molecules can be simultaneously grafted onto EPDM molecular-chains in the crosslinking process. In despite of showing an almost identical improvement in dielectric breakdown strength (DBS), two voltage stabilizers of 4-acryloxy-2-hydroxybenzophenone (ALRB) and 4-vinyloxy acetophenone (VPE) distinguish evidently in electric conductivity and emigration resistance. In contrast to VPE, the modified EPDM materials by grafting ALRB represent an explicitly higher conductivity than benchmark EPDM, while acquiring the preferred emigration resistant characteristics. Thermal stimulation currents (TSC) tests and the first-principles calculations consistently demonstrate that both the two grafted voltage stabilizers can introduce deep charge traps for electron carriers, which accounts for the almost identical DBS improvements. Meanwhile, the first-principles calculations also elucidate the nomadic nature of the ALRB-introduced electronic-states merging into the conduction band minimum of EPDM molecules, which is however absent for VPE and accounting for the conductivity discrepancy. Further for the present modifications of grafting voltage-stabilizers, the appreciable DBS improvements in well agreement with TSC analyses on trap level distributions confirm the theoretical estimation that deep traps can increase electric strength through the trapping mechanism of suppressing charge injections. On the advantage of appropriately increased conductivity in coordination with the well persisted DBS, the finite element simulations of electric field distributions in EPDM cable terminals provide a concrete manifestation of the significant field homogenization at the root of stress cone for ALRB/EPDM reinforce insulation. The present study suggests a prospective strategy to ameliorate EPDM materials used for cable accessories.

articleTitle: Study on the structure and mechanical and electrical properties of β-crystal blended polypropylene
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Copolymer polypropylene has good insulating properties and mechanical properties and has the potential to become a thermoplastic DC cable insulation material. However, its low breakdown strength limits its application in high-voltage DC cables. In this paper, ethylene propylene block copolymer polypropylene (EPC) was selected as the matrix, and isotactic polypropylene (iPP) and a β nucleating agent were added for blending modification. The crystal structure was characterized by wide-angle X-ray diffraction (WAXD), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and metallographic microscopy (POM). The results showed that flower-like β crystals were formed in the β-crystal blended polypropylene. The mechanical properties, included space charge, and DC breakdown properties of the composite were tested. Compared with that of pure iPP, the mechanical tensile strength of the β-crystal blended polypropylene material was greatly improved, the elongation at break reached 666.4%, the normal temperature impact performance reached 39.1 kJ/m2 at the same time, and the low-temperature embrittlement temperature point also greatly decreased to −39.8 °C, meaning that the material can completely meet the requirements of working at low temperatures. After applying a field strength of 50 kV/mm for 30 min, there was almost no space charge accumulation in the β-crystal blended polypropylene; the DC breakdown strength at 25 °C reached 267.6 kV/mm.

articleTitle: Thermally conductive polymer composites for high voltage insulation
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Electrical insulation isolates electric conductors from the earth, which is a necessary component to ensure the safe operation of electrical equipment and electrical lines. At present, the development of electrical power equipment towards high integration and high power density has raised more rigorous requirements for electrical insulation materials. Electrical insulating materials should not only have high dielectric breakdown strength but also have high thermal conductivity to rapidly dissipate the heat generated during the operation of the equipment. This review summarizes the application and research progress of thermally conductive insulating materials in a variety of power equipment. The design, fabrication and practical application of thermally conductive insulating materials were mainly focused. Finally, the future development of thermally conductive insulating materials is envisioned.

articleTitle: Review of transmission line protection in AC/DC hybrid system
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: To achieve the optimal allocation of energy and load, and consume as much clean energy as possible, China has built the world's largest high-voltage AC/DC hybrid system with the highest voltage level. And ensuring its safe operation has become a major and urgent national demand. The probability of transmission line failure accounts for a relatively high proportion of the hybrid system, especially the AC line fault on the inverter side can easily cause commutation failure of the LCC inverter station, which makes the hybrid system with more complicated fault characteristics, and it directly impacts the protection configuration of AC and DC transmission lines. Therefore, studying the high-reliability and ultra-high-speed protection methods for transmission lines, based on the characteristics of hybrid system, will have important theoretical and practical significance for reducing the hidden dangers of the hybrid system. This paper reviews the previous researches on the interaction effects of hybrid systems, protection of AC/DC transmission lines in hybrid systems.

articleTitle: Evaluation model of transformer state based on improved fuzzy comprehensive diagnosis theory
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The state evaluation of transformer includes analysing many kinds of operating signals, but the relationship between those signals and transformer states is fuzzy. To clearly describe the relationship, a multi-level comprehensive fuzzy mathematics algorithm is used. The algorithm is based on the intelligent fuzzy diagnosis theory. Taking the power transformer as the research object, the factor set and comment set are selected through appropriate methods, and the membership function relationship between them is established. The selected factors come from the electrical test, the amount of gas in the oil, and the insulating oil. And the comment set is the division of the transformer status, which is uniformly divided into four evaluations. Considering the multi-level nature of factors, fuzzy inferences are carried out to determinate the membership function, and a weight set of the factor set is established through an improved analytic hierarchy process (IAHP). In addition, a two-level fuzzy evaluation example for evaluating the state of a transformer in operation is given, which verifies the effectiveness and feasibility of the evaluation model.

articleTitle: Research on overvoltage and electromagnetic disturbance characteristic of AIS isolating switch
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: As the voltage level of the substation increases and the large amount of electronic equipment is put into use, serious electromagnetic interference has been generated. Especially when the disconnector in AIS is suitable for small capacitive current operations, it does not have the arc extinguishing ability, which leads to the occurrence of medium between the contacts. Break down several times and form a transient overvoltage. This paper builds a 110kV overvoltage electromagnetic disturbance source system simulation model based on logic judgment in the ATP-EMTP software, and compares and analyzes the overvoltage simulation signals under different capacitive loads. The finite integration method, which is suitable for solving the theory of electric large-scale space electromagnetic field electric dipole antenna, is combined with CST MWS software to analyze and calculate the radiation interference of overvoltage, and the magnetic field intensity at a position 1m from the disturbance source in the simulation model is 90-480A/m, the test shows that the magnetic field intensity at a distance of 1m from the disturbance source in the test substation is 100-455A/m, which verifies the correctness of the simulation model and has guiding significance for the installation and construction of substation equipment.

articleTitle: Effect of transformer oil and membrance of extrinsic F-P optical fiber sensor for PD induced acoustic emission detection and signal scaling
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Extrinsic F-P optical fiber sensors were widely studied for detection of PD induced acoustic emission in transformers in last decades. But attachment of transformer oil to the membrane of the sensor causes the increment of effective mass of the membrane, consequently affects the static pressure sensitivity and first order resonance frequency of the sensor. The interactive effect of transformer oil and membrane of F-P sensor for PD induced acoustic emission detection is investigated. By the deduction of ordinary solution of differential equation of the membrane which interacted with oil, the first order resonance frequency red shift of the membrane and the effect relations of oil density and viscosity are discussed. Computing simulation and experiments shown that when the temperature changed from 20°C to 80°C for a sensor with the resonance frequency about 58 kHz, the signal response resonance frequency only shifted 5.17% in blue, while as the amplitude response increased 62.26%. It was clear that it was the amplitude increment of the membrane response instead of resonance frequency had apparent affect to the PD sensing. Finally, the temperature caused interferometer pattern shift of F-P sensor was studied, and the temperature influenced sensor detection signal was scaled correctly.

articleTitle: Research and protection of stray current in grounding system of HV XLPE cable along subway
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In the DC traction power supply system, because the running rail is used as a return path, it cannot be completely insulated from the ground, causing part of the current to leak and form a stray current. Affected by stray currents, stray currents also appear in the metal sheaths of high-voltage cables laid along the subway, which cause corrosion to the metal sheaths, resulting in an increase in the contact resistance between the insulating shielding layer and the metal sheaths. When there is an air gap between the metal protective layer and the insulating shielding layer, the internal field strength of the air gap exceeds the breakdown field strength under the impact of over voltage, resulting in discharge ablation, and even in severe cases, insulation breakdown and power failure accident. By modeling the composition and operation mode of the DC traction power supply system, simulating the distribution of stray currents, analyzing the causes of insulation breakdown, and on this basis, proposes a stray current protection plan for high-voltage cables near the subway.

articleTitle: Partial discharge diagnosis for GIS equipment with deep decision network
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Partial discharge is a serious fault type in the GIS equipment operation. Due to the scarcity of fault samples, it is challenging to apply traditional deep learning techniques to diagnosis the partial discharge for the GIS equipment. To overcome this issue, this paper introduces a deep decision network (DDN) method to diagnose partial discharge diagnosis for the GIS equipment. The proposed DDN method consists of three main steps. First, the ultra-high-frequency (UHF) method obtains two spectrum characteristics, the phase resolved partial discharge (PRPD) and the phase resolved pulse sequence (PRPS), from the test sample. Based on the few-shot learning strategy, we construct a support set, which contains some labeled samples, including four types PD samples and a normal sample. Then, the two siamese networks are employed to estimate the similarity scores between a test sample and support set samples. One network is employed to measure the similarity scores in the PRPS spectrum characteristic, and the other is the PRPD spectrum characteristic. Last, a simple and effective decision fusion method is designed to fuse two spectrum characteristics-based diagnosis results. By jointly utilizing complementary information in different spectrum characteristics, the final diagnosis result can be generated. With limited training samples, experimental results demonstrate that the proposed DDN method can better diagnose performance than the current outstanding methods, including convolution neural network (CNN) and support vector machine (SVM).

articleTitle: Switching test of 35kv bridging regulation vacuum on-load tap changer
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The 35kV bridging regulation on-load tap-changer (OLTC) is an important device to dynamically adjust voltage to ensure the power quality of the distribution network. The developed vacuum on-load tap-changer is a replacement to the oil arcextinguishing one with longer lifespan. Its switching process is critical to the quality of the tap-changer and the safety of the power grid. The article introduces the circuit that tests the switching process with load based on the resonance method and carries out the switching test with peak current of 200 A for the OLTC. It is found that 1.3pu overvoltage can be excited at the load side during switching. The floating potential part of the OLTC which may cause insulation failure during switching process is pointed out as the weak spot of the apparatus. The most dangerous moment for the insulation is analysed and the insulation withstand voltage during the switching process is evaluated by measurement. No significant transition overvoltage is observed due to the floating potential. The presented work validates the OTLC prototype and can be used as guide for future OLTC design and test.

articleTitle: Improvement of energy storage density of P(VDF-TrFE-CFE) composites by filling with two dimensional BNNS nanosheets
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: As one of the most potential alternative materials for thin film capacitors, ferroelectric polymer has high dielectric constant, but its energy loss is larger when the applied field is high. In order to reduce the loss of ferroelectric polymer and improve the charge-discharge efficiency, ultrasonic assisted liquid phase stripping method was used to peel boron nitride and introduce it into P(VDF-TrFE-CFE) matrix. BNNS/P(VDF-TrFE-CFE) composite dielectric films doped with different volume fraction of BNNS were prepared by a simple solution scraping coating method. After a series of tests and characterization, 10.8 J/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> energy storage density and 55.6% charge-discharge efficiency were obtained in 1 vol.% BNNS/P(VDF-TrFE-CFE) composite dielectric. The results show that the stripped BNNS can effectively improve the breakdown strength and charge-discharge efficiency of ferroelectric polymer composite dielectric, which provides an effective way to solve the problem of low energy storage density of ferroelectric polymer.

articleTitle: Optimal analysis of electric field characteristics for live working on straight-line tower of ±1100kV DC transmission line
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In order to ensure the safety and reliability of ±1100kV DC transmission line live opera tion and to optimize the body surface electric field of equipotential operators entering and leaving the equipotential, this paper studies the potential transfer p rocess of ±1100kV DC transmission line. Combining with the engineering practice, an isometric model of DC transmission linear tower is established. The body surface field strength, suspension potential and local capacitance of the equipotential operat or entering the pole conductor from different directions are calculated by using electromagnetic s imulation software. The transient response calculation model of potential transfer was established, and the change law of transfer current and arc energy under different angles was analyzed. The simulation analysis results show that the human body surface electric field is the smallest when entering from 45° above the diagonal of the polar conductor, and the maximum field strength is located at the head, which is 279 kV/m. The transfer current decays exponentially with time, and the decay time is about 1 μs, and the maximum transient current is 596 A. The transfer energy is maximum at 45° angle in and out of the polar conductor.

articleTitle: Surface discharge aging characteristics of GFRP at low temperatures
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Glass Fiber Reinforced Plastic (GFRP) is usually employed as the insulator material of superconducting cable terminal, owing to its excellent mechanical properties and insulation strength at low temperature. However, in the presence of the long-term of surface discharge, GFRP often shows a poor insulation performance, which severely restricts its application on superconducting application. At present, the research on surface discharge and electrical aging of GFRP generally focuses on room temperature and high temperature, and there are few researches on low temperature. This paper designs surface discharge and electrical aging electrode models according to the actual working conditions of the AC superconducting cable terminal. To provide a stable cryogenic temperature environment and high voltage conditions, a cryogenic temperature experiment chamber is employed and builds a low temperature test platform. Based on the established experimental platform, by comparing the related surface discharge characteristics of GFRP at 278.7K, 223K and 153K, the influence mechanism was analysed. Compared with normal temperature, the partial discharge initiation voltage (PDIV) and breakdown voltage (BDV) of GFRP at low temperature are increased, and the average PD charges and PD repetition rate are reduced, indicating that the surface discharge is suppressed at low temperatures. However, for electrical aging at low temperature, the statistical life of the sample at low temperature is greatly reduced, and surface discharge increases in the later stage of aging. The low temperature accelerates the surface discharge and shortens the insulation life of the material. This may be related to the accumulation of space charge and the change of material surface morphology at low temperature.

articleTitle: A novel localization methodology for partial discharge in power transformer considering internal structure
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Ultrasonic method has been widely studied in the field of partial discharge location of power transformer. Previous studies mainly focused on solving the time difference of arrival (TDOA) equations by using different optimization algorithms. However, the complex structure in the transformer will have a great influence on the propagation path and arrival time of ultrasonic signal, and then affect the positioning accuracy. In this paper, the influence of the internal structure of transformer on the ultrasonic propagation paths is explained in detailed. Based on the theoretical analysis, a numerical node model of transformer is established. Based on the model, A* routing algorithm considering the influence of internal structure is proposed to calculate the fastest propagation path between nodes. In order to verify the accuracy of the positioning algorithm, the positioning experiment is carried out on a 35kV transformer.

articleTitle: Defect analysis of abnormal growth of hydrogen in 220kV transformer bushing oil
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: It is analyzed that the abnormal growth defect of hydrogen in oil of 220kV transformer bushing. Result was derived from visual examination, testing and disintegration analysis. It shows that the internal insulating paper, especially the inner screen (25-40 screen), has a more serious aging degree after about 19 years of operation.The aging effect makes the water content of insulating paper and the granularity in oil (5-50μm) increase. Due to polarization in high voltage electric field, particles in oil are aligned to form “Bridges”. It produces low-energy partial discharges, which generate hydrogen gas that accumulates over a long period of time, resulting in excess hydrogen content.

articleTitle: Fiber-optic sensing for partial discharge acoustic detection on power cable joints
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Fiber-optic acoustic sensors have been increasingly applied in the condition monitoring of power equipment for their high sensitivity and strong immunity to electromagnetic interference. The Sagnac fiber sensor system exhibits excellent sensitivity for the interferometric characteristics in the single-loop fiber route, while the phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry (Φ-OTDR) sensor system has great potential in long-distance distributed detection. In this paper, the performance of the two sensor systems was discussed on the partial discharge acoustic detection in power cable joints and compared with the conventional piezoelectric sensor. The acoustic signal characteristics of the two fiber-optic systems and the piezoelectric sensor were compared in terms of the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and frequency spectrum. The results showed that all three acoustic sensors could successfully detect the partial discharges caused by the defect within the cable joint, in terms of SNR, among which the Sagnac sensor system was the optimal as expected, and the piezoelectric sensor was superior to the Φ-OTDR sensor system. Nevertheless, the Φ-OTDR system realized the fault location of the partial discharge induced by the cable joint defect which is of great significance for the distributed detection.

articleTitle: Electro-impulse de-icing (EIDI) test of aircraft wing leading edge
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The aircraft electro-impulse de-icing (EIDI) technology is a kind of mechanical de-icing system, which has a good application prospect. In this paper, the planar coil is wound, the discharge circuit is built, and the parameters of the discharge circuit are calculated. The EIDI model of planar aluminium plate is established. The pulse current of the coil and the electromagnetic pulse force of the leading edge are calculated by simulation. The effects of coil turns, pulse voltage and gap on the pulse action are analysed. According to the drawings of the leading edge of the aircraft, the author made the wing skin with the 6061 aluminium plate of 1.5 mm thickness, fixed the self-made coil in the skin, completed the de-icing test in the artificial climate chamber, and preliminarily verified the feasibility of the electro-impulse de-icing scheme of the leading edge of the wing.

articleTitle: Investigations on detectability of different acids in paper-oil insulation
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Transformers are key elements in power generation and distribution. A large part of the world's transformer fleet is older than its intended service life. The risk of transformer failure increases with age, with the oil-paper insulation of the windings being a major cause of transformer failures. It is mainly the large expensive power transformers that have oil-paper insulation. During the service life of a transformer, its paper-oil insulation is exposed to mechanical and thermal stresses that initiate the aging and degradation process of the insulation. In the course of degradation, both high- and low-molecular weight acids (HMA and LMA) are formed. These acids change the physicochemical properties of the insulating oil and in turn, cause the paper to decay. The LMAs in particular are known to be responsible for paper aging, as they initiate chain scission of cellulose molecules and remain in the paper. In this article spectroscopic examinations of low-molecular weight acids, laboratory-aged paper samples, and unaged acid-injected paper samples are conducted, to determine whether different concentrations of acids in paper samples can be detected using IR-spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Modeling of hybrid DC fuse based on piecewise fitting
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: As a current limiting device, Hybird DC fuse can be used to limit the short-circuit current of the system, In order to precheck the current limiting capability, a simulation model of fuse needs to be established. However, the existing model is relatively complex, and there is no mature model that can be directly called in the existing simulation software. Therefore, this paper designs a piecewise fitting method based on the arcing test data of fuse to describe the whole process of arc drawing. First, considering the influence of resonance and other factors in the test data acquisition of the fuse breaking, the ripple is mixed, and a stepwise filtering algorithm is proposed; Then, according to the degree of fluctuation of the arcing curve, the piecewise points are selected using the normalized curvature criterion and the normalized residual norm criterion respectively, which solves the problem that the piecewise points rely on the designer's practical experience; Finally, according to the results of piecewise fitting, a fuse model of arcing resistance changing with time is constructed in PSCAD, and the simulation verifies the effectiveness of the method used.

articleTitle: Study of effect of core magnetisation on fra by using duality-derived nonlinear transformer model in ATP-EMTP
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: It is common knowledge that the transformer low frequency FRA characteristic is dominated by core magnetisation state. However, most FRA simulation studies do not properly represent the nonlinear characteristics of the core, hence limiting the study of the effects of the core. This paper presents a simulation study on the influence of core magnetisation on FRA traces by using a duality-derived nonlinear transformer model. In this model, the nonlinear characteristic of the core is represented by the use of nonlinear inductance based on open-circuit test data, the model is constructed in EMTP-ATP software and runs in the time domain, the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) is used to obtain the frequency spectrum, of which the whole process is more in line with a practical FRA test. FRA (end-to-end open circuit measurement) simulation results up to 3 kHz with different core residual magnetisations setting were observed and compared in this paper.

articleTitle: High dielectric permittivity copolyimide films by constructing polar units
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Polyimide (PI) film is a class of high-performance polymer materials containing imide rings in the molecular chain. Because of the excellent mechanical properties, reasonable dielectric loss and excellent thermal stability, it is considered to be an important dielectric materials that can be applied to high-temperature energy storage. However, the current polyimide film is difficult to meet its high-temperature energy storage applications due to its low dielectric permittivity (3.3~3.4). In this work, 4,4'-bis(4-aminophenoxy) diphenyl sulfone containing high polar sulfone group (4.25D) were used to alternating copolymerization with pyromellitic dianhydride and 4,4'-Diaminodiphenyl ether. As the content of sulfone groups increases, the dielectric permittivity of copolyimide film first increases and then decreases. When the content of sulfone groups is 40%, the dielectric permittivity of PI-4 reaches the highest value of 4.43 (102 Hz). It is much higher than PI-0 without sulfone groups. Meanwhile, it has good thermal stability and has broad prospects in the application of high-temperature energy storage capacitors.

articleTitle: Discharge characteristics and harmfulness of millimetre metal particles on the 1100 kV insulator surface
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The metal particle on the insulator surface is considered to be an important factor of insulator failures in the GIS/GIL. Studying the partial discharge (PD) characteristics and harmfulness of metal particles on the insulator surface will be helpful in improving the security and reliability of the equipment. In this study, an experiment platform for the 1100-kV insulator with a high-sensitive PD detection system was established. Then the PD characteristics provoked by metal particles (D=0.5 mm, L= 0.8, 2, 5, and 8 mm) at different positions on the 1100-kV insulator surface were investigated. The PD level as well as the harmfulness of metal particles on the insulator surface were discussed. The experimental results show that the apparent charge of the PDs provoked by metal particles shorter than 5 mm is lower than 1 pC under routine PD test condition, which will make the traditional PD detection methods ineffective in detecting these small metal particles on the insulator surface. However, it is noted that even the 5-mm-long metal particle will induce flashover and is a serious threat to the equipment. These results are expected to be helpful for condition monitoring and risk assessment of the GIS/GIL equipment.

articleTitle: Study on the controlled regulation method of Na+ doping on the crosslinking network of epoxy resin
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: During the production and use of epoxy resin insulation materials, metal ions such as sodium ions(Na<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>) can significantly affect the insulation and dielectric properties of epoxy resins. In this paper, it was found that the Na<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> content has a mechanism of promoting and then inhibiting the cross-linking reaction of epoxy resins. Firstly, epoxy resins with different Na<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> contents were prepared and tested for breakdown strength and dielectric properties. The test results show that as the mass fraction of Na<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> increases, the breakdown strength of the specimen gradually decreases, the dielectric constant first decreases and then increases, and the dielectric loss factor increases. Breakdown strength reduced to 68% when Na<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> content is 0.50%. Meanwhile, the effect of Na<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> on the crosslinking network of epoxy resins was calculated using Gaussian. When the Na<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> content is low, it reacts with the curing agent and resin molecules successively, promoting the crosslinking of epoxy resins; as its content increases, the excess Na<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> combine with the epoxy groups, forming O-Na bonds and inhibiting the formation of the crosslinking network. A combination of experiments and molecular simulations verifies the correctness of the mechanism of Na<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> modulation of the crosslinking network of epoxy resins.

articleTitle: VLF Monitored withstand test for distribution cables
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Different acceptance/diagnostics tests have been applied to MV distribution cables in the past. Distribution cables are often applied separately with different testing voltages, such as resonant AC for Withstand test, OWTS for PD test, and VLF for Tan Delta test. Under such testing arrangements, the distribution cables must undertake three rounds of high voltage application process under three different test systems, with much extended test time. Such test arrangements for acceptance and diagnostics tests are also likely to cause potential damage to the distribution cables. This paper presents an alternative and comprehensive MV cable testing system by integrating the withstand, tan delta and partial discharge tests within one testing system (3 tests in one system) by means of very low frequency (VLF) testing methodology, developed by BAUR GmbH in Austria. BAUR has developed a powerful software system BSW4.0 with a very friendly interface. The system has a built-in multiple test programs that the users can edit and modify them according to their needs. The biggest advantage is that it comprises a pre-defined program for doing parallel measurement of dielectric loss and partial discharge. This parallel measurement can shorten the test time to approximately 1 hour, and many measurements can be can be obtained in one round. The software interface can be switched freely between PRG/UI/TD/CAL/REC/PD/LOC/PRPD and it consists of built-in low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, and band-stop filters for doing better PD evaluations. The filter can be turned on and off during the adjustment of Signal gain and trigger level to get an optimum waveform. The dielectric loss data can be displayed in real time such as mean value of dielectric loss, stability, and dielectric loss difference (DTD). It can then be compared with the built-in automatic evaluation in real time and the results can be displayed with facial expressions, `smiling face', `flat face', and `crying face'. Hence, the on-site personnel would be able to receive the results and make a decision immediately. Combined with the cable life evaluation software, it provides a detailed database for the management and classification of cable assets and maintenance planning. Moreover, the system can effectively detect the overall insulation status of the distribution network cable, such as water ingress, water tree and other problems; it can effectively detect the partial discharge problems caused by defects in the construction process, materials of the cable joints and terminal accessories. This has a strong advantage over the traditional applications of applying three different voltage sources. For over two decades, BAUR's `3 tests in one system' VLF testing methodology has been adapted to many power utilities across the world, and proven to be the most efficient and comprehensive acceptance and diagnostics testing methodology for MV distribution cables.

articleTitle: Cumulative damage calculation and life prediction of switching device mosfet for charging pile
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: MOSFET is the core component of electric vehicle charging pile, and its reliability has an important influence on the safe and reliable operation of the whole pile. In order to correlate operating conditions with device aging and reliability, a method for predicting the lifetime of MOSFET in charging pile is proposed. Firstly, the electro-thermal coupling simulation model of charging module is built to calculate the power loss and junction temperature of MOSFET, and then the junction temperature stress distribution is calculated by rain-flow counting algorithm. Finally, according to the principle of linear fatigue cumulative damage, the damage and life of the device under the electro-thermal coupling condition are obtained. It provides a reference for the replacement scheme of module devices in periodic maintenance.

articleTitle: Dielectric properties improvement of polypropylene by silane grafting modification for HVDC cable insulation
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Polypropylene (PP) has extensively attracted attention as a new-type recyclable insulation material for HVDC cable. Grafting modification has been intensively studied for it can effectively improve the dielectric properties of PP. In this paper, vinyltriethoxysilane (VTES) grafting-modified PP with different grafting monomer contents were successfully prepared. The dielectric properties of modified PP were characterised and compared. The molecular electrostatic potential (ESP) of modified PP was simulated and calculated. Based on them, the effect and mechanism of grafting modification were analysed. The results show that after grafting modification, the DC breakdown strength under 30 ºC and 90 ºC is significantly raised by 16.2 % and 47.9%, respectively. The space charge accumulation near cathode is suppressed in VTES-grafted PP. Whereas these dielectric properties of grafting-modified PP deteriorate at high grafting content. Compared with original PP, grafting-modified PP shows higher potential well depth near the grafted silane group in the ESP calculation, which could be strongly correlated to the enhanced dielectric properties of modified PP. This work would provide a reference for the research and development of grafting modified PP-based insulation material for HVDC cable.

articleTitle: Analysis of wind deviation resistance of composite insulator replacing porcelain insulator in tangent tower at different wind speeds
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In order to study the feasibility of replacing disc insulator with composite insulator for suspension string of 500kV straight tower. In this paper, the finite element model of a tower and two lines is established by using ANSYS software. In the case of the same distance, elevation difference and other variables, the displacement of the wires and the wind deflection angle of composite insulators and porcelain insulators are compared when the reference wind speed varies from 15m/s-42m/s. The simulation results as follows :(1) At the same wind speed, after using composite insulators instead of porcelain insulators, the displacement of the wires only slightly increases. (2) At the same wind speed, the wind deflection angle of composite insulators is slightly larger than that of porcelain insulators, but the increase value of the angle is not more than 1°. The simulation results show that, for the general 500kV transmission line, since the mass of wire is much larger than that of insulator string, the change of porcelain insulator into composite insulator has little effect on the wind deviation resistance. This research provides a theoretical basis for checking the wind deviation resistance of composite insulators instead of porcelain insulators in coastal areas.

articleTitle: Dynamic external characterestics and technical weak points of insulated pull rods in GIS circuit breakers
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Insulated pull rod is one of the key factors to ensure the reliable opening and closing of GIS circuit breaker. In addition to long-term resistance to the electric field, the insulated pull rod is also subjected to the instantaneous impact loads during the opening and closing operations, and the impact resistance of pull rods of different materials varies greatly. The dynamic simulation software ABAQUS compared insulated pull rods of aramid material and glass fiber material. Under the same load condition, the stress of the glass fiber pull rod was 144 MPa, which was lower than 328 MPa of the aramid pull rod, indicating the impact resistance of the glass pull rod was better than the other. The weak points of the process appeared around the small holes of the parts, where need further consideration when designing the rod structure. Besides, the draw rod displacement was compared with the measured stroke results of the test to verify the validity of the simulation results. The research results can provide reference and basis for selecting the material performance requirements of insulating pull rods and optimizing the structure of insulated pull rods.

articleTitle: Effect of molecular weight on processability of LDPE based on multi-scale simulation
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In order to accurately establish the direct correlation between molecular weight of low-density polyethylene (LDPE) and processing performance, a multi-scale research method based on molecular dynamics (MD) and finite element (FE) simulations is proposed. The molecular models of LDPE with same branching degrees and different molecular weight are built by MD method. The material parameters of LDPE models are calculated by using reverse non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (RNEMD) approach. Moreover, the material parameters obtained above are taken as input of FE simulation. The Bird-Carreau model and Approximate Arrhenius law are employed to calculate non-isothermal three-dimensional non-Newtonian flow in single screw processing channel. The simulation results show that the materials with larger molecular weight will produce more viscous heat near the position of screw arris top, which leads to the rise of temperature. Due to the difference of shear radio and temperature, shear viscosity distribution of materials is not even. Besides, LDPE with higher molecular weight has the larger range of viscosity and temperature distribution than LDPE with smaller molecular weight. This work provides a new analysis method and theoretical basis for improving the processing and insulation properties of LDPE cables.

articleTitle: Research on application of distributed FBG in on-line temperature sensing of power transformer
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Transformer undertakes the task of energy transmission and is widely used in power system. As one of the core state parameters, temperature determines the lifespan of transformer. Therefore, the realization of accurate on-line real-time temperature measurement is the assurance of a safe and stable power grid. Fiber Bragg grating (FBG) overcomes the defects of traditional temperature measuring methods, such as lack of measuring points and susceptibility to electromagnetic interference. FBG has the advantages of corrosion resistance, high sensitivity, small size and low cost, showing high research and application value. In this paper, the packaging of FBG is optimized firstly and a series of performance tests are carried out. Results show that FBG has good dynamic response characteristics and stability in the range of 30°C∼160°C. Moreover, the linearity of the fitting function is measured to be 0.999 and temperature coefficient is 11.9pm/°C, which meets the needs of temperature measuring. Secondly, a distributed FBG temperature sensing system based on Fabry-Perot demodulation is developed. The FBG system is successfully embedded in a 110kV power transformer to realize distributed online temperature monitoring of transformer oil and three-phase windings.

articleTitle: Simulation analysis for partial deformation of transformer winding and distortion of magnetic leakage distribution considering asymmetric mechanical constraint
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: It is inevitable for transformer to suffer from the impact of short-circuit electromagnetic force during actual operation, which may cause deformation of winding and threaten transformer's stable operation. It is important to explore the relationship between different winding deformation and magnetic flux leakage distortion for the research of on-line diagnosis method for winding defects based on magnetic flux leakage distortion. There may be asymmetric mechanical constraints of winding caused in the actual manufacturing and installation process, such as loosening of vertical spacer and displacement of radial spacer, etc. In this paper, the three-dimensional finite element model of the transformer winding is built, and the structure of its vertical spacer and radial spacer are refined to fully simulate the conditions of asymmetric constraints of the winding. The forms of partial deformation defects of transformer winding are explored, and the distribution of magnetic leakage inside the transformer and the temporal and spatial distribution of short-circuit electromagnetic force are analysed. Finally, the distortion law of the leakage magnetic distribution before and after the winding deformation is analysed. The results show that the variation of magnetic field distribution varies with the deformation form of the winding and the position of the observation line, and the radial deformation of the high voltage winding can produce 73.68% difference on the observation line outside the winding.

articleTitle: Influence of box-in structure and environmental wind velocity on top oil temperature of the converter transformer
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In order to study the influence of Box-in structure and environmental wind velocity on the top oil temperature of converter transformer, a three-dimensional thermal-flow field simulation model of converter transformer with Box-in structure was established based on the finite element principle. Air flow field distribution, oil flow field distribution and temperature field distribution of converter transformer without and with Box-in structure under different environmental wind velocity were simulated by multi-physical field simulation technology. Then, the influence of Box-in structure and environmental wind velocity on the body and top oil temperature of converter transformer was studied. Finally, it is found that the Box-in structure has little effect on the temperature rise of the converter transformer body, but significantly affects the distribution of top oil temperature. With the increase of environmental wind velocity, the top oil temperature decreases. The research in this paper can guide heat dissipation and sensor layout on the top region of converter transformer.

articleTitle: The effect of annular sector pollution on the DC icing flashover performance of LXY4-160 insulators based on natural ice test station
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Affected by directional wind, where the annular sector pollution has been attached on the insulator surface windward side, the pollution flashover voltage decreases significantly compared to the uniform pollution. In this study, the further research of the DC flashover performance of iced insulators with the annular sector pollution is presented, based on Xuefeng mountain natural ice test station. Then the influence of non-uniform pollution on the DC flashover performance under natural icing tests was investigated. Results show that: the ratio WL of windward to leeward side salt deposit density (SDD) will significantly affects the flashover voltage of iced insulators; the U50 is less sensitive to the ratio SWL of leeward surface area to total surface area; Under various WL, the DC flashover voltage of iced insulators is still reduced by the power function with the negative index as SDD increases; Due to annular sector non-uniform pollution, the ice layer residual resistance decreases, which promotes the partial arc propagation and the iced flashover process, and finally reduces the DC icing flashover voltage. The research results could contribute to providing useful reference for the external insulation design of overhead transmission lines with pollution and heavy icing area.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of surface discharge in oil paper insulation based on finite element method and cellular automata
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Surface discharge of oil paper insulation is one of the insulation defects in converter transformers. However, the mechanism of surface discharge in oil paper insulation remains unclear. A novel method of surface discharge in oil paper insulation based on finite element method (FEM) and cellular automata (CA) was proposed to study the mechanism and fractal characteristics. Firstly, the needle-plate electrode without normal component of electric field density was adopted as the geometric model, on which the unstructured triangular mesh generation was performed. Then, the FEM is applied to compute the distribution of potential, electric field and charge in the simulated field, which performed better than finite difference method (FDM) in accuracy and complexity of computation. Finally, the CA model was adopted to simulate the development of surface discharge with the electric field threshold. The results indicated that the numerical simulation model based on FEM-CA can simulate the dynamic process and fractal characteristics of surface discharge in oil paper insulation. According to the fractal dimension curve, the surface discharge can be obviously divided into three stages: inception, propagation and flashover. With the increase of applied voltage, the fractal dimension of surface discharge increases in inception stage, then decreases in propagation stage, and finally increases in flashover stage.

articleTitle: CO2 adsorption effect on breakdown strength of cellulose paper
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The insulation performance of Ultra-High voltage (UHV) transformer is urged to be improved in order to meet the increasingly extreme operational conditions that UHV transformer serves. Carbon dioxide (CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>), an electronegative, non-combustible gas, is applied to improve the electric breakdown strength of UHV transformer insulation by adsorbing on cellulose paper. First, the Brunauer-Emmett-Teller measurement is utilized to find the CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> adsorption quantity and adsorption heat of different cellulose paper. The relationship between ply bond strength and the quantity of CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> adsorption is studied. Then, Alternating Current (AC) breakdown test show the breakdown strength is improved by CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> adsorption. In addition, this paper compares the differences of AC breakdown strength between different cellulose paper, explaining these differences based on ply bond strength and apparent density. Further, in this paper, CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> adsorption is also effective to oil-paper insulation which is widely used in UHV transformers. Finally, by comparing the breakdown strength and dielectric loss of Hydrochloric acid and Acetic acid treated paper pulp, the Acetic acid treatment shows promising future in cellulose paper manufacture. This research is conducive to promote both cellulose and oil-paper insulation performance and prolong the lifespan of UHV transformers.

articleTitle: Study on altitude correction coefficient of pollution flashover voltage of UHVDC insulators with different shed shapes
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In this paper, aiming at the pollution flashover characteristics of UHV large mechanical strength insulators in high altitude area, based on the artificial pollution test research of UHVDC base (Beijing, 45m) and Tibet high altitude test base (Lhasa Yangbajing, 4300m), Pollution flashover characteristic of standard type, 2-sheds and 3-sheds insulators with mechanical strength of 550kN are obtained, and the pollution flashover voltage altitude correction method is proposed The U50% of 2-sheds insulator, standard type and 3-sheds type increases in sequence under different ESDD at two altitudes of 0m and 4300m. Relationship between pollution flashover voltage and attitude was given, which is a linearity relationship and more convenient for application of the engineering design. The altitude correction coefficient of pollution flashover voltage (k1) of standard type, 2-sheds and 3-sheds insulators are 4.24%, 3.82% and 3.82% respectively. The arc floats and arc short circuit are the main reason for the difference of altitude coefficient. Different insulator shed shapes and altitude correction coefficient of pollution flashover voltage of this research can be used to select external insulation of UHV transmission line.

articleTitle: The effect of frequency-dependent soil electrical parameters on the lightning response of a ‘Y’ shaped composite pylon for 400 kV transmission lines
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In this paper, a novel composite pylon with ‘Y’ pattern for 400 kV transmission lines is introduced and its transient response to direct lightning strikes is investigated. The Donau and Eagle tower are also studied as a comparison. The paper focuses on the effect of the frequency-dependent soil model on the lightning response, including overvoltage stressed on the cross-arm (UL) and ground potential rise (GPR) at both first and return strokes. The ground electrode is a vertical metal rod buried into a single or a multi-layer soil. The harmonic behavior of the soil ground impedance at a full-wave frequency is obtained by an accurate method of moment (MoM). The results show that Y-shaped composite pylon has lower UL and GPR compared with the traditional towers when lightning strikes on the top of towers. This phenomenon is more evident for the soil with high resistivity. In addition, the length of the electrode rod can affect the inductive and capacitive characteristics, and a longer length rod would decrease the UL and GPR level, especially when the soil resistivity is high. This research finding can provide a scheme to select ground rods under complex soil conditions.

articleTitle: Optimization and simulation of circuits for dielectric elastomer flexible generator
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The dielectric elastomer can convert mechanical energy into electric energy, used as flexible generators (dielectric elastomer generator, DEG), which has attracted wide attention due to light weight, high energy density and environmental adaptability. However, the procedure of pre-charge is requisite for electromechanical conversion of DEG, which instead increase the complexity and bulk of the devices. Many efforts have been made to eliminate this required but undesired unit. In this contribution, we solved this problem from the view of circuit design optimization. Firstly, we presented the details that illustrate the circuit structure and work principles of double self-priming circuit. Secondly, on this basis, we put forward two circuit designs: promoted self-priming circuit and series polarization-storage circuit, and their simulation in MATLAB/Simulink, design concepts, merits and demerits as well as suitable application occasions were introduced in detail. The simulation results demonstrate that taking part of electric energy converted for pre-charge is feasible. Additionally, the voltage of DEG also can be clamped to a pre-set value which greatly reduce insulation requirements.

articleTitle: Research on the selection and layout of cantilever sensors based on photoacoustic spectroscopy technology
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Cantilever enhanced photoacoustic spectroscopy, as a novel gas content detection method in the maintenance of power equipment, has attracted much studies due to its high sensitivity and its convince in integration. While up to now, there is less quantitative analysis on the free end deformation of the cantilever under different sound wave pressure, which hinders the design and application of the detection device. In this paper, the distribution characteristics of the sound pressure insides the gas pool along with the deformation characteristics of the cantilever were studied through experiment and simulation in COMSOL. The results showed that the maximum sound pressure occurs at the geometric centre point of the gas pool working at the first-order feature frequency, which will decrease with the increase of the length and radius of the main resonant cavity. Meanwhile, the free end deformation of the cantilever decreases with the increasing of Yang's modulus of the cantilever's material, and is positively correlated with its length and width, and negative with the thickness.

articleTitle: Transport behaviour of residual charges in repetitively pulsed streamer evolution in gas gap and along solid surface
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Evolution mechanism and transport behaviour of residual charges in repetitively pulsed streamer discharge were investigated based on pulse-sequence resolved electrical and optical measurements in nitrogen rod-plane gap and along dielectric surface.
