The number of applied pulses before breakdown illustrates nonlinear dependences on the gas pressure and the pulse repetition frequency (PRF). With increasing PRF, the streamer discharge in nitrogen gas gap exhibits a three-stage transition process from an intermittent mode to a successive mode. In the surface discharge, a clear decrease in the inception moment and a slow rising stage are identified at 1 kHz. The average propagation velocity decreases and then saturates with increasing PRF. The space-charge-dominated memory effect mechanism is analysed based on preliminary fluid simulation and the distribution of spatial electric field.

articleTitle: Simulation on arcing process considering continuous motion of non-return valve for auto-expansion circuit breakers
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Auto-expansion circuit breaker has great advantages over puffer-type circuit breaker due to its lower operating energy. Motion statuses of non-return valve are closely related to the current interrupting ability of auto-expansion circuit breakers. Since movement of non-return valve is restricted by the movable parts where it is located, its statuses are hard to be determined. In this paper, based on an auto-expansion circuit breaker, two dimensional MHD (magneto-hydro-dynamics) model coupled with the continuous motion model of non-return valve is established. Nozzle ablation contributes to the pressure rise in the heating volume and therefore is considered. It is found that the proposed model could realize a more detailed prediction for the movement of non-return valve. Interaction between the non-return valve and the arc zone, and motion characteristics of the non-return valve during current interruption are investigated under 36 kA and 40 kA with arcing time 15.3 ms. Distributions of mole fraction of PTFE and temperature in the heating volume are obtained. Transient velocity of the non-return valve and the withstanding forces are acquired. Parameters mentioned above are compared. It is expected that the optimization design of auto-expansion circuit breakers could be conducted more accurately with the assistance of this coupled model.

articleTitle: Thermal-oxidative aging effected on the properties of EPDM used for nuclear cables insulation
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: To satisfy demands of cable insulation in the construction and development of nuclear power, a new formula of EPDM used for nuclear cable was prepared. The effect of thermal-oxidative aging on the mechanical, thermal and dielectric properties was researched in this paper. The change of elongation at break caused by aging were characterized by tensile testing. The differential scanning calorimeter (DSC) tests were carried out at different aging stages. The dielectric properties of polarity at different aging stages were measured. The results showed that, the elongation at break reduced with aging time prolonged, and the parameters of polarity changed obviously, which w ere comparable with the changes in mechanical structures.

articleTitle: The microstructure study on the high-flexible conductors for charging pile cable applications
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: As the urgent requirement for the sustainable development and green energy, the development of electric automobile technology is progressing fast in the recent years. The electric cable connecting the pile and the car during charging plays an important role on the performance of the charging station. Besides the electric properties, the mechanical behavior of charging pile cable, especially the fatigue of high-flexible conductors, has been considered as one of the central issue, which highly relies on the their microstructure characteristics. In this study, we have conducted the microstructure studies on four different types of high-flexible copper conductors by using X-ray diffraction (XRD), optical microscope (OM) as well as scanning electron microscope (SEM). The results show that three of the specimens show very uniform microstructure with homogeneous distribution of grain size from inner part to the outer part of the conductors, which all show more inferior mechanical performances. In contrast, the high-flexible conductor with superior mechanical performance exhibits a special “gradient” microstructure, which has a non-uniform distribution of grain size showing larger grain size with fibrous texture for the inner portion and smaller grain size in the outer portion. And the excellent mechanical performance has been ascribed to finer grain and such a gradient microstructure, which contains the outer layer of equiaxed grains providing enough ductile and electrical conductivity, and the inner layer of fibrous grain can gurantee strength of the conductor. Our work reveals the microstructure characteristics for high-flexible conductors, and provides guideline for the designning of high-performance conductors for charging pile cable applications.

articleTitle: Partial discharge measurements and effects of transients on power cables
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The advent of new combinations of equipment and integrations of different power grids can potentially be accompanied by transient voltage phenomena which affect the reliability of electrical insulation systems. In particular, this affects insulation susceptible to partial discharge behaviour due to additional transient waveforms. Nowadays in transmission grid planning, overhead lines are increasingly combined with underground power cables. In switching such connections impulses could occasionally occur and superimpose on the normal AC voltage which will lead to superimposed transient waveforms. Those transient voltages will impose an additional stress on the cable insulation that could trigger partial discharges, that sustain. This paper reviews our recent research of some cable insulation defects of industrial relevance by partial discharge measurement on high voltage power cables stressed by different waveforms, including impulses, superimposed transients on AC voltage. This paper identifies achievements and at the same time challenges still to be solved in partial discharge measurement under different waveforms.

articleTitle: Research on insulation aging state of XLPE Cables under accelerated aging
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to study the insulation aging state of XLPE cables under accelerated aging. We carried out the broadband dielectric spectrum test, power frequency breakdown test, differential scanning calorimetry test and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy test on XLPE specimens. The test results show that, with the accelerated aging, the breakdown voltage of XLPE specimens rises and then falls, the dielectric constant and dielectric loss integral values decrease and then rise, the crystallinity increases and then falls, and the carbonyl index first falls and then rises. The research results show that the insulation state of cross-linked polyethylene is first optimized within a certain time of accelerated aging, but gradually deteriorates with the increase of accelerated aging time.

articleTitle: Effect of thermal aging on the decay-like fracture of silicone rubber composite insulator
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In order to explore the effect of thermal aging on the decay-like fracture of composite insulator, this paper uses muffle furnace to conduct accelerated thermal aging test at different temperatures and different time lengths. The morphological changes of the samples are observed. The three-point bending test, thermo-gravimetric test and Fourier infrared test were carried out to test the bending performance, epoxy resin content and characteristic functional group content of the samples. The results show that thermal aging will accelerate the deterioration of composite insulator and play an important role in the decay-like fracture. With the increase of thermal aging temperature and time, the surface of the core rod sample gradually changes from emerald green to black, and the bending resistance of the samples gradually decrease. When the temperature is lower but the heating time is longer, the content of epoxy resin and bending mechanical properties will be reduced. Meanwhile, the energy from heating will attack the matrix of core rod epoxy resin, resulting in the fracture of main chain, the decrease of methyl, aromatic structure and the gradual degradation of polymer macromolecules of epoxy resin.

articleTitle: Development of management system for bushing UV imaging detection
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The insulation state of electrical bushing is related to the safety of power grid. To diagnose the insulation state of the in-field bushing, an intelligent diagnosis framework based on artificial intelligence is designed; the B/S development mode manages the UV images and videos of bushing discharge, and develops a set of image and video management data According to the database system, the database management system of UV imaging samples is constructed, which integrates the function of bushing recognition and discharge severity assessment based on UV image. The developed software is applied to the inspection of transmission lines and substations with good application result.

articleTitle: Anomaly analysis of 500 kv high voltage reactor based on multi-detection information fusion
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In this paper, a case of detection and diagnosis of a 500kV high voltage reactor is introduced. In routine test, it is found that the oil chromatographic data of a 500kV high voltage reactor is abnormal, the composition analysis of dissolved gas in oil is adopted, it is found that there is a discharge and overheating defect inside the reactor based on three-ratio method. In order to further determine the type and location of defect, various detection methods such as high-frequency method and ultrasonic method are adopted. Through the transverse comparison of mechanical vibration detection results, the abnormal vibration area is found in the reactor. At the same time, it is found that there are intermittent discharge and partial discharge signals in the corresponding area, and ultrasonic testing found that there is impact collision vibration signal in this area. Synthesizing various detection results, it is inferred that the long-term abnormal vibration of reactor leads to loose of structural parts and poor contact, which leads to discharge and overheating defects. A variety of detection methods are used in this case, which provides a reference for the processing and analysis of similar anomalies, and the operation reliability of reactor is effectively improved.

articleTitle: An integrated voltage generator for medium voltage power cable insulation diagnosis
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Power electronics are widely used in high-voltage testing equipment with the development of semiconductor technology. This paper proposes an integrated technique for power cable insulation diagnosis. By applying the design of a novel bidirectional high-voltage switch composed of IGBT stacks to a voltage multiplier, the integrated technique is capable of achieving both damped ac (DAC) and very low frequency (VLF) voltage waveforms for withstand voltage and partial discharge testing. This distinctive topology enables the equipment used in field become light-weight and compact. In this study, the generation principles of both voltages are analysed in detail and the feasibility of the integrated technique is verified using MATLAB/Simulink. The simulations are carried out to give a support for the hardware parameter design in DAC and VLF voltage generation. Subsequently, a laboratory prototype is built and experimental tests are performed under different load conditions in a laboratory to verify its performance in the field. The results show that the integrated test technique can greatly improve the efficiency of insulation diagnosis in power industrial practice.

articleTitle: Design of robust, safe and reliable switchgear with electro-thermal numerical simulations
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Thermal management is a very important issue in medium voltage switchgear design. A temperature rise test has to be performed in order to make sure that the allowed temperature limits are not exceeded. To optimise the number of needed design tests, it is important to predict the temperature rise with a simulation tool. Sulfur hexafluoride (SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>) gas, used widely in medium voltage circuit breakers, can produce a potent greenhouse effect if released into the atmosphere. Among the alternatives, Carbon Dioxide (CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) and its mixtures are considered promising. In this paper, a comparative study of thermal behaviour SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> and CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> in medium voltage switchgear is studied. Experimental investigations were also carried out to verify the simulation results and good agreement was achieved. SF6 gas exhibited the smallest temperature rise in comparison to CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. Additional simulations were carried out to assess the effect of conductor contact resistances, ambient temperature and increased load current levels. The simulation tool allows a number of iterative simulations to be performed in order to investigate design parameters, operating and fault conditions which are potentially difficult, destructive and costly to set up and test. Prototype materials, construction and, critically, time can reduced to a minimum by simulation. Such modelling capability is essential to ensure a safe and reliable and reliable operation of the switchgear.

articleTitle: Pulsed townsend measurement of electron swarm parameters in dry air
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In this study, we introduced the experimental setup for pulsed Townsend (PT) method as well as the physical model for acquisition of electron swarm parameters. The ionization rate coefficients, attachment rate coefficients, electron drift velocity and density-normalized longitudinal diffusion coefficients in dry air were obtained, with the pulsed Townsend experiment. Besides, the reduced critical electric fields for the gas were determined from the effective ionization rate coefficients. The results were compared with the swarm parameters calculated by a Boltzmann equation solver. These parameters are fundamental quantities for describing low temperature plasmas, which has great implications for finding SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>-alternatives.

articleTitle: Field measurement and analysis on wind-induced vibration response of single column lightning rod
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The lightning rod, as a towering structure device, is often in the wind vibration state. The wind response spectrum data and its natural frequency of the single pole lightning rod were tested by means of environment random excitation method. Through the time-history analysis, the wind vibration response of the single column lightning rod structure is mainly based on the first order vibration type in this direction, and the structure has a relatively obvious resonance response. The analysis of the displacement, bending moment, and shear maximum value of the single pillar lightning rod in time shows that the lightning rod increases with height, the displacement response increases, and the moment and shear response are constantly decreasing. The maximum value of the moment and shear force are all present at the root of the lightning rod. The difference of the wind vibration coefficient between the three is more obvious, indicating that the wind vibration effect of different responses is different, and different wind vibration coefficients should be taken for different response.

articleTitle: Cable deformation and electric field distortion of submarine cable insulation caused by anchoring impact
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Anchor damage is one of the most significant failure modes in submarine cable. Generally, it is difficult for anchor impact to cause an immediate cable broken and fault due to the buried depth under the seabed. However, majority of the anchor can penetrate into the seabed and cause the cable deformation. It presents little influence on the power transmission but affects the electrical performance and the lifetime of submarine cable. In this paper, the electric field distortion of submarine cable insulation on the basis of the cable deformation caused by anchor impact was studied. The cable deformation characteristics was obtained by simulation of anchor impacting in a 35 kV AC submarine cable. The relative permittivity, conductivity as well as dielectric loss of insulation caused by the effects of residual stress were considered. An obvious deformation occurred in the insulation near the anchoring impact region, which causes the local electric field distortion. The simulation results indicate that the increase of insulation electric field is not only due to the deformation of insulation, but also the decrease of relative permittivity. Meanwhile, the space charge in the insulation also increases in the deformed insulation layer, which probably enhance the degradation of cable insulation. This paper provides a correlation between the anchor damage and the cable insulation performance for submarine cable.

articleTitle: Calculating algorithm for the interface charge density of oil-pressboard insulation considering the scale-effect under DC voltage
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The interface charge characteristics and its influencing mechanism on electric field is critical for the reliable design of insulation structure of converter transformer. The presented calculating methods for interface charge density lack of the consideration for the effect of structure scale. In this paper, three oil-pressboard insulation model with different scales were established, and the electric field strength in oil was captured. Based on the infinitesimal method, a calculating algorithm for the interface charge density of oil-pressboard insulation considering the scale-effect under DC voltage was proposed. The results indicated that, with the model scale perpendicular to the electric field direction increasing, the interface charge density tends to decrease but with a maximum deduction of only 1.22%, while the total interface charge quantity shows a significant increase, which induced the large charge field and the exert severer negative effect on the applied field.

articleTitle: Study on the conduction characteristics of SF6 gas gap under capillary pulse plasma injection
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: With the rapid development of modern power systems, the requirements for switchgear are getting much stricter. Especially in flexible HVDC transmission system, switching time limited within 1ms under extremely operating coefficients is of much importance for fast protection switch to limit over-voltages. To solve this fast protection problem, in this paper capillary pulsed discharge is proposed to generate plasma injection into a SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas gap to initiate rapid conduction of the SF6 gap under extremely low operating coefficients. A high-speed camera was used to photograph the discharge process of the SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas gap. The breakdown performance of the SF6 gas gap under plasma injection has been investigated. The influence of working coefficient, gap distance, and gas pressure on the conduction of the SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas gap were also studied. The optimal capillary size and trigger pulse parameters are proposed according to the experimental results. Captured images of the discharge process of the SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas gap indicate that: due to the strong electronegativity of SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> and extremely low working coefficients, streamer will not be found unless the injected plasma develops almost through the entire gas gap. However, even if the streamer appears, still it takes a few microseconds to form spark discharge channel, which implies the breakdown of the SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gap. Some methods such as increasing the working coefficient, reducing the gap distance and gas pressure are proposed to obtain faster switching time.

articleTitle: Research on key technology of turn to turn insulation test of iron core reactor by high frequency method
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In order to solve the problem that the turn insulation of core reactor can't be tested effectively, we propose a turn insulation test method based on high-frequency resonance and clarify its advantages. In this paper, the principles for determining test voltage and the relationship between test current and frequency were discussed. Meanwhile, the range of test frequency satisfying series and shunt reactance was proposed in detail. Through theoretical analysis, the expressions about the output voltage of inverter and the reactor voltage under series resonance were obtained. To ensure the top voltage of reactor can reach the rated value, the time-domain synchronization algorithm of resonance condition detection and frequency tuning were analysed. The test scheme and the estimation of inter turn short circuit current were discussed in detail. It was concluded that the inter turn short defect will lead to obvious voltage detuning. That is, the amplitude-frequency characteristics of test system will decrease rapidly, which can be used as the criterion for turn to turn insulation defects of iron core reactor. The experimental results show that the test method based on high-frequency resonance can detect the insulation defects of iron core reactor effectively, which provides an important reference for practical engineering application.

articleTitle: Diagnosis and analysis of high-frequency PD detection in cable equipment
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: First of all, this paper describes the exist types of the partial discharge technology in cable equipment. Secondly, explaining the reason of high-frequency partial discharge phenomenon in power cables. Then explaining the detection principle and method of high-frequency partial discharge of cable equipment. Finally, this paper introduces a case of cable defect which is discovered by high-frequency partial discharge detection technology. The cause of the defect is analysed and the defect problem is dealt with, which could provide a meaningful reference for the high-voltage cable live detection work and improve the detection level of the live detection work in the future.

articleTitle: Generation mechanism and restraining measures of DC over voltage in metro power supply system
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The subway which is also called urban rail transit is an important part of urban transportation. At present, uncontrollable diodes are mostly used in subway traction grids to form rectifiers, so the current itself has the characteristic that the current cannot be reversed. Under the premise of this DC catenary, the voltage on the DC catenary side when multiple trains are running at the same time is still relatively stable, but when only a few trains are running, the larger feedback energy due to motor braking will appear more obviously. As a result, the reactive power on the DC catenary side changes, and the voltage on the DC catenary side is significantly increased. Aiming at this phenomenon, the AC motor is taken as the research object, and the starting and braking stages of the AC motor are studied separately, and the corresponding parameter changes of traction and braking force are calculated for each stage. PSCAD is used to reproduce part of the traction grid, reproduce the traction and braking operation of the motor, explain the overvoltage mechanism that appears in the DC catenary, and propose appropriate suppression measures.

articleTitle: Application of a cluster-algorithm for partial discharge analysis at DC voltage under practical conditions
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: A previous introduced approach for signal clustering at partial discharge tests under high-voltage direct current (HVDC) based on cross correlation and statistical evaluation performs well on selected test samples under laboratory conditions. The algorithm differentiates partial discharge signals originating from multiple sources and disturbances successfully and return groups with the data set separated in classes. In contrast to the laboratory, under real test conditions on large test objects new challenges arise regarding signal acquisition and processing to get a correct and reliable clustering of partial discharge signals. Hence, testing and verification the performance of the presented algorithm under practical conditions at a real factory test side is necessary. Furthermore, different clustering methods are compared regarding the usability for partial discharge measurements under DC voltage.

articleTitle: Effects of TiO2 nanoparticles and electrode materials on impulse breakdown performance of propylene carbonate under uneven electric field
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Liquid dielectrics are widely used in power systems owing to their excellent insulation properties. Nanoparticles and electrode materials have demonstrated a great capability of enhanced dielectric of base insulation liquids. In this study, the impulse breakdown performance of TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanoparticles doped propylene carbonate under an uneven electric field was investigated. We first proposed a measurement method for the uneven electric field under the blade electrode using an 8-channel array photodetector. The effects of nanoparticles and aluminum, copper, and stainless-steel electrodes on the breakdown voltage and electric field distribution characteristics of the liquid were studied. These results indicate that the breakdown voltage of the stainless steel electrode is the most significant polarity effect under an uneven electric field. The negative impulse breakdown voltage of the liquid under the stainless steel electrode is 24.6% higher than that of the positive polarity. The positive breakdown voltage of the TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanoparticles doped propylene carbonate under aluminum and copper increased by 25% and 17.2%, however, it is no obvious increase under the stainless steel electrode. The TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanoparticles capture electrons in the space charge zone which inhibits the development of streamers, and weakens the influence stage of electrode materials. For the negative polarity, the weakening of the polarity effect promotes the development of the streamer, resulting in a decrease in the breakdown voltage. This study enriches the discharge mechanism of liquids in uneven electric fields and provides a valuable reference for improving the liquid insulation performance and the discharge mechanism.

articleTitle: Determination of voltage dependence of capacitance of 100 kV and 300 kV compressed gas capacitors using the kinetic method
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Measuring voltage dependence capacitance of high voltage compressed gas capacitors is challenging when levels are below one ppm (one Micro-Farad per Farad). Indeed, traditional methods such as direct capacitor comparison, voltage transforming, voltage-doubling, direct voltage, frequency doubling, and simplified tilting are not suitable because they need complex procedures, reference standards with known voltage dependence and accurate capacitance bridges. The kinetic method could be used to determine a possible quasi-zero voltage dependence or at least to detect it. A 100 kV capacitor was studied using this technique at LNE with support from PTB. An excellent initial eccentricity, equal to (0,070 ± 0,010) mm, was determined and which is in accordance with what is claimed by the manufacturer. Quasi-zero voltage dependence (0.45 ± 0.10) ppm, was determined. This low level of uncertainty is difficult to reach with any other method, the internal dimensions of the capacitor have to be estimated. Another 300 kV capacitor was also investigated without any knowledge of its internal dimensions. It was concluded that it has a medium eccentricity despite its good calibration results, equal to (7.0 ± 5.0) ppm.

articleTitle: PD characteristic and motion behaviours of free metallic particles in transformer oil with paper-covered electrodes
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The existence of free metallic particle poses a serious threat to the oil insulation in power transformer. And ungrounded conductors in a transformer is generally covered by solid dielectrics, e.g. insulation paper. The introduction of insulation paper will change the charged performance of metallic particle, so its motion behaviours and partial discharge (PD) characteristics will be different from the case with bare electrodes. In order to clarify these, the circulation flow device of transformer oil was built. The movement behaviours of metallic particles with a diameter of 150μm was recorded by the high-speed camera. It is shown that the particles moved with oil flow in the horizontal direction while moving up-and-down in the vertical direction and colliding with electrodes. When electrodes were paper-covered, the particles would temporarily settle on the paper-covered surface. The landing-point spacing and time intervals of collision were longer than those for the bare electrodes. In addition, PD experiments of free metallic particles were carried out, and the PD characteristic parameters were extracted. It is found that when the electrodes were covered by insulation paper, partial discharge inception voltages (PDIV) became higher and the discharge magnitude and frequency decreased. The discharge mainly occurred around 45° and 160°. Finally, the influence of particle motion on PD characteristics were discussed.

articleTitle: Vibration simulation of high voltage parallel reactor based on multi-physics field
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Master the vibration characteristics of the internal core of the high voltage parallel reactor, build the 3D simulation model according to the actual core structure of the high voltage parallel reactor, use the COMSOL multi-physical field coupling simulation software, and calculate flux density distribution, volume strain and vibration displacement distribution of reactor core and winding under normal working conditions. The calculation results show that the maximum vibration displacement of top core of high voltage parallel reactor and the vibration strength of core column and left and right side column are equal. Simulation results can provide reference for structural design and vibration monitoring.

articleTitle: Simulation analysis of electric field distribution for terminal ball in 750kV substation
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The terminal balls of a 750kV high voltage substation located in the northwest of China is taken as the research subject in this paper. A three-dimensional finite element simulation model is established through Ansys and the electric field distribution on the surface of the terminal ball under ideally smooth and defective conditions is analysed respectively. Based on the threedimensional scanning technology, the distortion of the electric field for terminal ball with corona discharge is thoroughly calculated and discussed. The simulation results demonstrated that: The maximum values of surface electric field on the terminal balls vary greatly with positions and he surface electric field on the terminal ball near the arrester reveals to be the highest; The electric field of phase B and C at the same position are higher than that of phase A; The value of electric field decreases gradually as the diameter of the ball increases; However, when the diameter of the ball increases to a certain extent, the rate of reduction becomes slower and the degree of decline is limited;. The concave defect has a greater impact on the surface electric field of the terminal ball and the influence of the defect on the distortion of the electric field is related to the location. When the defect is located at the vertical center of the ball, the corresponding distortion proves to be the smallest. When it is located diagonally below the ball, the degree of distortion is the most serious. In actual operation, the defect of the terminal ball can cause the distortion of surface electric field, resulting in undesired phenomenon of corona discharge. The research results of this paper can provide references for the prevention and optimization design of corona discharge generated by terminal balls in 750kV substations.

articleTitle: Analysis of partial discharges of power cables with 50HZ and VLF
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Partial discharge measurement is the most important technique used to assess the quality of the insulation of Power Cables in the laboratory and as well as in the field. In the laboratory, the partial discharge measurement on power cables is carried out with 50 Hz sinusoidal frequency source. However, for field cables, due to the high energy requirement of the source and practical transportation difficulties, it is not feasible to carry out PD measurements at the normal operating frequency. Hence off-line partial discharge measurements are being carried out using a very low frequency (0.01 Hz - 1 Hz) source. In this paper, the mathematical model of a cylindrical void in the XLPE power cable is simulated and the partial discharge activities in the void at three different frequencies (0.01 Hz, 0.1 Hz and 50 Hz) are measured. The imperfections in the Cable insulation, such as voids, are modelled by using the improved ABC Capacitive model. The partial discharge current pulses developed due to voids are captured for all three frequencies. The PRPD patterns and statistical parameters of the simulated PD for all three frequencies are compared. The comparison of PD with 0.01 Hz and 0.1 Hz is also carried out for the field-measured PD signals.

articleTitle: Dynamic solidification process of silicone oil within outdoor cable terminals under cold conditions
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Outdoor oil-filled cable terminals play an important role in transmission and transformation network, but its frequent explosion and disintegration accidents in cold weather bring great risks to the stable operation of power system. So in this paper, the viscosity-temperature characteristics of the silicone oil were tested according to the actual situation of many similar faults this year, and the electric field-temperature-fluid multi-physical fields simulation model of 220 kV oil-filled cable terminals was built. Based on the phase transformation principle, the dynamic solidification process of the insulating silicone oil was analysed. The results show that the environmental conditions are the main factors affecting the internal temperature distribution of cable terminals with large nominal cross-sectional area. Because the load current of cables in operation is generally low, the insulating oil inside the cable terminals will solidify in different degrees in cold weather. To a certain extent, the analysis results reveal the failure mechanism of oil-filled cable terminals burst breakdown and disintegration under cold conditions, and also provide theoretical support for material selection optimization and fault risk assessment of high voltage oil-filled cable terminals.

articleTitle: Study on transient electric shock of human body under high-voltage hybrid transmission lines
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The hybrid electric field produced by the AC and DC lines is subtly different from that of separate AC lines or separate DC lines. The body feeling under the hybrid electric field is also different. The human transient shock test system under the transmission line is established in the laboratory. The discharge process and the charge amount can be recorded by the system. The transient electric shock under three different conditions is simulated in the test system. The influence of the transmission line radius and voltage on the quantity of electric charge is analyzed. The results show that the charge accumulated on the suspended metal plate is influenced by the AC electric field and the total electric field. Based on the requirement of transient electric shock control, the control level of AC/DC hybrid electric field is proposed in this paper. There is a negative linear correlation between the normalized value of power frequency electric field and the normalized value of total electric field intensity when the charge amount of transient shock discharge is constant. It is of great significance to solve the complaint of electromagnetic environment and to choose the parameters of transmission line design.

articleTitle: Influence of lighting rod flange connection parameters on bolt fatigue performance and improvement measures
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of multiple accidents of steel pipe lightning rods in high-voltage substations, the bolt stress is calculated by finite element software, the pre-tightening force and the influence of adjacent bolt damage on the flange connecting bolts are analyzed, the rain flow counting method is used to calculate the stress time history, and the known SN is used The curve judges the damage of the bolts on the right side, calculates the damage value within the corresponding time, and obtains the fatigue mechanism of the flange bolts of the steel tube lightning rod of the high-voltage substation, and then proposes methods to reduce the fatigue of the bolts and improve the connection of the steel tube.

articleTitle: Influence of oil-pressboard combination on electric field distribution of main insulation structure on valve-side winding of HVDC converter transformer
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The main insulation structure of the valve-side winding of converter transformer bears the effect of AC and DC superimposed voltage during operation. This condition leads to a higher probability of failure in converter transformers than in AC transformers. The simulation calculation of electric field distribution of insulation structure is an important method for design of converter transformers. The current simulation study only considers the electrical performance of the oil-pressboard insulation in the initial state. However, the effect of aging on the electric field distribution of oil-pressboard insulation is not considered. This study analyses the effect of different oil-pressboard combinations on the electric field distribution under heat aging. Firstly, this study establishes a model of the main insulation structure of the valve-side winding of the HVDC converter transformer. Secondly, the variation of resistivity and relative permittivity for different oil-pressboard combinations with different aging states is obtained. Finally, the influence of oil-pressboard combination on the electric field distribution of the main insulation structure of the valve-side winding under AC and DC superimposed voltage is calculated by simulation.

articleTitle: The influecne of the background gas on photoacoustic signal
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The cantilever beam photoacoustic(PA) spectroscopy technology has attracted the attention of many scholars due to its high sensitivity. For different application objects, the background gas type of the gas to be measured may be different. At present, there are few reports on the influence of background gas types on the intensity of PA signal for cantilever enhanced PA gas detection technology. In this paper, we carried out CO detection under the background gases of nitrogen (N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>), sulfur hexafluoride (SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>), helium (He) and argon (Ar), respectively. The results show that for CO gas with the same concentration, the order of PA signal intensity from strong to weak is Ar>He >N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>>SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>. Through the theoretical derivation of the intensity of PA signal, the theoretical formula of the intensity of PA signal is obtained. When the detection device and the gas to be tested remain unchanged, the intensity of PA signal is related to the heat capacity ratio of the gas, and the greater the heat capacity ratio, the stronger the PA signal.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation on the hysteresis loop effect of the body force induced by DBD plasma actuation
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The application of a dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) plasma actuator to achieve active flow control is one of the most widely studied objects of plasma flow control. For DBD actuation with millisecond AC power supply, the aerodynamic effect plays a major role in flow control, and the body force induced by the DBD plasma actuator is one of the important parameters which can characterize the aerodynamic effect. The geometric and electrical parameters of the DBD plasma actuator are the key factors of the body force. This paper uses high-precision electronic balance and electrical measurements to analyze the influence of different geometric parameters, different voltages and unsteady actuation parameters on the body force. The experimental results show that: (1) The increase of the buried electrode width can significantly improve the body force within a certain range, while the exposed electrode width has little effect on the body force. (2) The induced body force increases linearly with the applied voltage, but the linear growth rates of different voltage intervals are different. The curve of body forces have an obvious abrupt change as the applied voltage changing from 13kV to 18kV, which forms a typical hysteresis loop. (3) In the case of the same voltage, the induced body force generated by the unsteady actuation is less than that of the steady actuation. As the increase of the duty cycle, the body force will gradually approach a steady stage, and the increase of the pulse frequency will reduce the body force.

articleTitle: Analysis of internal electrothermal performance of varistor under impulse current
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In order to study the mechanism of the electric heating distribution inside the varistors under the action of impulse current, the electric heating environment inside the varistor was theoretically analysed by constructing a model with the help of Comsol Multiphysics simulation software. It is found that under the action of the impulse current, the current distribution of different part of the varistor is different. The current density of the contact area between the edge of the electrode and the varistor sample is larger than other parts, and the current in this area shows a trend of "outward diffusion". On the other hand, the uneven distribution of current makes the temperature at the edge of the electrode much higher than other parts, forming a ringshaped high-temperature zone. It can be inferred that the electrical and thermal degeneration of this part is more serious, which is consistent with the experimental results that samples often have perforations in the edge part. Finally, we briefly analysed the changes of related parameters under different impulse current amplitude.

articleTitle: Development approach of a leader-propagation-model for the discharge process of various voltage forms in long air gap rod-plane electrode configurations
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In insulation co-ordination, it is desirable to utilize deterministic simulation models to evaluate long air gap discharge/break-down processes under different electrode configurations and voltage forms, especially in the form of leader propagation models (LPM). Yet, current LPMs show inconsistencies and deviations due to their empirical nature and the historically related time-sampling measurement limitations. Through sub-process differentiated investigations of lightning impulse (LI) voltage dis-charges conducted in the 2010s, it was shown, that the leader sub-process exhibits a low statistical uncertainty in its physical parameters and dependencies. The investigations resulted in the development of a semi-physical LPM of LI voltage under rod-plane configurations for near-standard atmospheric conditions, with the voltage-time characteristic as its sole input. Following that approach via a joint Sino-German research project, recent high-resolution, electrical-optical measurements of the discharge process in rod-plane configurations under switching impulse (SI) and AC voltage were analysed to expand the LI-LPM for SI and AC voltage. As a first step, the paper at hand presents a selection of measurements of various gap distances and the func-tional principle of the LPM. The LPM-specific dependency between leader length and pre-discharge current is validated by comparing the optically measured leader lengths with the calculated leader propagation based upon the measured current. It is shown, that the LPM is basically suited to be utilized for various voltage forms.

articleTitle: Transient response characteristics of metal oxide arrester under high altitude electromagntic pulse
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In order to study the strong electromagnetic pulse effect of the critical vulnerable equipment of power system and evaluate the survival ability of the high-altitude electromagnetic pulse, it is necessary to study the transient response characteristics of the metal oxide arrester to the high-altitude electromagnetic pulse by experiment. In this paper, an experimental platform of high altitude electromagnetic pulse conduction current injection for a typical 10kV metal oxide arrester is set up, and the key parameters such as peak value of overshoot voltage, peak value of residual voltage, action voltage and response time are obtained by the experiment. The results show that: the action voltage of this type of metal oxide arrester is 3.53 times higher than that of its rated voltage, the peak value of overshoot voltage is 2.20 times higher and the peak value of residual voltage is 1.57 times higher than the residual voltage under the lightning impulse current, and the response time varies little with the electromagnetic pulse conduction current amplitude, with an average of 45.86 nanoseconds under high altitude electromagnetic pulse conduction environment.

articleTitle: The thermal decomposition characteristics of HFO1234ze(E) gas for MV equipment
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Gas insulating medium SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>, which is widely used in high voltage electrical equipment, has serious greenhouse effect. HFO1234ze(E) has very low greenhouse effect, low liquefaction temperature (-19°C) and excellent insulation performance, so it has great application potential as a new eco-friendly insulation gas. In this paper, the partial overheating decomposition characteristics of HFO1234ze(E) gas under different temperatures (150-400°C) were explored through experiments. It was found that HFO1234ze(E) did not decompose at 150°C to 200°C, and the isomer HFO1234ZE (Z) was produced at 250°C. With the increase of temperature from 250°C to 300°C, the yield of HFO1234ze(Z) did not increase much. When the temperature was higher than 350°C, the decomposition of HFO1234ze(E) intensified, and when the temperature reached 400°C, the gas would decompose violently, and other decomposition products would be produced. Meanwhile, the decomposition mechanism of HFO1234ze(E) under partial overheating fault was investigated using density functional theory (DFT). The research conclusions in this article provide theoretical guidance for the application of HFO1234ze(E).

articleTitle: Estimating equivalent air core inductance of a uniform winding as a function of its length from measured DPI magnitude-experimental results
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Knowledge about the variation of equivalent air-core inductance along the winding length (termed as M0x) of a uniform transformer winding has significant importance in studies involving localization of mechanical damages in a winding and in the synthesis of ladder network equivalent circuits. A simple empirical relationship to estimate M0x of a uniform transformer winding from its measured driving point impedance (DPI) is presented. The proposed method requires three DPI measurements: one with neutral-end open and the other with neutral-end shorted. The third DPI is measured with a known external lumped capacitance connected between the neutral and ground. This method requires only the first few dominant natural frequencies observable in the first two of the DPIs. The proposed methods feasibility was initially verified by simulation on a typical ten section mutually coupled ladder network. Experimental results are also presented by implementing the method on 33 kV continuous disc winding, 11 kV interleaved disc winding and finally on a 2.2 kV, 70 kVA transformer winding containing a shorted LV secondary.

articleTitle: Research on spectral Recognition Method of Tree Species in Transmission Corridor
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The threat of tree barriers in the transmission corridor will seriously affect the safe operation of the power grid, and accurate prevention of tree barriers is required. Facing the situation that existing tree barrier models mostly model a certain type of trees, it is imperative to accurately identify the types of trees. In this paper, through the spectral identification of common tree species of transmission lines, the competitive adaptive weighted algorithm is used to extract the spectral line features, adding the vegetation index is used as an input to establish the model. The validity of the model for blade identification was verified through experiments, and the aerial images of transmission lines were used to verify the feasibility of field application. At the same time, the spectral lines after feature extraction are compared with the full spectrum segment modeling, and it is verified that the model after feature extraction has higher recognition accuracy than the full spectrum segment modeling when used for the prevention of transmission corridor tree barriers.

articleTitle: Failure analysis for water-blocking cushion layer erosion of HV XLPE cable
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Recently, erosion failures of the water-blocking cushion layer of HV XLPE cables occur frequently, which have attracted widespread attention in the power cable research field. This paper firstly summarizes the development history of high voltage cable cushion layer structure in china. Secondly, Fault statistics and analysis of cushion layer erosion of high voltage cable were analysed. Thirdly, the white powder produced by erosion was analyzed by physical and chemical analysis methods such as scanning electron spectroscopy and infrared spectroscopy. At last, this paper proposed some suggestions on inspection and production control of cable cushion layer of HV XLPE cable, expecting to strengthen the control of production links and reduce the failure rate.

articleTitle: Research on bus electrodynamic force of 750KV Micro-loss economical fault current limiter under power frequency short-circuit
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The short-circuit current will bring serious threat to the security and stability of power systems. Under the action of first half wave of short-circuit current, the electrodynamic force analysis of the bus is an important issue in its design and manufacture. In this paper, the finite element method is used to study the electrodynamic force of bus in the first half wave of short circuit current. Firstly, the domain decomposition method is used in the simulation, and the whole calculation area is partitioned into blocks. Different grid methods are used to improve the efficiency of finite element calculation. And we can obtain the distribution of the magnetic field of the flexible bus and hard bus under the first half wave of short-circuit current. And then, the electrodynamic force of the bus can be further calculated by using the calculated magnetic field. Finally, according to the electrodynamic force on the bus, the maximum stress and displacement of the bus are analyzed. Also, the variation characteristics of stress and displacement under different support numbers are discussed. The research results of this paper will provide an important theoretic and practical value for the design and manufacture of 750 kV economical fault current limiter.

articleTitle: Simulation of electrical performance of algae contaminated insulator
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In overhead transmission lines, in order to ensure the safety and reliability of power transmission, insulators are often used as insulating devices. In the outdoor environment, the surface of the insulator is often covered with a layer of green algae, which may affect the pollution flashover protection of the composite insulator. Therefore, in order to intuitively understand the influence of green algae on the external insulation characteristics of RTV-coated porcelain insulators, this paper will use the finite element method, using COMSOL software and AUTOCAD 2019 software to analyze 110kV RTV-coated porcelain simulation analysis of the insulator. The influencing factors considered in this paper include the environment where the green algae is located and where the green algae grows. The simulation results show that: when clean and dry, the surface electric field of the composite insulator presents a U-shaped distribution, and the electric field strength is the largest at the junction of the fittings and the silicone rubber material; when the green algae is in a humid environment, the influence of the external insulation is much greater than that of the green algae. The condition under dry conditions; whether it is dry or humid conditions, when the green algae grows on the lower surface, the influence of the external insulation of the green algae is much greater than when the green alga grows on the upper surface; the wet green algae grows on the lower surface. At the time, the impact on external insulation is the greatest and the most dangerous; there will be a local high point of electric field strength at the boundary between green algae and silicone rubber material; whether it is wet or dry conditions, the impact of green algae on the first insulator at the end of the insulator is significant.

articleTitle: Active power control strategy depending on frequency for MMC-HVDC system connected to offshore windfarms
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The study proposes an active power control strategy of the modular multilevel converter (MMC) for connecting large offshore windfarms. The strategy can be used to enhance the frequency stability of onshore alternating current (AC) system. It considers the working principle of windfarms, and can tightly control the output of active power of offshore network, which contributes to onshore frequency regulation by a changeable transmission of the offshore wind energy. The dynamic performance of the High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) based on MMC system using the proposed methods has been verified by PSCAD/EMTDC simulations. In different scenarios, the HVDC system can adjust active power accurately depending on the onshore frequency which confirms the feasibility of the methods.

articleTitle: Breakdown characteristics and synergistic effects of eco-friendly hydrofluorocarbon gases for replacement of SF6
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Sulfur hexafluoride gas is widely used in electric system due to its excellent insulation properties, but its greenhouse effect is 23,500 times greater than that of CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. Now the eco-friendly gases for replacing SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> are needed in electric industry. Hydrofluorocarbon gases have been widely used in production and living. Among them, HFC-32, HFC-125, HFC-134a, HFC-227ea, HFO-1234yf and HFC-410a gases have low GWP. The fluorine atoms in gases result in strong electronegativity and good insulation properties. Based on the calculated saturated vapor pressure characteristics, the DC breakdown voltages of the six gases and their mixtures with CO2, N2 and synthetic air were measured under extremely inhomogeneous electric fields, and the synergistic effect coefficients were calculated. The breakdown voltages of pure HFC-227ea and HFO-1234yf could reach that of pure SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas, and more than half of SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> after mixing with buffer gases. The breakdown stability and self-recovery characteristics were good. The calculation showed that all target gases had positive synergistic effect with buffer gases. Hydrofluorocarbon gases, especially HFC-227ea and HFO-1234yf, have the potential as eco-friendly insulating alternative gases, but it is necessary to find some buffer gases with better synergistic effect in order to obtain higher dielectric strength and wider application range.

articleTitle: The influence of adjacent lines on the surface electric field of outage maintenance personnel
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In this paper, the induced electric field generated by the adjacent ±800 kV UHV line on the body surface of ±1100 kV DC transmission line operators in outage maintenance is studied. The distribution characteristics of the electric field on the body surface of line maintenance personnel are obtained based on the upflow finite element method. The distribution of electric field on the human body surface at five typical operation locations commonly used for line maintenance is simulated and measured on site. The simulation results show that when ±1100 kV line is shut down for maintenance, no matter where the working location is, the induced electric field on the operator's body surface caused by adjacent UHV line is generally small, and the electric field at the tip of human body is too large. The maximum is no more than 13 kV/m, and the field strength of smooth parts such as the trunk is very small. The electric field on the body surface decreases with the increase of line spacing, and the decline rate of the tip of the body is less than that of the smooth part. The field measured data verify the reliability of the simulation results.

articleTitle: The temperature distribution analysis of 220Kv gis with different structure
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Gas insulated switchgear (GIS) is widely used in power grid. GIS has big current through busbar in its operation and it will lead to high temperature distribution in busbar and enclosure. It is very important to get the temperature difference between busbar and enclosure under different influence factors. The 220kV GIS simulation model with line, T and L structure are created in this paper and the temperature distribution are studied. The simulation results show the temperature of the top part is relatively higher for the influence of SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas, the closer to the outside, the lower the temperature, and the greater the temperature gradient near the busbar. For L structure GIS, the lowest value of temperature appears at the L-shaped corner. The L-shaped structure has a relatively larger space at the corners, and the current density is not uniformly distributed. The larger space brings more space for heat dissipation. For T-shaped structure, the temperature of the top part of the T-shaped branch part is lower than that of the bottom. This is due to the fact that the main busbar is divided into two branches in the bottom structure, and the current at the junction is still very large. The heat is much larger than a single busbar, so even if the SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas transfers heat, the top temperature is still lower than the bottom. The influence of environment temperature and wind speed are studied in this paper. The results show the ambient temperature has basically no effect on temperature rise. The wind speed has great influence to the temperature distribution, the wind can take out the heat and make the temperature decrease.

articleTitle: Experimental research on erosion detection method of high voltage cable cushion layer
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: At present, cases of cushion layer erosion failures in high-voltage XLPE insulated cables are not uncommon, but there are few corresponding successful cases and documents in the detection and evaluation of cushion layer erosion defects. The existing fault case analysis results show that there may be partial discharge, contact resistance increase, capacitive current concentration, local overheating and erosion during the development of defects, which can cause damage to the semi-conductivity and even the main insulation, and ultimately lead to breakdown. For defective cables, this article introduces the use of partial discharge, X-ray, broadband dielectric spectroscopy and other methods to carry out inspections, explore effective detection methods after the cushion layer has defects, and carry out actual testing on the spot to evaluate the operating status of the cable.

articleTitle: Influence of crosslinked behavior on the dielectric properties of XLPE/OMMT nanocomposite dielectric
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In order to investigate the influence of crosslinked behavior on the dielectric properties of polyethylene-matrix/layered silicate nanocomposite dielectrics, polyethylene/organic montmorillonite (PE/OMMT) and crosslinked polyethylene/organic montmorillonite (XLPE/OMMT) nanocomposite dielectrics were prepared by a melting blending method respectively, and the dielectric spectrum tests was used. It is found that the dielectric constant of the nanocomposites decreases with the increase of frequency. Its numerical value is closely related to the dispersion state of OMMT in matrix. At the same OMMT content, the dielectric constant of XLPE/OMMT composites after crosslinking is higher than that of the PE/OMMT nanocomposites. Because the crosslinked process affects the dispersion of OMMT in the matrix, the dielectric loss peak changes from unimodal to bimodal after crosslinking, and its peak value becomes bigger. As the temperature rises, the peak width of the double-peaks increases and the relaxation time distribution widens, so that the low-frequency peaks disperse in the low frequency and the high-frequency peaks move to a higher frequency. The increase of OMMT content and the crosslinked process together lead to the change of the dispersion state of OMMT in the matrix. The dielectric spectrum and thermogram change obviously due to the interface polarization and the loss of diversified groups.

articleTitle: Simulation and analysis of polypropylene dielectric constant based on molecular simulation method
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: As an important parameter reflecting the macroscopic dielectric properties of polymer materials, the dielectric constant is determined by the size and mode of the interaction between molecules and atoms, and the microscopic morphology of polymer chains, in particular, the structure and energy distribution between the chains is the key to determine the intermolecular interaction. In this paper, the simulation model of long chain structure of isotactic polypropylene is established by using simulation software, the steady state conformation of the molecule is calculated according to the principle of minimum energy, and the structure of the molecule is optimized by using force field, calculation of the permittivity of polypropylene based on Clausius-Mossotti equation. The results show that the dielectric constant of PP is 2.42, and that of industrial PP is 2.20-2.38(mean value is 2.25) . The calculated results are close to the experimental values, and the accuracy of the simulation model is 92.4%. The relationship between the micro-chain morphology and the macro-dielectric properties of polypropylene is established, which provides reference value for the chemical modification of polypropylene.

articleTitle: Adsorption properties of SO2F2 on α-Al2O3(0 0 0 1) surface: a dft study
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: With the purpose of ensuring the safe operation of SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas-insulated equipment, SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> molecular sieve adsorbent is used frequently to adsorb trace moisture and partial discharge decomposition components such as SO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> in the equipment. In this paper, the adsorption properties of SO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> on α-Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>(0 0 0 1) surface, the main component of SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> molecular sieve adsorbent, were investigated, including adsorption enthalpy change, adsorption distance, density of states (DOS), and frontier molecular orbitals theory. According to the study mentioned above, it is found that the molecular structure of the adsorbed gas has no obvious change, besides, the adsorption enthalpy change and charge transfer amount of the whole system are small. Furthermore, based on the frontier molecular orbital theory and the analysis of DOS, it is concluded that there is no obvious change in the energy gap of the system after adsorption, which further confirms that the physical adsorption of SO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> on the surface of SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> molecular sieve adsorbent is dominant. This study enhances the basic understanding of the interaction between SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> typical decomposition gas and SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> molecular sieve adsorbent and provides a theoretical basis for the adsorption of SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> typical decomposition gas on SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> molecular sieve adsorbent.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the grounding system of the high voltage laboratory: Case study
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The grounding system is essential for the reliable and safe operation of a network or electrical installation. Characteristics of a reliable grounding system must include low resistance in low frequency tests and low potential increase in high frequency tests. Besides that, the correct dimensioning and choice of the grounding elements must consider aspects such as intensity, frequency and type of faults or failures that may occur in the electrical installation. In the case of high voltage electrical test laboratories, the grounding project must also consider other aspects such as the interference between tests areas, the flow of disruptive discharges and high frequency response. An evaluation of the grounding system of LAT-EFEI was carried out, and to check the high frequency grounding, a current generator was used to inject high intensity impulsive current on the grounding point. This method allowed the evaluation of the voltage rise on the grounding point as though as its distribution over the grounding mesh. From the measurement data, impedance in the frequency domain was analyzed by through the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). Obtained results allow the identification of risks for equipment integrity, human safety, and measurements accuracy.

articleTitle: On-site partial discharge diagnosis and location of high voltage power apparatuses and case study
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: When a partial discharge (PD) liked discharge signal of high voltage power apparatuses is found, on-site PD diagnosis and location is difficult due to the complicated operating environment. In this paper, a novel diagnosis and location method for suspected PD signals of high-voltage power apparatuses is proposed, including comparison of PRPD, discharge source location and offline test verification. The suspected PD signal of a 35kV high voltage power apparatus is taken as a research case, and the diagnosis and positioning results are performed according to the proposed method. The results show that, through this process, the suspected PD signal can be effectively diagnosed and located, which provides a basis for the outage maintenance of the high voltage power apparatus.

articleTitle: The influence of temperature on surface discharge characters of oil-pressborad insulation
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Surface discharge is one of the most dangerous issues to oil-pressboard insulation inside power transformers, it might cause catastrophic flashover especially under high temperatures. In this paper, a needle-plate test model and a standard test circuit were designed to generate surface damage to oil-pressboard system. The research analyzes the development processes of surface damage and phase resolved partial discharge (PRPD) pattern from the beginning to the final flashover with the help of a high-speed camera and a discharge detecting system, to find the similarity and difference of surface discharge characters under different temperatures. The research found surface discharge generated more damage to the pressboard surface layer under high temperatures.

articleTitle: Finite element analysis of electrical stresses in the insulation system of rotating machines fed by static converters
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Nowadays, thanks to the recent advances in semiconductor technology, variable frequency drives (VFD) can be implemented in high voltage rotating machines. However, such applications require new considerations both in design as well as manufacturing processes of insulation systems, in particular as to the stator winding. In practice, due to practical problems in electric field sensors, the addressed new electrical stresses can only be measured as for the tangential electric field component over a surface of the insulation system. Finite element methods (FEM) entitle manufacturer to have an accurate estimation of electric fields at arbitrary regions of a defined geometry. In this contribution, three dimensional models of stator winding including both roebel bar and multi-turn coil are developed to highlight the major differences of electric field distribution between two cases of a conventional power frequency supply and a converter-fed supply on the insulation system.

articleTitle: Prequalification of capacitors for high-precision voltage dividers
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: To ensure long-term stability, it is very important to prequalify capacitors used in high-precision voltage dividers. This paper analyzes how film and foil capacitors change due to charge and discharge cycles under different test conditions. The presented experiments aimed at simulating the electric stress associated with high voltage tests in a laboratory. The test procedure considers parameters like magnitude of test voltage, number of impulses, series resistor, test circuit geometry, cooling, selfheating, and temperature. The results indicate that with a variation of up to 500 ppm the change of capacitance caused by repetitive impulse stress can be significant. However, this effect will be smaller when there is natural cooling between test cycles. In this case, the best-suited capacitors showed a variation of less than 200 ppm. In addition, the comparison of different tests shows that the temperature coefficient plays a significant role in the change of capacitance. During the whole test, some of the capacitors show non-recoverable damage. The prequalification testing identified a suitable type of capacitor, which will be used for the realization of a high-precision RCR divider in the European research project “HV-com<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>”.

articleTitle: F-P ultrasonic sensor based on four-cantilever beam-supported structure
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Based on the principle of F-P (Fabry-Perot) interference, this paper designs an optical fiber F-P sensor with a four-cantilever beam-supported structure with a square diaphragm in the center, which improves the detection sensitivity of the partial discharge in Gas insulated switchgear (GIS), ensures the consistency of the insulation medium inside and outside the sensor and eliminates the influence of temperature changes on the sensor. Based on COMSOL, this paper analyzes the influence of the side length of the square diaphragm on the first-order natural frequency and static pressure sensitivity of the four-cantilever beam-supported structure. Through simulation, this paper selects the optimal size parameters to design the four-cantilever beam-supported structure with the first-order natural frequency of 26216Hz. Based on the optical detection platform, this paper uses Electric ignition to simulate partial discharge ultrasonic signals in the air. The measured first-order natural frequency of the sensor is 23709 Hz. This sensor can accurately detect the partial discharge in GIS.

articleTitle: Research on electromagnetic transient response of photovoltaic system when lightning strikes the earth
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
