abstract: Two kinds of fiber Bragg grating sensitizing structures are proposed and packaged to fabricate partial discharge ultrasonic sensors. The sensitizing structures are numerically simulated and optimized. On this basis, the partial discharge detection platform is used to test the ability of the fiber Bragg grating ultrasonic sensor after sensitization, and the response characteristics of the sensor before and after sensitization are compared. The results show that the ultrasonic sensor based on diaphragm type and coupling cone type can effectively detect the ultrasonic generated by partial discharge. The former has a long response time to partial discharge, and the signal is easy to capture. The latter has a short response time, strong response characteristics, and high sensitivity. The whole sensor adopts non-metal package. The sensor has little interference with the electric field. The designed ultrasonic sensor has the advantages of high measurement sensitivity, flexible and adjustable layout, and can be reused. It is an on-line detection sensor for built-in insulation equipment with good prospects.

articleTitle: Study on dispersion characteristics of epoxy resin nanocomposites at Terahertz range
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In this paper, we prepared three kinds of nanocomposites based on epoxy resin. They are epoxy resin/silicon dioxide, epoxy resin/silicon carbide and epoxy resin/zinc oxide, respectively. By employing terahertz time-domain spectroscopy, we investigate their dispersion characteristics at terahertz range. We fitted the results by Lorentz harmonic oscillator model. The obtained optical dielectric constants of EP/SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, EP/SiC and EP/ZnO nanocomposites increase monotonously with the filler content increaseing. The damping coefficients of EP/SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and EP/SiC nanocomposites increase first and then decrease with the increase of filler content, while that of EP/ZnO nanocomposite decreases monotonously. We speculate that the increase of the damping coefficient result from the restriction of the interfacial region on the molecular chain motion. When the filler content is larger than 5%, the damping coefficient decreases significantly due to the agglomeration of nanoparticles and overlap of interfacial regions. There is no interaction region between the ZnO nanoparticles and epoxy resin, resulting in that the structure of epoxy resin becomes loose with the incorporation of ZnO nanoparticle. These results show that the damping coefficient can be employed as a typical parameter to characterize the strength of the interfacial region.

articleTitle: A semi-resolved algorithm for euler-lagrangian model of charged particulate flows under slightly non-unifomed electrical field
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Based upon coupling the finite volume method and discrete element method, an insight which could compute the charged particles' motion, the change of flow field and distortion of external electrical at the same time has been proposed. In order to further improve the computational efficiency and accuracy, a semi-resolved strategy was employed as well, which deals with the meshes a Lagrangian particle occupied larger than 80%. This work provides a new idea for resolving the four-way coupled computational question of the charged particulate flows modelled by Euler-Lagrangian method. This algorithm is also immensely helpful in the analysis of the particulate movements in electrostatic precipitation and gas insulated switchgear.

articleTitle: Simulation methodology for HVDC cable accessories: focus on oscillating polarity reversal and temporary overvoltages
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: HVDC cables and cable accessories play a fundamental role within the spreading of the HVDC transmission technologies. Depending on the transmission topology of the HVDC network, the overvoltage during fault can have different shapes and amplitudes, including oscillating polarity reversal (OPR) and temporary overvoltages (TOV). Due to the reversed polarity and space charge accumulation inside insulating materials the electric field can significantly increase and might lead to failure of the insulation. The knowledge of the electric field under those type of stresses is thus mandatory to ensure a reliable design. Time dependent simulations are essential to determine the electric field distribution and they became more complicated in the case of OPR and superimposed impulse voltage (S/IMP). The aim of this paper is to propose a time decoupled simulation method to compute the electric field in case of OPR and S/IMP without losing in result accuracy. The proposed simulation method, applied in a fluid-filled cable/Gas Insulated Switchgear (GIS) termination, shows that OPR can be very critical for this accessory and might not be covered by standard tests. The results show that, due to space and surface charges accumulation, the maximum stress could occur after the first peak of the OPR.

articleTitle: Study of vacuum thermal aging on the mechanical and dielectric properties of liquid silicone rubber
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Liquid silicone rubber (LSR) is widely used in the cable joints, and the stability of which is key to the safe of cables. In the present study we performed a series of vacuum thermal ageing tests on LSR at the temperature of 80°C, 100°C and 120°C for 1000h, to investigate the ageing mechanism. The mechanical properties of the samples were studied by tensile test and Dynamic Mechanical Analysis (DMA) test, while the dielectric properties were measured by the broadband dielectric spectroscopy (BDS) and the Terahertz time-domain spectra (THz-TDS). Combining with the microstructure observation and the cross-linking density measurement, results were obtained that the vacuum thermal condition impacted on the mechanical and dielectric properties of LSR by causing the molecules motion and cross-linking. When the aging temperature is 80°C, the destruction of the original cross-linking points caused by the heat led the elongation at break and the permittivity increased. However, when the aging temperature was higher, except for the precipitation, the Si-OH on the nano SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> formed hydrogen bond with the main chains, making the cross-linking density higher, causing the elongation at break and the glass transition temperature increased while the permittivity decreased and the loss peak of steering polarization disappeared.

articleTitle: Investigation on enhancement of flashover voltage of high temperature vulcanized silicone rubber by micron composite coating
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: High temperature vulcanized silicone rubber (HTV) is one of the most extensively used insulating polymers in power transmission cables (including its accessories) due to its preferable dielectric properties. However, complex of environmental conditions during its service time could lead to its dielectric degradation and then results in its dielectric failure, which would endanger the safety of power grid operation. Therefore, it is crucial to improve the flashover voltage of HTV for its better performance in insulating cables. In this research, room temperature vulcanized silicone rubber (RTV-II) doped with micron BN was prepared using constant temperature magnetic stirring approach and the HTV was then modified by these prepared micron coatings in order to improve its dielectric properties. The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) test showed that the micron-BN in RTV-II matrix was evenly distributed, then, the test results show that HTV films with micron-BN RTV-II coating has better qualities of dielectric and corrosion resistance compared with raw HTV film. Furthermore, find BN micron coating films with different proportions of micron fillers that improves the electrical properties of the composite the most. The addition of micron BN decreased the BN/HTV relative permittivity and increased its flashover voltage. When the micron BN particle size was 1 μm and the mass fraction was 5%, the micron BN had better dispersion in the matrix material, flashover voltage reaches the highest and the dielectric constant was relatively low.

articleTitle: Cost-effective lightning protection of high-performance photovoltaic power plants
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Renewable energy sources, such as photovoltaic power plants, are an increasing part of the power system. Consequently, the chance of losing these power plants during a thunderstorm is growing and their loss leads to lower green energy share during appropriate circumstances, as well. This publication aims to present the design of primary lightning protection of photovoltaic systems, which has an important part in the protection of solar inverters and panels from overvoltage. The risk of lightning induced phenomena increases with greater and greater plant performance i.e., larger area, however considering plant arrangement and environmental factors a cost-efficient primary lightning protection can be realised for any installation. Incorrect solutions used to construct lightning protection system are presented. The article states that a lower lightning protection rating is sufficient, and primary lightning protection can be omitted in a lot of cases.

articleTitle: Effect of modified silicone rubber on discharge of SR/XLPE composite interface
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Cable accessories are the weak link in the operation of the entire cable system, and the SR/XLPE composite interface is most prone to accidents. In order to improve the electric field distribution near the interface, researchers usually modify the silicone rubber to improve its mechanical properties and nonlinear conductivity characteristics. In this paper, according to the theory of composite material percolation, the silicone rubber is modified, doped with different proportions of SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. Then the flashover characteristics of the composite interface and the mechanical properties of SR are measured. The results show that the modified silicone rubber has an impact on the insulation strength of the composite interface and can also enhance the mechanical strength of SR.

articleTitle: Application of SiC-Filled permittivity and conductivity graded material (ε/σ-FGM) in HVDC GIS spacer
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The size reduction of HVDC GIS is needed for reduction of SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas use. The challenge concerning the insulating material in HVDC GIS is to reduce the high electric field strength in gas around the solid insulators (spacers). Our previous works have shown the effectiveness of the functionally graded material (FGM) with graded permittivity (ε) and conductivity (σ) in controlling the high electric field strength under various DC operating conditions. However, ε/σ distributions were independent of each other. For practical implementation of FGM to HVDC GIS, the flexible mixture casting (FMC) method so far allows us to create a material whose ε/σ distributions are interdependent. In this paper, based on the measured dependence between ε and σ in SiC-filled epoxy composites, the electric field relaxation effect is evaluated under three different ε/σ distributions (U-type, grading-to-higher conductivity (GHC)-type and grading-to-lower conductivity (GLC)-type) applied to a 320 kV HVDC GIS spacer model. The results show that GLC-type ε/σ-FGM has effectively and constantly reduced the maximum electric field strength under the time-varying voltage application from DC-on to DC-steady state and against temperature differences between the high voltage and ground sides up to 70 K.

articleTitle: Inhibition of the space charge of LLDPE by crosslinking effect
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In this paper, the space charge behaviour of linear low density polyethylene (LLDPE) crosslinked polyethylene (XLPE) materials with different crosslinking degree is investigated by pulsed electro-acoustic (PEA) method. It is found that the distortion of the field strength is mitigated with the increase of the crosslinking degree. But the improvement of distortion is less obvious with the increase of the crosslinking degree when the crosslinking degree reaches 77% (1.4wt.% dicumyl peroxide (DCP)). The conductivity measurement is in accordance with this phenomenon by showing a decreasing trend in the conductivity of samples with the increase of DCP content in the range of 0wt.% to 2wt.% DCP content. Moreover, the crosslinking degree illustrates the mechanism of this phenomenon, for the rate of the increase of crosslinking degree decreases with the addition of DCP, and SEM observation implies an increase of the non-uniformity spherulites and amorphous region due to the crosslinking process. This study may help to understand more of the function of crosslinking and make better choice of the crosslinking degree of HVDC extruded cable insulation materials.

articleTitle: Design of a miniaturized bounded wave simulator for broadband and intensive electric fields
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The challenge of EMC test is the requirement of broadband and intensive electric fields and magnetic fields. Here, we design a miniaturized parallel plate bounded wave simulator. The overall size of the simulator is about 1300 mm × 300 mm × 100 mm. This bounded wave simulator has three working areas and is able to generate broadband and intensive electric fields. The electric fields in different areas connected by transition sections are in different field intensities. To optimize the electric-field distribution in a broad bandwidth, the distributed load is adopted to match the wave impedance, effectively limiting the waves generated by refraction and reflection. The design of the whole system is finally validated by the finite element simulation. In this bounded wave simulator, an up to 40 kV/cm uniform electric-field is realized, along with stable distribution in a broad bandwidth from 1kHz to 300 MHz. Therefore, it is an applicable and miniaturized simulator suitable for EMC test in academic and industrial fields.

articleTitle: Improved breakdown strength and energy density of all-organic polymer dielectrics at elevated temperature
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Polymer dielectrics with high breakdown strength and energy density at high temperature conditions are critical for film capacitors. In this work, all-organic composite films are prepared by thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) and poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) (P(VDF-HFP)), and the dielectric as well as energy storage properties at elevated temperature conditions are investigated. It is found that the dielectric constant and dielectric loss of TPU/P(VDF-HFP) decrease with the introduction of organic TPU filler. Due to the improved breakdown strength of 235 MV/m at elevated temperature, the TPU-1 vol%/P(VDF-HFP) composite film shows 82% higher discharged energy density compared with neat P(VDF-HFP). The low dielectric loss, high breakdown strength, high electrical resistant, high discharged energy density and charge-discharge efficiency of TPU/P(VDF-HFP) film make it potentially to be utilized in the field of high temperature capacitive energy storage applications.

articleTitle: Study on internal electric field distribution of on-load tap changer for converter transformer
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In this paper, the insulation of tap changer is checked by simulation calculation. Under normal working conditions such as normal loading interstage voltage or main insulation power frequency voltage, the insulation performance of tap changer can maintain a good safety boundary. However, relatively speaking, under the working condition of power frequency voltage of main insulation, it is close to the insulation withstand value of transformer oil. It is necessary to regularly sample and check the water content in tap changer transformer oil to ensure that it meets the safety requirements.

articleTitle: Study on external insulation durability test of composite cross arm insulator
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: It is of great significance to evaluate the external insulation durability of composite cross arm insulators because of their serious aging after long-term operation. In this paper, ultraviolet aging test, corona aging test and electrical erosion aging test of silicone rubber were carried out for the external insulation aging performance of composite cross arm insulators. The results show that the breakdown strength decreases from 23.2 kV/mm to 20.2 kV/mm after 3000 h UV aging test. The volume resistivity decreased from 5.6×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup> Ω•m to 1.7×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>Ω•m; The hydrophobic Angle decreased from 108° to 102°; Corona discharge aging will cause the fracture of silicon rubber molecular chain Si-CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, and local high temperature carbonization will occur, resulting in the serious loss of hydrophobicity of silicon rubber materials. The tracking wheel test has little effect on the mechanical properties of the silicone rubber skirt, but the electrical properties have obvious changes, in which the volume resistivity decreases by 2 orders of magnitude and the breakdown strength decreases by 18.5%. The results of this paper can provide a technical support for the evaluation of external insulation aging state of composite cross arm insulators.

articleTitle: Dielectric strength of environmental-friendly gas mixtures of C4H2F6/CO2 and C4H2F6/AIR
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas is widely used in electric power apparatus as an insulation and arc-quenching medium. However, SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas has a high greenhouse effect. There are many investigations focusing on searching for environmentally friendly insulation gases which can achieve equivalent insulation strength with SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>, meanwhile, reduce global warming potential (GWP) apparently. C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> is a novel, chemically stable, non-toxic and non-flammable gas which has a low GWP of 18, a zero Ozone Depletion Potential (ODP), a boiling point of 7.5℃ and a critical temperature of 137.7℃. In this paper, we set up an experiment platform to study the dielectric strength of C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>/CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>/Air under DC voltage. Experiments in the plate electrode were done in 5mm gap distances, different pressures and gas ratios of C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>/CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>/Air mixture gas. The results were also compared with SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> in the same conditions. The insulating properties will be used to evaluate the dielectric strength of C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>/CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>/Air gas mixture, providing significant fundamental data for its potential use in the medium voltage gas insulated switchgear cabinet.

articleTitle: Investigation on loss reduction strategies of single-core HVAC submarine cables
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Submarine cables play an important role in the cross-sea transmission system. However, the power loss in such systems should be reduced as it affects the service life and limits the ampacity of the submarine cables. This paper proposes an accurate methodology based on the multi-conductor analysis theory to investigate the loss reduction strategies of the single-core high voltage AC (HVAC) submarine cable. The coupled line model is used to improve the calculation efficiency. The case study of the 500-kV submarine cable line of Zhoushan 500 kV power transmission project is conducted. The results show that connecting resistors and reactors at the grounding ends of the cable sheath can significantly reduce power loss. The connection of reactors exhibits a higher reduction of power loss than the resistors.

articleTitle: Effect of soil discharge channels on cables under lightning strikes
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Soil discharge channels formed by high-amplitude impulse current have differing spatial structures that affect the interference on adjacent cables through alteration of the electromagnetic field. This work built a test and observation platform for the further study of the interference effect of soil discharge on a cable under an impulse current. Images of soil discharge channels were captured and the relative angle between the discharge channel and cable was extracted to reflect their relative position. A smaller relative angle corresponded with a closer relative position. Furthermore, measurements of the coupling current of the cable shielding and the grounding potential revealed that the discharge channel affects the local potential surrounding the cable. The test results show that a closer relative position results in larger in-soil local potential surrounding the cable, and the maximum amplitude of the surface potential of the cable differs by a factor of 1.33∼1.45 across different relative positions.

articleTitle: An algorithm for anomaly detection of on-line monitoring data of dissolved gas in transformer oil based on rule extraction
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The data collected by dissolved gas-in-oil analysis (DGA) online monitoring devices generally have inadequate quality because of the complex operating environment. In addition, no standard is available for unified standardization of the data. These issues considerably limit the effectiveness, accuracy, and timeliness of DGA. To improve the usability of the DGA online monitoring data, we propose an integrated set of rule-based methods for detecting anomalies in DGA online monitoring data. The method was tested by applying it to the DGA online monitoring data of a 220-kV transformer at a 220-kV substation.

articleTitle: A portable partial discharge locating tool for 10-kV covered conductor lines
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Partial discharge (PD) has been regard as one of the most valuable techniques for condition-based assessment and predictive maintenance of power apparatus. In this study, a portable double-sided PD detection and location method driven by a pulse-based interaction mechanism is presented to diagnose PD characteristics of 10-kV overhead covered conductor (CC) line. The pulse-based interaction mechanism is implemented by injecting specific high voltage pulses into the CC line and utilizing the CC line as the carrier of the pulses for the interaction between the double-sided testing units. The mechanism is capable of not only synchronizing the double-sided testing units, but also estimating the signal propagation velocity. This helps to eliminate the errors and inconsistency in determining PD source location that are caused by varying physical parameters of CC line that can change the propagation velocity. Based on the methodology, a practical portable PD locating system is implemented and validation experiment was carried out on a 2350-m CC line under operation. The results showed the proposed methodology and system could be effectively used to detect and locate the PDs on CC lines.

articleTitle: Acoustic method for identification and detection of free metal particles defects in GIS/GIL
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The presence of metal particles has brought immense threaten to the insulation of gas-insulated switchgear/gas-insulated transmission lines (GIS/GIL). The acoustic method as a non-invasive detection method has been dramatically focused. Existing detection methods ignored electric field force between neighbouring collisions or based on the acoustic amplitude-flight time pattern are not accurate and applicable for practical diagnosis. In this study, a new method of estimating particles' parameters by combing the applied voltage and collision signal has been proposed. The most crucial point of this method is to extract the particle collision signals at the zero crossings of the voltage phase from acoustic signals' raw data. A real-scale simulation model of GIS/GIL and an experimental platform was established to explain and testify the new detection method separately. The results of this method show immense robustness for predicting the properties of different geometric and material particles. This study provides a workable reference for GIS/GIL condition monitoring.

articleTitle: Influences of low temperature on luminous characteristics of positive streamer in air
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The constructing of Global Energy Interconnection will be expected to cross high latitude areas and work in extreme environments. In this study, a test chamber that can achieve a low temperature environment (173K-293K) is established, and a de-moisture system provides dry air to keep the chamber at a low humidity. A three-electrode arrangement is placed in the chamber to create a uniform field where the positive streamer propagates forward. For investigating, we use PMT and ICCD to detect pulse signals of UV-light and streamer morphologies. We characterize the streamer luminous intensity by the PSA and the OAD respectively, and results show that the streamer luminous intensity under initial field decreases linearly with the temperature falling, and the OAD appears a linear growth relation with the field rising at different temperatures, which is in-line with the streamer propagation theory. From images captured by ICCD, we also find that the streamer turns gloomier as the temperature falls. The conclusions manifest that there are less limitations when use the OAD to indicate the luminous intensity of streamer, and the low temperature decreases the space photoionization and inhibits the development of streamer.

articleTitle: Experimental research on the arcing characteristics of C4F7N/CO2 gas mixtures
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N-CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> mixed gas as the potential substitute for SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> has attracted more and more attention, so it is of great significance to study the arcing characteristics. In this paper, a set of experimental device was designed to study the arcing characteristics of 5%C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N/95%CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>sub> and 10%C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N/90%CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. The arc images are captured by high-speed camera to visualize the motion characteristics of arc breaking process, and compared with SF6 gas under the same charging current and gas pressure conditions. The experimental results shown that: with the increase of pressure, the arc voltage increases, which can promote the arc extinguishing performance; The arc conductance of SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas is the largest, and the fluctuation range of arc diameter of 10%C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N/90%CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> is relatively smaller, with the average diameter of 5.5mm; With the increase of C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N content, the arc stability is improved, the arc voltage and arc conductance are close to SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>, and the arc extinguishing ability is enhanced.

articleTitle: Measurement method for physical properties of an arc generates and propagates over an ice surface
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Physical characteristics of the discharge generates and propagates over an ice surface are essential for revealing the discharge mechanism and developing the physical model. This paper proposed a time-domain synchronous measurement method to obtain the thermal, spectrum and electrical characteristics during a DC arc that generates and propagates over an ice surface. The discharge channel model and plasma components model are established to analyse the channel's size and temperature. An improved quasi-Newton iteration algorithm is proposed to solve the deeply non-linear problem in calculating the plasma composition. The calculation results show that the proposed algorithm has a faster iteration and convergence speed than the traditional algorithms while guaranteeing calculation accuracy. The experimental results show that the proposed method can realize the synchronous measurement of the emission spectrum, gas temperature, discharge channel shape, geometry size, current, and voltage in the time domain at all discharge stages. The results can provide a reference for measuring the physical properties of gas discharge over the ice surface and the calculation of plasma temperature and components.

articleTitle: An improved method of thermal resistance calculation for the buffer layer in HV XLPE cables
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The buffer layer in high voltage (HV) cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) cable is a kind of spongy material, which can be regarded as a composite of fibre and still air. A constant value of thermal conductivity is recommended for this layer by IEC and CIGRE for the calculation of cable current rating, ignoring the change of compression ratio, which may lead to a noticeable deviation. In this paper, the relationship between the thermal conductivity of buffer layer and its compression ratio was established by laboratory measurement using the transient plane source method, which showed the increase of thermal conductivity along with the increased compression ratio. Then the thermal field distribution of a HV XLPE cable with smooth aluminum sheath was numerically studied, by considering thermal conductivity of the buffer layer under the actual compression ratio determined by the cable structure and thermal expansion of XLPE insulation. The rated current provided by this numerical model was in a better agreement with the experimental data, compared to the value calculated by IEC standards. Finally, based on the numerical research, some suggestions were put forward to improve the analytical algorithm for the thermal resistance of buffer layer during the determination of cable current rating.

articleTitle: Modeling of multilayer coated polyimide graphene nanocomposite films and thermal conductivity
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In this paper 3D model of multilayer Polyimide nanocomposite films is designed on the basis of actual boundary conditions obtained from SEM images of synthesized films. Here, using the binary fillers graphene oxide (GO) nanosheets and functionalized silica (SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) nanoparticles based composite films are fabricated. The impact of multilayer structure and nanoparticle dispersion on the thermal conductivity is explicitly studied in this study. The thermal conductivity of these synthesized multilayer PI/nanocomposite films are also measured through experimental results. The results expose that the chances of nanoparticles dispersion are improved by pasting a thin PI/nanocomposite layer on both sides of PI film as compared to the single layer of PI/nanocomposite film. In consequence, high thermal conductivity is achieved for two-layer PI/nanocomposite films. The proposed methods will help to reliably predict the material characterization for polymeric based nanocomposite films.

articleTitle: The electrical properties along the radial distribution of 500kV DC cable insulation
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The electrical properties along the radial distribution of 500kV dc cable insulation play an important role in cable design, especially for the cable and accessory matching. Here we investigate the conductivity space charge density and breakdown strength along the radial distribution. The conductivity for the middle portion is slightly higher compared with that for the middle and outer portion for the un-degassing HVDC cable. The space charge density under low electric field is obviously reduced, but the effect under high electric field is not obvious after 60 days of degassing. Breakdown strength increases and then decreases from the inner to outer portion. In general, the change of conductivity and breakdown strength along the radial distribution is not obvious. In contrast, the HVDC cable after degassing shows different trend. With the increase of degassing time from 0 to 1440 hours, the conductivity of the insulation gradually decreases from the inner to the outer portion along the radial direction. Breakdown field strength shows a trend of gradual increment from the inner portion to the outer portion.

articleTitle: Research on protection characteristics of ZnO arrester under very-fast-front impulse voltage
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The operation of the disconnector and electromagnetic pulse from nuclear HEMP could generate a very-fast-front impulse voltage on the power system. If the amplitude of this very-fast-front impulse voltage exceeds the tolerance of the power equipment, it will affect the normal operation of the power system. To study the protection characteristics of the ZnO arrester under the impulse voltage, a device that can generate this impulse voltage with a front time of less than 100 ns was designed and manufactured. Based on protection characteristics, the method of reducing the residual voltage by changing the external circuit structure of the arrester was researched. The results show that the protection characteristics of the ZnO arrester under very-fast-front impulse voltage are poor. The waveform of residual voltage has a large overshoot, and its amplitude can reach more than 3 times the voltage limit value. Besides, the ZnO arrester cannot respond to the pulse voltage whose pulse width is less than the operating time. When the LC filter structure is used, the overshoot amplitude and the reverse overshoot amplitude of the residual voltage waveform can be reduced. The gap structure in parallel can also reduce the voltage limit value of the residual voltage waveform.

articleTitle: Space charge distribution characteristics of polyimide (PI) films modified by nano-Al2O3/SiO2
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Polyimide (PI) film as a kind of insulating material with strong practicability and wide application, which is used in lots of fields. At present, the PI film is widely used in the insulation of the high temperature superconducting transformer. Its insulation performance is affected by the combined effect of overvoltage and high temperature, which has become increasingly unable to meet the requirements of the high temperature superconducting transformer. Many scholars have found that partial discharge and space charge are the main causes of insulation aging between turns of coils. Therefore, it is of great significance to study the space charge characteristics of PI films. In this paper, PI films modified by nano-Al2O3/SiO2 had been prepared, the pulsed electro-acoustic (PEA) method was used, and the distribution characteristics of space charge and electric field strength of the PI film samples modified by nano-Al2O3/SiO2 with different mass fractions were analyzed. The experimental results show that the nano-Al2O3/SiO2 in PI films can effectively suppress the space charge injection and accumulation behavior. The addition of nanoparticles can cause the traps content increase in PI films to form a stable electric field, which improves the dielectric properties.

articleTitle: Intelligent recognition of insulator video stream based on embedded edge computing
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Traditional intelligent recognition algorithm models of insulators are large and mostly completed by back-end servers, with large data transmission volume, high power consumption and poor real-time performance at the front and rear ends. In this paper, a miniature SSD convolutional neural network model is designed to enable it to be deployed in embedded edge computing devices and to recognize video images of insulators. Firstly, the low-latitude Core convolution group subnetwork is used to replace the high-latitude VGG network to extract the shallow features of the insulator, and then the auxiliary feature extraction subnetwork is used to predict the target, so as to reduce the number of model parameters. The model weight files generated by the training were transplanted to the edge computing platform of Jetson nano equipped with vision sensor. OpenCV was used to extract frames from the video images captured by vision sensor every 1 ms and real-time recognition performance was compared under different video resolutions. Experimental results show that the scheme reduces data transmission and realizes low delay recognition. The average recognition frame rate of insulator video images is 16.8 FPS and 19.7 FPS respectively at 1280*720 and 640*480 resolutions. The recognition process is relatively smooth and the recognition accuracy can reach 91.53%. The energy consumption of the whole identification process is less than 5W, which is an order of magnitude lower than that of traditional servers.

articleTitle: Study of hierarchical support technique for managing assets - development of support program for substation equipment
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Recently, the electric power industry has been facing of difficult problems, such as strong social request of cost cutting and the aging of facilities. Advanced diagnostic techniques are expected to rationalize and improve the operation and maintenance of electric power equipment, but their performance should be evaluated by some objective methods. The “asset management” or “managing assets” technique has been expected to support the rationalization of the maintenance and operation of electric power equipment, and the accountability of these activities. CRIEPI has been examining its introduction in Japan for more than 15 years. It has become apparent that actual maintenance-related data should be collected, and concrete evaluation should be carried out using these data, because individual situations generally differ depending on the equipment used and sometimes on the utility. For examination by the staff of each utility company, concrete support programs have been developed by considering the lifecycle cost for substation equipment (oil-immersed transformers, gas circuit breakers (GCB) and gas insulated switchgears (GIS)). In this paper, these support programs are presented and a trial study of hierarchical managing assets evaluation is carried out.

articleTitle: Research on “8”-shaped magnetic core current transformer based on magnetic field cancellation
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In the AC transmission and distribution network, electromagnetic current transformers are still the main solution for electric energy measurement due to their high measurement accuracy and strong anti-interference. This article uses a special structure of the “8” shape structure magnetic core and realizes the magnetic field cancellation by shunting the primary current, so as to achieve the purpose of extending the current measurement range without increasing the number of secondary winding turns and ensuring the measurement accuracy. In turn, the theoretical analysis and three-dimensional finite element simulation analysis of the current transformer are carried out. Finally, using the existing conditions, a prototype of a “8” shaped magnetic core current transformer was made, and a corresponding test platform was constructed to test the prototype using the equal ampere-turn method. The three-dimensional finite element simulation results and the test results show that the “8”-shaped structure core current transformer and the double-sided primary current with a suitable primary current ratio coefficient can achieve the purpose of extending the measurement range while ensuring the accuracy of the measurement. The measuring range expansion multiple is inversely proportional to the primary current ratio coefficient.

articleTitle: Measurement and analysis of partial discharge of bubble defects in GIS basin insulator
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: According to the actual size of the basin insulator, a three-dimensional simulation model is established. The electric field distribution rule of the defect-free basin insulator under the rated voltage is calculated. The influence of bubble defects at different positions and different volumes on the electric field distribution of the basin insulator is analysed. In addition, the experimental tooling is designed and the experimental platform is built in combination with the actual operating environment. Under the standard test voltage, the parallel circuit measurement method of pulse current method is used to detect the partial discharge signal of the tested basin insulator. the initial partial discharge voltage, the initial discharge quantity and the discharge signal waveforms of different volume bubble defect samples are measured. the influence of different volume bubble defects on the partial discharge characteristics of the basin insulator is analysed; the process of discharge development is investigated; the variation rule of bubble discharge under different field intensity is summarized, and the discharge rule of bubble defects with different volume inside the insulation is obtained by processing the raw data obtained from different experimental models.

articleTitle: Distributed temperature sensing for ultra-high voltage GIL spacer based on improved optical frequency domain reflectometer
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Spacers are the core component of Gas insulated transmission lines (GIL), which plays a vital role in isolating the gas chamber and supporting the high-voltage conductor. The temperature distribution of spacers affects the charge accumulation and mechanical properties, which are directly related to the insulation performance of the GIL. In order to obtain the temperature distribution of GIL spacers directly and accurately, a distributed temperature sensing method based on improved optical frequency domain reflectometer (OFDR) was proposed. Firstly, the sensing principle of OFDR was introduced, and the method to deal with the nonlinear sweeping effect of the light source was proposed. Then, according to the principle of OFDR, the method of realizing distributed temperature sensing for GIL spacer was given. Furthermore, a temperature-rise test platform based on real ultra-high voltage (UHV) GIL was built, and the actual temperature distribution of a 1000 kV GIL spacer during the heating process was obtained.

articleTitle: Measurement of electric field distribution in 2μm thick Polyethylene naphthalate film
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Thin dielectric films become popular in electrical engineering for their high electric field endurance. However, operating in a high electric field is prone to accumulate space charges inside the polymer dielectric film, which will distort the internal electric field and affect the film working reliability. In this paper, we first attempt to study the space charge behavior in 2-micron thick PEN films by thermal pulse method. The PEN films were subjected to DC high voltage electric field at different ambient temperatures. The electric field changes in the films were continuously monitored. The experimental results show that thermal pulse method is successfully utilized to detect the evolution of electric field in the 2-micron thick PEN films. Under high DC electric field, the change of electric field distribution in PEN film is very sensitive to the experimental temperature, which is characterized by obvious space charge injection at slightly elevated temperature. The results also show high spatial resolution of thermal pulse method, which is considered to be suitable for the measurement for thinner film with thickness less than 1 micron.

articleTitle: The voltage endurance characteristics of HVDC cable insulation slices
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The direct current (DC) voltage endurance coefficient n is used to represent the DC voltage endurance characteristic of insulating materials, which is important in structural design and test assessment of DC cable. However, the research on n of HVDC crosslinked polyethylene (XLPE) cable insulation slices at 90℃ is rare, and there is a lack of long-term test data to support the design of HVDC cable working at 90℃. Therefore, the actual measurement of DC voltage endurance characteristics of XLPE at 90℃ is of great significance. In this paper, the DC voltage endurance characteristics of XLPE insulation slices from the HVDC cable at 90℃ are studied. The DC breakdown field strength of XLPE samples at 90℃ is obtained by continuous boosting method, and the endurance voltage tests are carried out at 10 different electric strength levels respectively. The result shows that the E-t characteristic curve of XLPE slices is approximately linear in domain I and n=7.34, while the curve tends to become horizontal in domain II and the electrical threshold stress is 95 kV/mm. The electrical aging might be negligible for the HVDC cable working at 90 ℃ in the long-term operation.

articleTitle: Insulation characteristics of quasi-uniform electric field and effect of metallic particle contamination in highly compressed dry air
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Global warming due to greenhouse gases has resulted in an increased effort worldwide to reduce their emission. An alternative gas to SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> is now in great demand, and dry air has attracted interest as an efficient solution to reduce the environmental impact. This paper describes the fundamental insulation characteristics of dry air. First, the breakdown voltages at lightning impulse (LI) and the AC voltages under a quasi-uniform electric field in dry air using an actual sized bus were measured. In the highly compressed dry air, it was found that positive LI breakdown voltage was lower than that of negative LI. Second, the dielectric performance under metallic particle contamination was investigated by observing the free particle motion at AC voltage and measuring the AC breakdown voltage under the condition of free metallic particle crossing. The LI flashover voltage of an insulator with a particle attached to its surface was also measured. It became evident that the breakdown voltages initiated by free particles in dry air were lower than those under the clean condition. Moreover, the dielectric coating on the inner enclosure surface was an effective measure against the particle motion.

articleTitle: Application and research of resistive superconducting fault current limiter in 60kV HVDC system
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In recent years, flexible DC transmission technology has developed rapidly and matured in the industry, but it has brought about unavoidable problems: once a short circuit or other fault occurs in the high voltage DC transmission system, the rapid increase in fault current will cause irreversibility to the power grids damage. Aiming at the problems of rapid rise of fault short-circuit current and high peak current in the existing HVDC system, a resistive superconducting fault current limiter (RSFCL) model was built, which takes advantage of the quench characteristics of the second generation high temperature superconducting tape YBCO. This article introduces the working principle and working status of RSFCL in detail, uses PSCAD/EMTDC software to adopt new numerical modelling of RSFCL, applies it to 60kV high voltage direct current system, and verifies its correctness through a series of simulation experiments. The simulation results show that RSFCL will quench in a very short time and form a high resistance state. The larger the quench resistance value, the more obvious the current limiting effect. The final quench resistance value of 20Ω is the ideal choice for this article, but at the same time the quench process will cause the temperature of the superconducting strip to rise sharply, requiring additional auxiliary cooling equipment. The simulation results verify that the proposed RSFCL has an obvious role in limiting the rise rate and peak value of the fault short-circuit current.

articleTitle: Test and operation analysis of natural ester retrofilled 110kV mobile transformer
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The power industries of China have been growing rapidly for more than 40 years, and now the electricity consumption and power grid size of China tops the world. A sizable fleet of transformers are left idle because they lack the appropriate unit MVA due to the speedy growth on power needs, for example, fully functional 25∼40MVA power transformers are replaced by new 50~80MVA units. To optimize asset management, utilities are seeking ways to reuse the idle transformers, as the journey of CSG (China Southern Power Grid) to retrofill 110kV mineral oil transformers started in 2019. This mineral oil filled 40MVA unit was made in 1993 and deenergized in 2013, retrofilled on site with FR3® Fluid in April 2019. It is assembled on a skid and serves as a mobile substation. Due to transportation limits, bushings, turrets, radiators, and conservator need to be removed and reassembled when changing service site. The feasibility evaluation and operational steps, transformer handover dielectric test results comparison before and after retrofilling, oil tests with DGA history of two servicing cycles are also briefed and discussed in this paper. The drying effect of natural ester to the aged transformer solid insulation is confirmed based on the operational data analysis.

articleTitle: A correction model of furfural loss in transformer oil under partial oil change
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Oil change as an oil treatment method can improve the performance of transformer oil. However, oil change leads to loss of furfural in oil, which will affect the results of insulation aging assessment. Existing studies only focus on the effect of total oil change on furfural loss, while partial oil change is neglected. In actual situations, total oil change treatment of the transformer is quite expensive, partial oil change is more practical. In view of this, a correction model of furfural loss under partial oil change was studied in this work. Firstly, accelerated thermal aging and partial oil change experiments were performed on oil-paper insulations. Secondly, the influence of partial oil change on furfural loss in oil was analyzed, and the furfural correction model was established. Finally, the furfural correction model was verified by newly prepared samples, and the average error of the corrected results was within 12%. In that respect, this work reports a correction model of furfural loss under partial oil change, which aims to provide a theoretical basis for the paper insulation aging evaluation under partial oil change.

articleTitle: Discussion on pollution accumulation characteristics of insulator on top of EMU based on multi field coupling
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In the entire power supply traction system, the roof insulator of the EMU has the function of isolating related equipment, supporting the pantograph, busbar and other high-voltage equipment, which is very important to the stable operation of the EMU.This article is based on the fluid flow tracking model and the turbulence model in the flow field, combined with the actual situation, establishes a two-dimensional model of the insulator in CAD and imports it into the Solidworks software to build a three-dimensional. Use COMSOL Multiphysics finite element software to explore the pollution particle deposition of the top insulation of high-speed and low-speed airflow environment.The research results show that the amount of contamination on the roof insulators increases with the increase of the flow rate and the growth rate gradually slows down. When the angle of the incoming flow is less than 45°, the amount of dirt accumulation decreases with the increase of the angle, and when the angle is greater than 45°, the amount of dirt accumulation decreases greatly and tends to be gentle. At low speed, with the increase of AC voltage level, the electric field force will make the surface pollution of insulator increase first and then decrease, but the effect is very small in one cycle. This research provides a basis for reducing the flashover phenomenon of insulators, improving the anti-pollution work of insulators, and ensuring the safe operation of EMUs.

articleTitle: How conductance characteristics of nonlinear materials influences the performance of field grading in needle plate model
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The local intensified electric field, caused by structural design or charge accumulation, is the main cause of insulation problems in electrical equipment. With the field-dependent conductivity, nonlinear material is promising to be applied to electric field grade and charge suppress, which is an effective answer to the local overstress. The σ(E) relation widely used in nonlinear materials contains two variable constants, σ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> and A, which are related to the initial conductivity and nonlinear coefficient respectively. To understand how conductivity characteristics of nonlinear material influence the effect of field grading, this paper establishes a needle plate simulation model. The nonlinear material was coated on the needle electrode to uniform the extreme electric field at the tip. The results show that the excessive initial conductivity will cause a local high electric field at the interface of air and nonlinear materials, while low initial conductivity affects the limitation of the electric field at the needle tip. The nonlinear coefficient determines the equivalent electrode size generated by the local high conductivity area of nonlinear materials. The higher the nonlinear coefficient, the greater the equivalent electrode formed, and the lower the electric field at the tip obtained.

articleTitle: Beam structure capacitive electric field sensor
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Electric field measurement has applications in power grid status monitoring, equipment fault diagnosis, meteorological monitoring, aerospace launch and other fields. Moreover, electric field measurement can also be used for non-contact measurement of voltage. Traditional electric field measurement methods are often bulky and costly, and cannot be applied on a large scale. Micro electric field sensor can be applied to a variety of electric field measurement occasions, due to its advantages of small size, low cost, and easy integration. In this paper, we proposed a beam structure capacitive electric field sensor based on piezoelectric effect. Through mathematical calculations and finite element methods, the principle of the proposed sensor is verified. At the same time, we studied the relationship between sensor performance and sensor parameters. Finally, we fabricated the sensor through the design of the microfabrication process.

articleTitle: Ramp sinusoidal breakdown of epoxy resin under high voltage waveforms at different frequencies
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In this study, the immediate time to breakdown for pure epoxy resin is measured by applying a ramp sinusoidal voltage signal at certain frequency (50Hz, 500Hz and 5000Hz) until breakdown occurs. The HV testing procedures, epoxy resin sample and experimental set-up preparation and Weibull analysis of obtained results are elaborated. The experiments were carried out on epoxy samples with the thickness between 0.1mm and 0.2mm and the thickness was divided into three groups for more accurate statistical analysis.

articleTitle: Obtaining attachment cross sections of C4F7N by analysis of electron swarm parameters
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Some new fluorinated gases such as C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N and C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub>O are potential SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> alternative gases but the fundamental properties including cross sections data are still very limitted. The electron attachment process is extremely important in the kenetic of electronegative gases. We introduced a method for obtaining attachment cross sections by analysis of electron swarm parameters. For this purpose, the investigated gas was added in small proportion to different carrier gases and the effective ionization rate constants were measured, with the pulsed Townsend experiment. Based on some reasonable assumptions, we can obtain attachment cross sections by solving an integral equation. We used the finite difference approximation method to convert the integral equation into a system of linear equations.Then the regularization method was used to obtain a stable solution. We described the principle of this method in detail and applied it to the C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N. The present estimations gave us some useful information. For energies below 0.01 eV, the solution for attachment cross sections of C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N tends to converge to zero. There are three peaks in 0.01~0.1eV, 0.1~1eV and 1~3eV respectively, which is in agreement with the reference results. Finally,we discussed the usefulness of the method for the cross sections derivation from swarm data as well as its limitations.

articleTitle: Study on partial discharge pulse propagation characteristics and clustering analysis of cable
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: At present, a lot of research work on anti-interference and pattern recognition of partial discharge has been carried out at home and abroad, among which the research focus is on how to construct local discharge modes that can reflect different discharge types. For this reason, the propagation attenuation characteristics of steeply rising edge pulse in cable are firstly studied. On the basis of previous studies, the improved equivalent time-frequency feature extraction method is used to classify pulses, which provides a practical pulse classification technology for the wide-band detection based on local amplifier pulses. Through the laboratory calibration pulse and the measured data of 220kV in-service cable local-discharge, the validity of the proposed method for clustering multiple types of local-discharge sources is verified, which lays a foundation for the identification of non-local-discharge sources in in-service high-voltage cable local-discharge testing.

articleTitle: A method to accurately determine the electric field strength in prefabricated joints for DC XLPE cables
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Prefabricated joints are the weakest points of a cable line because of complex structures and composite interfaces contained. Under direct-current (DC) voltages, due to the discontinuity of material conductivity, space charge will accumulate at the dielectric interface, leading to the locally concentrated electric field and increased risk of joint breakdown. Besides, the charges will be injected from electrodes under high temperature and high field, which makes the situation more complex. At present, the local electric field in a DC cable joint cannot be precisely determined either by measuring techniques or through simulation methods. Therefore, a method combining experiment with simulation was proposed in this paper. The variation law of the field strength distortion coefficient (FSDC) caused by injected charges with the operating condition characterization parameter (OCCP) was derived, and it was illustrated by the silicone rubber (SIR) joint for 10 kV cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) cable. The maximum field strength of the joint ignoring the charge injection was obtained by COMSOL Multiphysics and then multiplied by the corresponding FSDC to obtain the real field strength. This method is useful for the accurate evaluation of the insulation field strength in DC cable joints, and it has good applicability.

articleTitle: Effect of nanofiller content on DC conductivity and breakdown strength of PP/MgO nanocomposites
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: With the rapid development of high-voltage direct-current and flexible power transmission technology, the demand for power capacitors has increased dramatically. So, developing the power capacitor with lighter weight, smaller size and larger energy density is of great significance. The dielectric material properties in capacitors are critical to the energy storage performance of capacitors and thus has drawn much attention. Nanodoping is currently a more promising method. With appropriate nanofiller content, the energy density can be effectively improved. Thus, in this paper, to investigate the influence of nanofiller content on DC conductivity and breakdown strength, we utilized two-step melt blending method and hot-pressing method to prepare PP/MgO nanocomposite film samples with different nanofiller contents. We tested the breakdown characteristics of PP/MgO nanocomposites and the microscopic structure, crystallization, melting characteristics will also be given. The breakdown mechanism will also be explained. It was found that as the nanoparticle content increases, the breakdown strength reached a maximum value and then decreased, but the conductivity showed the opposite trend. This is because MgO nanoparticles can reduce the charge injected into the nanocomposite from electrodes, decreasing the migration of carriers and then the breakdown strength are promoted accordingly.

articleTitle: Research on vibration law of converter transformer oil tank surface
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The vibration characteristics of the converter transformer are closely related to electrical parameters such as current and voltage. Based on this, the vibration change law of the converter transformer oil tank surface under different operating conditions is explained theoretically. Taking the vibration monitoring data of a converter transformer as an example, the characteristics of the vibration change in the order of time and current are analyzed in detail. The results show that there are obvious differences in the vibration of the converter transformer at different operating conditions. The research results provide an effective application interval for mechanical condition monitoring and fault diagnosis of transformers based on the vibration method, and eliminate errors caused by its own different operating conditions.

articleTitle: Lightning stroke identification for transmission line based on the joint criterion: the polarity of transients and wavelet transform energy
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: This paper presents a novel lightning stroke identification method that can be employed to local protection based on the voltage and current obtained from insulator string and transmission tower by employing Wavelet Transform (WT). The EMTP model of transmission lines is built which takes the shielding failure, back flashover, lightning stroke to the tower, lightning current amplitude, corona models into consideration, and the performance of the novel method is presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Molecular design of eco-friendly insulating gases based on structureactivity relationship
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Sulfur hexafluoride gas has been widely used for its excellent dielectric strength. However, the GWP of SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> is 23,500 times greater than that of CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and listed as one of the greenhouse gases with restricted use. Therefore, the eco-friendly insulating gases has become a hot research topic. Although g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> gas and the perfluorinated ketone (PFK) gases have attracted extensive attention for dielectric use, they have ax number of disadvantages. However, their similar molecular structure and atomic composition, which consists of a fluoropropyl group and an electron-withdrawing group, provide the ideas and reference for searching novel alternative gases. In this study, the fluoroalkyl groups and sulfur fluorine groups are used as the main groups. The electron-withdrawing groups such as fluorine atom, cyano, carbonyl and sulfur-containing groups are introduced as the modification. The hybrid designed alternative gas molecules are obtained by combining the main and modification groups. Then a set of methods predicting the dielectric strength of hybrid gas molecular models are established based on structureactivity relationship. Finally, a series of candidate molecular models with high dielectric strength and low boiling point are accurately screened. It provides new insights in designing and screening the eco-friendly alternative gases to SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>.

articleTitle: Research on the differences of partial discharge of different insulation defects under special-shaped asymmetric wave voltage
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In accordance with the installation and operation of cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) cables, the insulation inevitably deteriorates, which results in different types of insulation defects. Thus, this paper proposes a special-shaped asymmetric wave method to detect partial discharge (PD) inside internal insulation. As this wave voltage is easier to excite PD, it not only plays a sensitive and accurate role in the PD detection, but also causes less damage to equipment insulation. Therefore, it is vital for us to explore the PD of different insulation defects under special-shaped asymmetric wave voltage. Firstly, two types of insulation defects samples are designed. Secondly, the phase resolved partial discharge (PRPD) patterns are exhibited. Finally, the characteristic quantities of discharge number in the same period, discharge phase distribution range of PRPD, and maximum discharge magnitude are picked out. The results show that in comparisons with the maximum discharge magnitude, discharge number in the same period and discharge phase distribution range of PRPD, the differences of the insulation defects are apparent. And it reflects the PD differences of different insulation defects through this method. Consequently, the results of the detection method establish the groundwork for pattern recognition, which can be used for insulation defects.

articleTitle: Research status and prospect of on-line monitoring and fault diagnosis technology for transformer on-load tap-changer
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The on-load tap-changer (OLTC) is the only part of the power transformer that needs to carry out the mechanical action and its reliability plays a critical role for stable operation of a power network. A gradual increase has been observed in the proportion of transformer faults caused by OLTC faults which result in the increase in the OLTC condition monitoring issues. This paper comprehensively reviewed the recent advancements and future trends in OLTC on-line monitoring and fault monitoring technology in order to provide an important reference for continuously conducting the future research work. The structure, types of faults in OLTC, and challenges in realization of OLTC's online monitoring are described in the start. The research methods of OLTC online monitoring are explained that are based on vibration signals, other signals, and multi-signal coordination. In addition to the monitoring principals of each method, the advantages and disadvantages of these monitoring approaches and their application are pointed out. Furthermore, the challenges and potential research contents in each section needed to be taken into consideration are revealed. Finally, future trends about the exploration and application of the online monitoring technology of OLTC are summarized.

articleTitle: A case analysis on suspension discharge defect of 220kV GIS disconnecting switch
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: This paper introduces a typical suspension discharge defect of 220 kV GIS disconnecting switch (DS) of a substation in Chengdu, which is found by live testing. Firstly, a suspension discharge in the gas chamber of a GIS disconnecting switch was detected due to the presence of the abnormal UHF signal and SF6 decomposition products. Then, after the gas chamber was opened, it is discovered that the equipotential spring may have lost tension and cannot operate satisfactorily during long-term work. This made it impossible to keep the reliable electric contact between the shifting fork and the drive shaft pin, and therefore a suspension discharge easily happened at this place. The DS discharge case in this paper can provide helpful experience and reference for the detection and processing of similar defects in the future.

articleTitle: Study on the difference of DC breakdown strength between XLPE and LDPE
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In order to study the difference of DC breakdown strength between cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) and low-density polyethylene (LDPE). XLPE and LDPE from three kinds of cable insulating materials samples were selected to test the DC reakdown strength and thermally stimulated depolarization current (TSDC) and X-ray diffraction (XRD) experiments. The results showed that the increase of DC breakdown strength after crosslinking is the result of the synergistic effect of two factors. One factor is that the density of deep traps will increase after crosslinking, resulting in the increase of DC breakdown strength. The other factor is that the crystallinity will decrease after crosslinking, which will hinder the improvement of DC breakdown strength. The effect of deep trap density on DC breakdown strength is greater, so DC breakdown strength will increase after crosslinking. This work provides a reference for investigating the DC breakdown strength of XLPE and LDPE.

articleTitle: Effect of micro-nano particles Co doping in epoxy on surface flashover
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Surface flashover, which is mostly occurring at the gas-solid interface of insulators, is the weakest of the insulation system both in electric power system and rail vehicle electrical equipment due to it being lower than both solid and gas breakdown voltage. Although it has been proved that adding micro and nano particles to the material can improve the flashover voltage effectively, there still exists some terra incognita. In this paper, we change the order of doping particles to prepare different micro-nano co doped epoxy based samples. The results of dielectric permittivity and DC surface flashover hold that adding microparticles first means better performance. The nanoparticles will fill the void in the epoxy. As a result, it could reduce the free volume in the compound and increase the migration barrier of polar molecules comparing with adding nano particles first.
