The increasing barrier decreases the permittivity which is crucial to the surface flashover voltage by controlling the electric field intensity of the cathode triple junction. The reduction of dielectric permittivity reduces the distortion of electric field at the triple junction. As a result, the initial stage of surface flashover is limited because the electron emission from cathode being restrain. Therefore, the surface flashover voltage increases when the nano particles added after micro particles.

articleTitle: Partial discharge statistical characteristics of oil-paper insulation under high frequency stress
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: High-frequency (HF) oil-immersed transformers with small size and light weight, have been paid widely attention by researchers at home and abroad. The oil-paper insulation of HF transformers frequently withstands high-frequency overvoltages at frequencies of several kHz and above caused by the development of power electronic devices towards high frequency and high power, resulting in the too early failure of oil-paper insulation due to partial discharge (PD). In this study, we try to analyse PD characteristics of oil-paper insulation with HF voltages using the pulse current method. The experimental results show that the dissimilarities in PD characteristics between HF voltages and AC voltages are very evident. PD inception voltage is basically no change with the increase of frequency under HF voltages. The max PD charge of HF voltages is two times higher than that of AC voltages. PD repetition rate is two times higher than that of AC voltages. In addition, it is also observed that a frequency-induced inflection point is existed near 10 kHz. These results might contribute to the higher dv/dt, the effective duration of PD in single cycle and the number of cycles caused by the change of frequency.

articleTitle: Modelling of partial discharge behavior at DC applied voltage by using ABC model
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The increased application of HVDC components leads, at the same time, to forced usage of Partial Discharge (PD) measurement as an important tool for quality testing and reliability. Current issues are missing relations between the PD behaviour caused by insulation defects and the measured PD parameter as well as requirements for appropriate PD measuring systems. The adequate modelling of PD behaviour under DC conditions could improve that situation and might lead to deeper understanding of physical PD processes within the insulation. The paper deals with the modelling of partial discharge behaviour at DC condition by using a modified three capacitances (abc) model and compares it with its behaviour at AC applied voltage. The improved model has been used to study the effect of temperature, applied voltage, and void dimensions on partial discharge behaviours within a cylindrical void inside XLPE insulating material. The results show that under DC, the temperature rise will greatly affect the repetition rate, while the magnitude of the applied voltage is of higher influence in the case of AC. Also, the results show the magnitude of PD increases with higher void size, and the larger effect is the increase of the void radius.

articleTitle: Partial discharge diagnosis based on TMR magnetic field sensor
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The detection of partial discharge signals is an effective means to avoid major safety accidents caused by partial discharges. If the measuring device can be buried inside the equipment and the partial discharge pattern recognition can be performed, faults can be better located and repaired in time. This article intends to design a partial discharge measurement device based on a Tunneling Magneto Resistive magnetic field sensor. The main research content of the thesis includes the following four aspects: First, use Rogowski coil to analysis the electromagnetic signal characteristics of the partial discharge. Then the energy distribution is concentrated between 20MHz-40MHz. The current amplitude is milliamp. According to the current characteristics of the partial discharge, the partial discharge detection device of the TMR sensor is developed. Complete the performance test of the sensor. The sensor is used for waveform detection and data statistics of the discharge model. Discover the features in the data. Finally, the data will be classified and visualized by dimensionality reduction, and machine learning methods will be used to train the data, with a recognition success rate of up to 100%.

articleTitle: Physical parameters calculation of C4F7N/CO2 mixture
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N/CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> mixture is a new type of environment-friendly insulation gas that is expected to replace SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>. The research on the physical properties of the mixed gas has great reference value for understanding its application range and application prospects. Consequently, we calculated the constant pressure specific heat capacity of the C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N/CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> mixture under different mole percentages and different pressures by the P-R equation and the Joback group contribution method. The viscosity and thermal conductivity of the C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N/CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> mixture were calculated based on the Thodos method and Chung method, and the liquefaction temperature of C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N/CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> was calculated by the Antoine equation. The results show that the constant pressure specific heat capacity of the C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N/CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> mixture is smaller when the amount of heat absorbing, temperature rise variation of C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N/CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> mixture is greater than that of SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>. C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N has little contribution to the viscosity of the mixed gas, and the viscosity of the mixture will not change greatly with the ratio of C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N. The thermal conductivity of the C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N/CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> mixture tends to increase with the increase of the mole percentage of C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N, and the temperature rise effect of the corresponding gas mixture will be smaller. C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N has a greater contribution to the liquefaction temperature of the C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N/CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> mixture, and it will grow with the increase of the mole percentage of C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N. The calculation results in this paper can provide basic data for the physical characteristics of C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N/CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> environment-friendly mixture and their application in gas-insulated switchgear and gas-insulated lines.

articleTitle: An innovative solver for electric field computing in three-phase power systems
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: This paper presents a novel solver for calculating three-dimensional electric fields in substations and overhead lines, based on the well-known Charge Simulation Method. The software has been written using Python 3, which allows full integration with FreeCAD, and all other well-proven vector computational capabilities of NumPy. The geometric data of substations or overhead lines can be imported from CAD or SVG files (lay-out and section) and the program includes routines for automatic creation of discretized electrical conductors with a straight, parabolic or catenary profile. The other data defined by the operator are the electrical parameters of the conductors throughout the system, and the region of interest for field calculation, whose points coordinates are automatically generated along a given line or plane surface of regular form. The program discretizes the conductors into a large number of segmented cylindrical elements; each is replaced by a user specified number of equivalent charges, distributed concentrically around the element axis and with their own linear density to adequately consider the electric field asymmetries. Great flexibility to evaluate and visualize results has been achieved with high-quality 3D electrostatic field representations. The results obtained have been compared with other calculations in the literature and they were quite satisfactory.

articleTitle: Research on ultraviolet spectrum characteristics of corona discharge on porcelain insulator under different pollution degrees
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: It is well known that the contamination on the surface of porcelain insulator will lead to the distortion of electric field on the surface of insulator, and corona discharge is more likely to occur under the action of external electric field. Long term corona discharge will damage the surface of insulator, produce physical or chemical defects, and then lead to the decline of insulator insulation performance, which may eventually lead to flashover under normal working conditions. Previous studies have shown that the UV spectrum of insulators is a good means to detect corona events, and the relationship between the severity of corona discharge and the relevant UV spectrum characteristics can be used as a good index to judge the insulation state of porcelain insulators. In this paper, a UV spectral imaging acquisition system composed of high voltage power supply, spectrometer and low light level CCD camera is established to observe the corona phenomenon on 10kV porcelain insulator. Before the formal test, the artificial pollution of insulator samples is divided into four pollution levels: clean, light pollution, moderate pollution and heavy pollution. Corona discharge is observed from the corona inception level up to 35 kV. The relationship between light intensity and wavelength was collected. The experimental results show that once the corona occurs, there will always be 4–7 peaks in the ultraviolet spectrum in the wavelength range of 310–400 nm. At the same voltage level, with the increase of pollution degree, the peak amplitude and number increase gradually. On this basis, support vector machine is used to recognize the pattern of ultravio let spectrum, which provides guidance for the prediction of pollution degree of porcelain insulator in practical application.

articleTitle: Surface charge accumulation under nanosecond pulse discharge and its effect on the breakdown voltage of the gas switch
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The surface charge can reduce the breakdown voltage of the gas switch and then effect the insulation performance of the pulsed power device. In order to quantify the effect of the surface charges generated by nanosecond pulse discharge on the breakdown voltage of gas switch, this paper set up an experimental platform for charge accumulation under the action of the nanosecond pulse voltage. Two-dimensional distribution of surface charges on the tank wall after the negative pulse discharge was measured, and the effect of the surface charge generated by pulse voltage on the breakdown voltage of gas gap was also studied. The results shown that all surface potentials are negative under the action of negative pulse. The potential of the upper surface is greater than the lower for the sample, and the maximum potential of the sample surface is up to about 0.5kV. In addition, the surface charge generated by pulse discharge can reduce the breakdown voltage by 7.6% in the device insulated by air. Finally, the surface charge may have a more significant effect on the pulse discharge at lower voltages.

articleTitle: A new single-phase multi-winding low-frequency converter transformer model based on the design parameters
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Tap-changers are important but frail components of converter transformers. It is important to investigate the transients from the transformer windings to tap-changers. However, available transformer models in the Electromagnetic Transients Program (EMTP) cannot accurately and physically simulate the transient characteristics of the transformer when the tap-changer works. Furthermore, the parameters of the present transformer models rely on laboratory tests or finite element model (FEM) simulations. In this paper, a multi-winding single-phase converter transformer model based on the material parameters, the structure of the transformer, and duality is built and validated. The model can be realized easily in EMTP software and used to simulate the low-frequency transients of the multi-winding transformer considering the tap-changer before the manufacture.

articleTitle: Partial discharge pattern classification of composite insulators by electromagnetic spectrum and stacked autoencoder network
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Due to the material aging and poor manufacturing technology, there will be some defects during long running process of composite insulators. Almost all the defects will lead the distortion of the electric field of composite insulators and give rise to the partial discharge. Therefore, this paper proposes a partial discharge pattern classification method for composite insulators by electromagnetic spectrum and stacked autoencoder network. Every partial discharge will generate charge neutralization, which can excite ultra-high frequency (UHF) electromagnetic waves with a frequency of 50 MHz~3 GHz. Then, the UHF spectrum of the partial discharge caused by the distorted electric field has been measured in the laboratory using the electromagnetic spectrometer from diverse positions, for six kinds of artificially made defects. The signals are divided into peak mode and average mode. Finally, a dual-input feature fusion stacked autoencoder network has been proposed to classify the partial discharge patterns. From the result and confusion matrix we can conclude that the algorithm achieves a well classification precision. In addition, more data that helps to determine the type of insulator defect can be processed and merged into the network to reduce the amount of network training and improves the comprehensiveness and accuracy.

articleTitle: Characterization of Polypropylene/Titatium dioxide composites used for 3D printing of dielectric functionally graded insulators
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Dielectric functionally graded insulation (d-FGI) can significantly increase surface flashover voltage without increasing the geometric complexity of insulator. 3D printing technology has been proved to be an effective method for manufacturing d-FGI. The most widely used Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) technology in 3D printing can use recyclable thermoplastic materials as printing raw materials, which solves the problem that traditional thermoset insulating materials cannot be recycled. In this study, polypropylene (PP), a thermoplastic material with excellent electrical insulation properties, was used as matrix, and high-dielectric titanium dioxide (TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) was used as inorganic filler to study dielectric properties and 3D printing feasibility of the composites. The effect of filler content on dielectric properties of the composites (i.e., relative permittivity, dielectric loss, and volume resistivity) is studied. At the same time, the influence of filler content on 3D printing properties of the composites (i.e., melt flow rate) has also been studied, which is critical to the 3D printing accuracy of d-FGI. This research lays an important foundation for the accurate manufacturing of 3D printing for d-FGI.

articleTitle: Effect of light stabilizer injection technology on insulation properties of the thermal-oxidative aged XLPE cable
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: With the increase of service time, the internal additives of cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) cable insulation gradually lose, which leads to the acceleration of insulation aging. To study the effect of light stabilizer injection on the insulation performance of the aging cable, two light stabilizers were selected and added into the siloxane rejuvenation fluid, then injected into the thermal-oxidative aged cables samples under gas pressure. The electrical tree initiation voltage and the polarization and depolarization currents (PDC) of the samples were investigated after rejuvenation. The results indicated that the electrical tree initiation voltage was increased, and the UV-P had the best effect on restraining the electrical tree initiation. This was because the aromatic light stabilizer UV-P had the dual functions of absorbing ultraviolet light and capturing high-energy electrons in the initial stage of electrical tree initiation. The DC conductivity and power frequency dielectric loss factor were also increased because the content of polar substances in the XLPE insulation increases after injection rejuvenation fluid. But the increased degree was not enough to affect the dielectric properties of the cable. The above studies showed that the light stabilizer injection could improve the electrical performance of cable insulation, which was of great significance for delaying electrical aging.

articleTitle: Research on the motion behavior and characteristics of metal particles in 320KV DC GIS
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: High Voltage Direct Current(HVDC) technology has been developed and widely used since 1960s, and gas insulated switchgear (GIS) is an important part in gas insulated transmission line. One of the research hotspots is the gas breakdown and insulator surface flashover caused by the free movement of metal particles generated in the production, transportation, assembly and operation of GIS system under high voltage. In order to study the movement behavior and characteristics of metal particles in GIS, a three-dimensional finite element simulation model based on the actual 320kV GIS equipment was built in COMSOL Multiphysics, and the movement behavior of spherical metal particles was simulated and analyzed by using electrostatic field and particle tracking module. The process of the spherical particles jumping, colliding, moving and stopping in the cavity is simulated, and the motion characteristics of the spherical particles in GIS are described and summarized. Furthermore, the collision between the particles released at different positions and the basin insulator is analyzed statistically. The simulation results show that the motion characteristics of particles are different at different release positions; On the convex surface of the basin insulator, the particles are more likely to collide with the surface of the insulator, and the collision mainly occurs in the first two seconds.

articleTitle: Development of a novel optical sensor for condition assessment of insulating paper in transformers
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: This paper describes the possibility to determine the degree of polymerization of insulating paper for transformers through an optical measuring method. Knowledge of the current aging condition of the insulating paper is of decisive importance for the operational safety of transformers. Aging processes continuously reduce the mechanical stability of the insulating paper, increasing the risk of unscheduled failures. A novel, patented method was developed for the determination of the current paper condition, which allows conclusions to be drawn about the degree of polymerization of the insulating paper by evaluating reflected light. For this purpose, a light source is used and the measurement of its reflection spectrum via optical fibers and a compact spectrometer is performed. The investigation shows that the reflectance spectrum changes with the aging state of the insulating paper, in which a value can be calculated that shows a very strong linear correlation with the degree of polymerization of the paper. This form of measurement method offers for the first time the possibility to measure the degree of polymerization directly in the transformer and during the operation of the asset. Thus, this measurement method can be used to increase the reliability of transformers.

articleTitle: Gas generation in environment-friendly insulating fluid under partial discharge and sparking faults
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Environment-friendly insulating fluids have good fire resistance as well as biodegradation properties. They can also extend the insulation life of transformers and improve their load capacity, so they are increasingly used in transformers. In order to investigate the differences in dissolved gas in oil under electrical faults for different types of environment-friendly insulating fluids, this paper first determined the Ostwald coefficients of five environment-friendly insulating fluids. In addition, the discharge fault simulation platform was established to simulate three types of faults: partial discharge, breakdown discharge and surface discharge, and the dissolved gases under electrical faults were analysed using chromatography to obtain the corresponding gas components and percentages. The experiments show that there is a difference in the solubility of gases in mineral oils and environment-friendly insulating fluids. Under partial discharge, H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> is the main characteristic gas of environment-friendly insulating fluids, with CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> and C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> as the second characteristic gases; under breakdown discharge, C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> are the main characteristic gases.

articleTitle: Packaging method and temperature characteristics of miniature e-field probe with fiber-lInBo3 evanescent coupler
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The fiber-waveguide evanescent coupler (FWEC) is one of the most promising directions in optical fiber sensors for electric field measurement. FWEC has extraordinary measurement performance, including millimeter-level size, high spatial resolution, broad upper limit, and free of discrete optical elements. Therefore, it has a wide range of applications, especially for very fast transient overvoltage and high electric field measurement. However, like all kinds of optical electric field sensors, the output of FWEC also shifts with temperature. Besides, the mechanical stability of FWEC is weakened as most of the cladding of D-type single-mode fiber (D-SMF) has been removed. In this paper, the FWEC sensor with stable transmission spectra is fabricated by monitoring the real-time coupling state of D-SMF and Z-cut LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>. A uniform package coating of about 150 μm is formed by precisely controlling the injected QLE 1101 silicon gel. The stability test shows that the spectral distortion of packaged FWEC is only about 1.7%, indicating that the impact of packaging on the measurement performance is negligible. Through theoretical analysis and experimental verification, the peak wavelength of FWEC shifts linearly with temperature with a sensitivity of 0.08 nm/˚C. Therefore, the peak wavelength shift can be selected as the characteristic index to correct the measurement result in practical application.

articleTitle: Sheath overvoltage on 220 kV XLPE cable under fault conditions
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Utilization of Power Cables especially XLPE cables have grown many folds, both in distribution and transmission system. At present underground power cables are available up to 500 kV voltage rating with conductor cross sections up to 3000 sq.mm. During installation of long length higher cross section cables, Special bonding of metallic sheath is adopted to reduce the induction currents and hence to improve the current rating. Generally adopted methods are single point bonding, middle point bonding, both end bonding and cross bonding. The length of cross bonding depends on the induced voltages developed at the metallic sheaths of power cable. The induced voltage on metallic sheaths depends up on the length of the circuit, diameter of cable, current carried by the cable and the type of installation adopted. Hence computation of this voltage is required for calculating the length for which the single point bonding or cross bonding must be provided. In this paper an attempt is made to compute the induced sheath voltages of various bonding methods by calculation and MATLAB simulation.

articleTitle: Analysis of the influence of winding structure on winding vibration of epoxy cast dry-type transformer
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Compared with the traditional circular winding transformer, the oval winding transformer has a smaller core center distance and a narrower core window width. With the same core cross-section area and core window height, the size in the length direction of the core is more compact, and less silicon steel sheets are used. The design cost of the transformer has been effectively reduced, and has a smaller no-load loss. Therefore, the use of oval coils in distribution transformers has received widespread attention and promotion. However, since the oval winding adds a straight section in the middle of its semi-circular arc compared to the circular winding, and the change of the winding structure will cause the forced vibration characteristics of the winding to change. Therefore, the vibration characteristics of the oval winding under the electromagnetic force when the transformer is running are different from the circular winding. The vibration characteristics of transformer windings are closely related to their mechanical conditions. Therefore, the research on the analysis of the vibration characteristics of the oval structure winding has very important significance. In this paper, the characteristics of transformer winding vibration are studied. Based on the "magnetic field-structure field" coupling model, the transient simulation analysis of the winding vibration response from electromagnetic force excitation to the winding vibration when the epoxy cast dry-type transformer winding coil flows through the load current. The vibration characteristics of the circular winding and the oval winding are obtained by transient simulation analysis. The simulation results show that the vibration of the circular winding are evenly distributed, but the distribution of vibration and deformation of the oval winding and the circular winding are different. Due to the change of the structure of the oval winding, the mechanical stability of the winding is significantly lower than that of the circular winding. Under the excitation of electromagnetic force with similar amplitude, the vibration is mainly concentrated at the fundamental frequency, and the vibration intensity is much greater than that of the circular winding.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of space charge in XLPE DC cable under temperature gradient
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: High voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission can solve the problem of sustainable energy integration, and it is the key link to realize low-carbon power energy supply. However, under DC electric field, the insulation layer of XLPE high voltage DC cable will accumulate space charge, which will distort the local electric field and reduce the service life of the cables. Besides, the temperature gradient formed in the insulation layer of DC cable in operation will also affect the distribution of space charge. Therefore, it is significant to explore the relationship between the temperature gradient and the distribution of space charge in the insulation layer. In this paper, different temperature gradients were set based on the bipolar carrier transport model, the influences of temperature gradient on the distribution of space charge and field strength were researched. The relationships between the temperature gradient and the charge characteristics (carrier extraction limitation and the heteropolar charges generation) are discussed. The results show that the main reason for the generation of heteropolar charges is that the limit of carrier extraction, and the temperature gradient can promote the transport process of homopolar charges on the high-temperature side, thus increasing the accumulation of heteropolar charges on the low-temperature side and further aggravating the distortion of the electric field.

articleTitle: Space charge and trap characteristics of high voltage power module packaging insulation based on simultaneous measurement
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Space charge phenomenon has been brought to the forefront for power equipment with solid insulation material such as HVDC cables. However, the space charge issue in the packaging insulation of high voltage power module has not been paid enough attention to. The space charge behavior and trap energy density of silicone packaging material is investigated at various temperatures in this paper. Thanks to the simultaneous measurement system developed by our group, the space charge and isothermal relaxation current measurement of silicone samples are performed at 40, 60, and 80 °C under the applied electrical field from 3 to 15 kV/mm. According to experimental results, the space charge accumulation is getting worse with the increase in temperature and applied field. It is found that charges with the same polarity are accumulated near the electrode which affects the local electrical field distribution. As the temperature increases and the charge injection intensifies, the electric field distortion coefficient begins to increase. Furthermore, the trap distribution of the silicone packaging material is obtained through the analysis of isothermal relaxation current. The relaxation currents at various temperatures are analyzed to provide the whole picture of the trap energy distribution from 0.8 to 1.2 eV.

articleTitle: PD characteristics and defect type identification of typical defects in oil-pressboard insulation
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In view of partial discharge caused by internal defects in oil-impregnated transformers, an identification method based on partial discharge signals and patterns from three defective oil-pressboards and deep neural networks is proposed method according to the three signal patterns with excessive partial discharges. Firstly, the characteristics of the partial discharge patterns are obtained and extracted as the input. Then the influence of different parameters of the deep neural network is compared on the identification effect and the optimal deep neural network structure is found. Then trained deep neural network is used to identify the partial discharge type. The results show that the use of Adam algorithm to make the loss function quickly decline and converge, the accuracy of identifying partial discharge signals is higher than the Gradient Descent method and RMSProp algorithm. The loss function can quickly decline and converge with the learning rate of 0.001. The performance of the neural network is optimal without overfitting under the network structure of 64–32–32–32–16. The partial discharge identification rate of the optimized deep neural network is higher than that of the support vector machine and BP neural network.

articleTitle: Research on diagnosis technology of foreign matter in GIS equipment based on vibration signal
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In the process of installation and maintenance of GIS equipment, maintenance tools are often left inside the equipment. The traditional equipment fault diagnosis method can not well detect the existence of foreign matter in the equipment. Vibration detection can make up for the shortcomings of foreign matter detection in GIS equipment to a certain extent. Based on the 330kV GIS equipment test platform, foreign matters are placed inside the GIS equipment, the vibration signal of the GIS equipment shell under the power frequency voltage and current is obtained. The results show that the vibration signal intensity of the equipment shell is closely related to the applied current. By analyzing the frequency spectrum of the vibration signal of the GIS equipment shell, the influence of foreign matters on the vibration signal can be observed. When there is no foreign matter in the equipment, most of the frequency components of the measured vibration signal are frequency multiplication components of 100Hz. When foreign matter is placed in the equipment, there are more stray signal components in the vibration signal spectrum, and it has a certain impact on the proportion of frequency multiplication signal components in different frequency bands.

articleTitle: Simulation of grid particle trap for switch fault current limiter
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The switch fault current limiter can ensure that the power grid is in the micro loss state during normal operation, and act quickly when the system is short-circuit to limit the short-circuit current. As the voltage level of FCL is higher and higher, it is very important to optimize the electric field of FCL. This paper refers to the trap structure that has been studied in GIS, and creatively puts forward grid like particle trap structure, which is used in switch FCL. A simulation model is built to simulate the actual operation condition of FCL. The electric field strength of FCL with different trap thickness, slot width and slot spacing is simulated. The typical design scheme of particle trap of FCL equipment after optimization is proposed to guide the safe and reliable application of FCL.

articleTitle: Influence of gas flow on surface discharge development under AC voltage
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Surface discharge can degrade the insulating equipment and even cause their complete breakdown. Because the insulating equipment is inevitably affected by the natural environment like the wind. It is necessary to investigate the characteristics and physical mechanism of surface discharge at different airflow velocity. The surface charge measurement system which based on Pockels effect was employed to observe the surface discharge process and discharge current waveform. The dynamic distribution of surface charge at different airflow velocity under AC voltage in needle-plate electrode system were researched. It was found that the breakdown voltage increased first and then decreased with the airflow velocity. The positive discharge channels developed radially and the negative discharge developed uniformly. Airflow changed the charged particles tracks and accelerated the decay of surface charge. This is contribute to the increase of breakdown voltage.

articleTitle: AC breakdown performance of natural esters combined with different biodegradable antioxidants under accelerated thermal ageing
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Natural esters derived from natural plants are being considered as potential substitutes to conventional mineral oils, due to their less-flammable, non-toxic and environmentally friendly properties. To date, natural esters have been successfully applied in sealed distribution, traction transformers and even a few cases in power transformers. But the fact of being susceptible to oxidation presents it still an engineering challenge of replacing mineral oil by natural esters in those free-breathing transformers. At present, the most commonly used antioxidant in natural esters is BHT, but its non-degradability also brings a big problem. In this paper, different biodegradable antioxidants were added into natural esters and liquid samples filled into specially designed test cells with a volume/surface ratio of 20 mm. The liquid samples in the test cell were aged in an air-circulating oven at 120°C. AC breakdown strength (kV/mm) of the liquid samples was measured periodically during the accelerated ageing experiment. Acid value of the liquid samples was also measured to provide additional information. The results show that the natural ester with biodegradable antioxidants can not only meet the aging property, but also have good breakdown property, which is an ideal substitute for BHT.

articleTitle: Analysis of decomposition by-products and its formation mechanism of SF6/N2 mixed gases under spark discharge
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The greenhouse effect caused by SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas in the power industry can not be ignored, and the use of SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>/N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> mixture gas instead of pure SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> has become an important means. In order to explore the regulation of SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>/N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> gas mixture decomposition components, a series of spark discharge experiments were carried out. The technical problem of rapid and effective detection of trace components was solved by gas chromatograph combined with copper tube gas entrapment technology, and the qualitative and quantitative detection of SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>/N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> gas mixture decomposition components were achieved. The changes of SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>/N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> decomposition components under different mixing ratios and different spark discharge times were analysed. The experimental results show that the decomposition components of SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>/N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> gas mixture under spark discharge mainly include SO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, SOF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, SO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, CF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>, CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>, NF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O, C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>, etc. Among them, NF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> and N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O can be used as the characteristic products of SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>/N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> gas mixture under spark discharge. The density of these two components was positively correlated with the discharge times. On the basis of the experimental study, the energy of the main decomposition path was calculated by using density functional theory, and the variation law of component density was analysed.

articleTitle: Operation and monitoring technology of ultra-high voltage transformer equipment
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: As the important part of the power energy Internet, the power grid has become a variety of energy sharing network, at present China has initially formed the AC-DC UHV power grid pattern, among which over 1000 sets of UHV transformer equipment are operating. There have been several instances of failure burnout caused by tap-changers, bushings and hoist seat, and even expanded into substation fires, causing serious economic losses and threatening grid security. This objectively reflects the existing online monitoring configuration based on the body oil chromatography, grounding current of iron core clamp and temperature, which is unable to adapt to the rapid development of accurate early warning and diagnosis of faults. At the same time, high frequency partical discharge, status of bushing monitoring, tap changer status monitoring and other technologies are still in the pilot application stage. It can be seen that the existing condition monitoring technology mainly suffers from bottleneck problems such as insufficient amount of monitored states, separate design of each monitoring quantity, insufficient reliability of monitoring system, and data chimney. To address the above problems, this paper proposes a transformer condition monitoring solution to improve the reliability of the monitoring system, such as unified hardware interface, unified communication protocol, unified high standard protection, and unified data streamlining processing. The method takes into account the integrated design with primary equipment, realizes flexible and scalable edge computing, and can significantly improve the accuracy of fault detection. The standardization, modularization and openness of this paper is an attempt to supplement the existing series of standards, which can strongly support the introduction of more effective new monitoring technologies. Multi-means integrated online monitoring technology is the future development direction, and there are still many problems to be solved.

articleTitle: Study of phased decomposition characteristics of insulator surface discharge under negative polarity DC voltage
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In the thesis, discharge simulating apparatus with insulator surface defect have been set up firstly. The development process of the surface discharge and SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> decomposition characteristics in different discharge phases were investigated under insulator surface defect. The typical by-products are SOF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, SO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, CF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>, CO and CS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, and the characteristic components of insulation medium defect are CF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>, CO and CS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. The process of insulator surface discharge can be divided into stable discharge stage, flashover discharge stage and breakdown stage. During the stable discharge phase, the decomposition products are SOF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and SO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> under the positive and negative polarity, and the total concentration of SOF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and SO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> grow nearly linearly with the time. During the flashover discharge phase, the decomposition products are SOF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, SO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, CF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>, CO, CS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> under the positive polarity, and their yields become explosive growth at some point. The decomposition products are SOF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, SO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, CF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> under the negative polarity, and their yields show a steady growth. During the perfoliate breakdown phase, the decomposition products are SOF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, SO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, CF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>, CO, CS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> under the positive and negative polarity, and their yields become explosive growth.

articleTitle: Transient enclosure voltage measurement and analysis of 1100kV disconnector bus-charging current switching tests
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Gas insulated switchgear (GIS) is widely used in power system, especially in the field of ultra-high voltage (UHV). But the very fast transient overvoltage (VFTO) caused by the switching of disconnectors seriously threatens the stability of power system, and accompanying transient enclosure voltage (TEV) will also affect the normal operation of the measurement and control part. In this paper, Bus-charging current switching tests on 1100kV GIS disconnectors are performed, the tests are carried out according to IEC 62271-102: 2018. The VFTO of power supply side and load side were measured respectively, The TEV at different positions of the enclosure was also measured. At the same time, the high-speed camera was used to photograph the arc process of the disconnector closing and opening operation. The VFTO and TEV of different types of test objects are analysed, the amplitude-frequency characteristics are also analysed. According to the test results, the measures to restrain VFTO and TEV are put forward. This paper provides useful experience for the operation and design of UHV GIS.

articleTitle: High voltage dielectric response characteristics of oil-paper insulation with different moisture content
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Power transformer is the key equipment in power system. Frequency dielectric spectroscopy (FDS) is widely used in moisture content measurement for oil-paper insulation used in transformer. But at present, FDS test voltage used in the field and laboratory is low, the response signal is weak and vulnerable to be interferenced, so it is unable to accurately detect and evaluate the insulation state of large power transformer. Therefore, it is of great significance to carry out frequency dielectric response test and analysis under high voltage. In this paper, the frequency dielectric response of oil-paper insulation under high voltage is tested firstly. The influence of different excitation voltage and moisture content on the FDS of oil-paper insulation is studied, and the dielectric characteristic quantity which can characterize the moisture content of oil-paper insulation is extracted. The results show that increasing the excitation voltage can effectively suppress the noise interference on the response signal. The relationship between dielectric loss factor and moisture content of oil-paper insulation is linear. With the increase of excitation voltage, the fitting line of dielectric loss factor and moisture content moves up, while the slope of the line is almost constant.

articleTitle: Simulation research on commutation failure in fault removal
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: At present, most of the research on commutation failure is focused on the commutation failure after fault occurs. However, in engineering practice and simulation studies, it is found that commutation failures also occur while the fault is removed, that is, subsequent commutation failure, causing a secondary impact on the AC-DC interconnection system, and threatening the safe operation of power grid. Starting from the mechanism of commutation, and considering the change of electrical quantities before and after fault removal, the factors that may affect the commutation process are analysed comprehensively. Then, the influence rules of asymmetric fault type and severity, fault duration and fault removal moment on subsequent commutation failure is analysed in detail, and the simulation is carried out to verify the correctness of the analysis. Finally, the results of the research show that the commutation voltage which is most likely to occur subsequent commutation failure is different under different fault types, and subsequent commutation failure will no longer present the half-cycle symmetry rule when removing the fault during the transient stability stage of the system. Also, fast removal of fault is beneficial to the system recovery. The research results provide ideas for optimizing the parameters of DC control system.

articleTitle: Research on partial discharge simulation device and evaluation method based on GIS
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In this paper, a GIS partial discharge simulation device is designed. Based on the simulation device, a GIS partial discharge measurement system is developed. The model simulates the 110 kV GIS bus cavity. In this paper, four kinds of discharge physical models including tip defect, suspension defect, air gap defect and particle defect are designed, and the GIS partial discharge measurement system is established. Pulse current detection method and ultra-high frequency detection method are used to test and analyze the data to study the characteristics of different types of partial discharge in GIS.

articleTitle: Time transition of gas conductivity and charge behavior in SF6-epoxy composite insulation system under DC partial discharge
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The charge accumulation at the interface between gas medium and solids in DC gas insulated switchgear (DC-GIS) and DC gas insulated line (DC-GIL) is crucial in their electrical insulation design and operation. In this paper, the charging process on solid insulator surface under DC partial discharge (DC-PD) in SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas is reported. A needle-epoxy plane electrode system is installed in SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas at atmospheric pressure. The measured surface potential distribution on epoxy plate is compared with the simulation considering charge behavior in SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas such as ion generation due to DC-PD, drift and diffusion. As a result, we quantitatively clarify the charge accumulation process under DC-PD as the main source of charge carrier in terms of the activated conductivity distribution in SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas. The charging process under DC-PD is attributed to the time transition of activated conductivity distribution in SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas gap, which is approximately 1010 times higher than that in non-activated conductivity space. This means that the activated conductivity distribution in SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas is the crucial parameter that determines the charging process for DCGIS/GIL under DC-PD occurrence.

articleTitle: Influence of low frequency dielectric relaxation on electric field distribution of epoxy impregnated paper
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: High voltage DC dry-type bushings withstand high voltage and have large current carrying capacity in operation, which lead to the internal electric field will be high as well as internal insulation withstand combined action of electrical, thermal and mechanical stress. The interface effect of epoxy impregnated paper will be prominent.Under the polarity reversal voltage, the dielectric properties of epoxy composites show significant nonlinearity. At the same time, the low frequency dielectric relaxation processes such as interface polarization of epoxy impregnated paper, carrier dispersion and space charge transport appeared in the composites, which will affect the electric field distribution of bushing. In this paper, the finite element model of high voltage DC dry-type bushing epoxy impregnated paper was established. Through it, study about the influence of low frequency dielectric relaxation on electric field distribution of epoxy impregnated paper under polarity reversal voltage has done. The results show that the electric field intensity of epoxy resin was less than the crepe paper when polarity reversal voltage was just finished. When AC and DC voltages were applied, the electric field intensity in epoxy resin was much larger than in crepe paper. It shows that the dielectric properties of epoxy composites were affected by the low frequency dielectric relaxation process under polarity reversal voltage. Which leads to the change of electric field strength and affects the electric field distribution of DC dry-type bushing finally. This research results can provide important theoretical support for further improving the design and manufacture of high voltage DC dry-type bushing.

articleTitle: Transformers fault identification by frequency response analysis using intelligent classifiers
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Failures in power transformers generates high financial loss inherent to equipment cost and power interruption. Thus, the industry has been working into developing efficient and reliable monitoring techniques with the objective of detecting incipient faults. Frequency Response Analysis (FRA) is among well-known methods to detect faults in transformers' active parts. FRA is very sensitive to changes in the winding geometry and a comparison between healthy and faulty measurements can present deviations that leads to the fault identification. However, until now, FRA interpretation is performed with the aid of experts. The development of FRA and the spreading of its application in transformers' diagnostics, have led studies to focus on the advancement of objective interpretation techniques. To contribute to this matter, intelligent classifiers are evaluated over its capabilities to classify transformers faults. For this purpose, a database of measurements performed on a laboratory winding model including different faults is used. Numerical indices are used as input for machine learning classifiers. This analysis indicated that the use of one individual index is appropriate for a good classification performance using Radial Basis Function neural network. Meanwhile Support-vector machine and Backpropagation neural network performed better with a combination of indices.

articleTitle: Model-based data augmentation to improve the performance of machine-learning diagnostic systems
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Machine-learning diagnostic systems are already being used to detect abnormal conditions in electrical equipment. The challenge in machine-learning diagnostic approaches lies in dealing with small training databases of abnormal-condition samples available as the performance of the machine-learning diagnostic systems relies on the quality and quantity of the training data. One possible solution to this problem are data augmentation techniques generating synthetic data from the available data to augment the training data. However, these generic methods do not consider domain-specific knowledge about the diagnosis task. In this paper, a model-based data augmentation approach using computer-implementable, electromechanical models is presented. This approach uses statistical information extracted from the available data to sample model parameters and input variables to generate synthetic normal- and abnormal-condition data. The model-based data augmentation is showcased for detecting a distribution transformer fault. Machine-learning diagnostic systems are trained utilizing the model-based data augmentation and benchmarked with state-of-the-art diagnostic systems. The number of abnormal-condition measurements for training is limited and the performance of all diagnostic systems is analysed. It is shown that the model-based data augmentation is capable of improving the diagnosis accuracy for the analysed diagnostic task especially when only a very small amount of abnormal-condition data is available.

articleTitle: Investigation on surface charge accumulation characteristics of C4F7N/CO2 mixture under different electric fields
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In this paper, the surface charge characteristics of C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N/CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> mixture under different electric fields was investigated. The electric fields with intense vertical component and intense horizontal component were established by needle-plane configuration and two semi-circle electrode configuration, respectively. The surface charging characteristics of pure SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> was also studied as a comparison group. The results show that in needle-plane configuration, the surface charge distribution of C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N/CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> mixture is hilltop- like with a certain randomness, while that of pure SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> is bell-like. Polarity effect is found that negative charges are easier to accumulated on sample surface than positive ones in both two gases. And the polarity effect of pure SF6 gas is more remarkable than that of C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N/CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> mixture. The total amount of surface charge in C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N/CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> mixture is more than that in pure SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas.

articleTitle: Research and application of the phase-checking method based on the leakage current signal of metal zinc oxide arrester
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The phase-checking of two period signals is commonly used in power system. In order to ensure the same phase and the safe operation of the power grid in some cases, such as grid-connected of the new power plant, new construction, renovation, expansion of substations and transmission lines, and before transmission to the user, the phase-checking work must be done in three-phase circuit. However, the traditional phase-checking method is a time-consuming process and low safety factor. Therefore, an innovative phase-checking method based on the leakage current signal of metal zinc oxide arrester is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the equivalent model of the metal zinc oxide arrester is analyzed. Secondly, the feasibility of the phase-checking method based on the leakage current signal of the metal zinc oxide arrester is analyzed. Finally, the phase-checking method is applied in the substation,and the safety, effectiveness and accuracy of the leakage current phase-checking method are verified.

articleTitle: Study on the temperature distribution of composite insulator of UHV-DC line considering solar radiation
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Composite insulator is an important external device in UHV-DC transmission lines. In recent years, abnormal temperature rise of composite insulator occurs frequently in China, which seriously affects the safety of clean energy transmission. In this paper, the abnormal temperature rise phenomenon of composite insulator of UHV-DC transmission line in China, which was studied in finite element method. The influence of solar radiation on the temperature distribution of composite insulators at different times of a day, which was simulated and analyzed. It was found that the abnormal temperature rise spots of composite insulators were mainly concentrated in the fittings of grading cover at low-voltage end, individual umbrella plates, core rod, and the sheath close to the voltage-equalizing cover also have abnormal temperature rise. This paper considers that the abnormal temperature rise of composite insulators is related to the environmental temperature, solar radiation intensity and the influence of the low-voltage end grading cover.

articleTitle: Analysis of the application of the rod-rod gap structure in the protection of power transformers
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The rod-rod gap structure is a protection device that has been used a lot in the electrical system assisting the insulation coordination of power transformers. Currently, the rod-rod gap has fallen into disuse due to concerns about coordination problems, however, in old installations, they continue to be used. The objective of this article is to analyze the insulation coordination of power transformers protected by the rod-rod gap structure when subjected to electrical stresses arising from atmospheric surges, switching surges and sustained overvoltages. For this purpose, a methodology for computational modeling dielectric supportability curves was developed based on the stochastic distribution of the formation of the rupture in the dielectric medium. The dielectric supportability curves of a 138 kV transformer and a 59 cm rod-rod gap structure were analyzed over time. It was found that the protection capacity of the structure in relation to a 138 kV transformer is limited to switching surges and sustained overvoltages, in the industrial frequency. The results allow us to conclude that the rod-rod gap is not effective in protecting the transformer against atmospheric surges, as the estimated time to rupture obtained in the simulations was 26.5 μs. The methodology is capable of being replicated for the analysis of the insulation coordination of other equipment.

articleTitle: Impact of stratified frequency-dependent soils with variable water content on transmission power lines
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: This work computes the harmonic grounding impedance (HGI) and the generated Ground Potential Rise (GPR) for a cross- foot grounding system buried in distinct topologies of frequency-independent (FI) and frequency-dependent (FD) soils with variable water content. Then, the overvoltages at the transmission tower hit by two types of lightning strikes are computed for an overhead transmission line (OHTL) located above these soils. Results indicated that harmonic grounding impedance is significantly modified as the water content increases and when the frequency dependence of soil parameters is considered. It is shown that the difference between the overvoltages computed by the FI soil and those computed with the FD soil is higher when towers are located above high resistive soils. However, this difference can be neglected when these towers are located on FD soils with high humid content in comparison with those computed for the same ground modeled by FI soil electrical parameters.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional finite element modelling of electrical field intensity induced in human body with pacemaker implanted during transient processes in power network
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Electromagnetic interference (EMI) is an inevitable concern for implanted cardiac pacemakers when they are exposed to electromagnetic radiation. Our previous research indicates that cardiac pacemaker may suffer EMI from transient electromagnetic processes occurred in power system. However, the mechanism behind the generation of high frequency induced voltages in the pacing loop is still not clear. A numerical calculation for the electromagnetic field distribution inside the human body with pacemaker implanted is necessary for describing the variation laws of EMI occurred on the surface of myocardium as well as providing recommendation for protective measures. In this paper, a threedimensional finite element model of dual-chamber pacemaker immersed in human chest is created by using low frequency electromagnetic field module in COMOSL Multiphysics. The size of the human chest model follows the anatomical structure of the chest wall and the human heart strictly, as well as the physical parameters. Impulse current waveforms with amplitude in the order of kA and frequency in the order of kHz are injected into a cylinder with diameter of 8 mm to simulate transient process in power system. The physical parameters of the cylinder are the same as copper wire and the distance between the cylinder and human chest model is 150 mm. When simulating by changing the relative position of the wire and the human body model, the induced electric fields of different magnitudes are obtained. Finally, we conclude that when the wire sets parallel to the surface of the human-body, the intensity of the induced electric field in the pacemaker circuit is the largest, which can reach as high as 0.15 V/m.

articleTitle: Research on development and performance of the strain composite cross-arm in 10kv distribution line
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The composite cross-arm could effectively reduce the lightning accident in the 10kV distribution line. However, the previously research mainly focuses on the composite cross-arm for the straight-line pole application, the research on the strain tower is still rear. In this paper, the triangular cross-section strain composite cross-arm is studied through the following five aspects, which are core material properties, mechanical properties, electrical properties, interface properties and durability properties respectively. 1) Through combing with the stress characteristics of the strain composite cross-arm in distribution line, the triangular cross-section core with 98mm × 52mm isosceles was designed and pultruded with epoxy and E-glass fibre. 2) The simulation analysis and test verification of mechanical and electrical performance were carried out with dry arc distance of 600mm. 3) In order to verify the interface properties, three samples were selected to conduct 48 h thermal -mechanical pre-stressing and 42 h water immersion pre-stressing. 4) A vibration fatigue test device was designed. Six cross-arm samples were tested for 30 million times vibration at a frequency of 10 Hz. The above simulation and test results show that the strain composite cross-arm developed in this paper could not only meet the requirements of long-term operation, but also effectively improve the lightning protection level of the distributed line. Nevertheless, it is necessary to stress the stability of the end fitting crimping process in the production process.

articleTitle: A new method to detect corona discharge in power equipment
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Corona discharge in insulating material commonly occurs in power equipment, which endangers the operation of power system. Early detection of corona discharge can prevent large-scale failure, protect the expensive electrical equipment and ensure the reliable operation of power system, which is of practical significance and economic value. In this work, a new composite insulating material, poly(3-hexylthiophene)/polystyrene (P3HT/PS) blend film is fabricated, which shows observable colour changes under corona discharge. Based on oxidation of P3HT, the colour change of P3HT/PS blend film becomes more obvious with the increase in applied voltage and discharge duration. Thus, P3HT/PS blend film can be used as an estimation material of corona discharge intensity with eye observation. According to the UV-Vis spectra, the absorption peak position of corona treated P3HT/PS film is blue shifted and the film absorbance is decreased with enlarged applied voltage and corona treat duration, which can be utilized as a quantitative method to characterize corona discharge. Breakdown results show slightly decreased insulating strength when insulating polymer is coated with P3HT, which prove the potential of P3HT detector in detecting corona discharge in power applications.

articleTitle: Improved energy density and suppressed dielectric loss of polypropylene/maleic anhydride-grafted polypropylene /ZrO2@Al2O3 ternary nanocomposites
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Dielectric material with high energy storage density and low dielectric loss is the key to the development of film capacitors. Here we report a ternary system composed of polypropylene (PP), maleic anhydride-grafted PP (PP-g-MAH), and core-shell structured ZrO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>@Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> nanoparticles, which shows excellent energy storage properties compared with most traditional nano-composites. The alumina is selected as the shell because of its intermediate permittivity which can alleviate the local electric field distortion and the excellent insulation performance that may inhibit the carrier mobility of ions. Finite element simula-tions are carried out to demonstrate the influence of core-shell nanoparticles on the breakdown strength and dielectric loss. As a result, the nanocomposite films loaded with 0.5 wt% ZrO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>@Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> nanoparticles possess an excellent energy density of 1.8 J/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> at 402.9 MV/m, which is 50% higher than that of biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP) (≈1.2 J/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> at 640 MV/m); meanwhile, the dielectric loss presents an extremely low level (5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>). This research opens up an effective strategy to balance the energy density and dielectric loss for high performance dielectric nanocomposites.

articleTitle: A novel cable defect localization technique via time-frequency domain reflectometry
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
