abstract: Cables are of great importance to the transmission of electricity. To ensure the quality of electricity, the defects of cables must be found in time. Time-frequency domain reflectometry (TFDR), a non-destructive defect localization technique, is utilized in this paper. Besides, this paper proposes pseudo Wigner-Ville distribution (PWVD) to avoid the influence caused by the crossterm of Wigner-Ville distribution (WVD). And the technique proposed in this paper is proved to be effective with great accuracy after several experiments.

articleTitle: Site experimental study on smart de-icing device based on the de-icing method by the transferred current of bundled conductors
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Icing seriously threatens the safety of transmission lines. Transferring the current of bundled sub-conductors through smart de-icing device is a promising de-icing method. In this study, site experiments on smart de-icing device based on the de-icing method by the transferred current of bundled conductors were carried out in the natural environment at the xuefeng mountain national field science observatory of chongqing university. The smart de-icing device was hanged on the glaze tower and connected between the 4-bundled conductors (4×LGJ400/35) and a rectifier which was equipped with other device so that a high current is acceptable for this study. In order to complete the test loop the 3-bundled conductors (3×LGJ240/30) were connected with the 4-bundled conductors (4×LGJ400/35) and the rectifier. The site experiments included three tests: the intelligent of the smart de-icing device test (test 1), the heating rate of the conductor test (test 2) and the practical effect of melt-icing test (test 3). The experimental results in this paper proved the feasibility of the transferred current of bundled conductors de-icing method, and the smart de-icing device showed a good performance, which shows the specific potential and broad application prospects

articleTitle: Multi-physical field simulation and optimization of integrated voltage selfsharing interrupter
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In order to meet the urgent needs of small space and compact structure for the tank type multi-break vacuum circuit breaker (TMVCB). This paper proposes a new structure of integrated self-sharing vacuum interrupter (ISVI) based on the ring ceramic capacitor (RCC) and external grading field shield (EGFS). The 3D electro-thermal model of ISVI are established. The difference of electric field distribution and the equalizing effect of tank type series connection between the ISVI and commercial vacuum interrupter is obtained by comparative analysis. The influence of different structural parameters on electric field intensity is verified, and the structural parameters of ISVI are preliminarily determined. The temperature field of the TMVCB composed of the ISVI in series is analyzed by Thermal field module in COMSOL. The influence rules of the tank structure parameters, environmental protection gas type, air pressure parameters and tank layout mode on the temperature increase of different parts in the TMVCB and the ISVI are obtained. Based on national standard, the optimization design of the component which the temperature rise is relative high by analyzing on thermal field is verified. The technical scheme of ISVI for series connection of TMVCB which both insulation and temperature rise meets the requirements of national standard is determined. The paper provides the design basis for the engineering application of the ISVI.

articleTitle: ARC extinguishing performance of environmental-friendly gas mixture C4F7N-CO2 in a disconnect switch
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Sulfur hexafluoride (SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>) is known for its excellent arc extinguishing performance and insulation performance. However, SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> is a strong greenhouse gas, and its liquefaction temperature is relatively high. Therefore, looking for an environment-friendly, high-performance gas to replace SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> is an urgent problem to be solved in the field of high-voltage power switches. The current research results show that C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N and its mixed gas have great potential in replacing SF6 gas. According to other papers, the gas mixture of C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N and CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> can meet the ambient temperature requirements of the current power equipment application and has good insulation performance and low global warming potential. Although the mixed gas of C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N and CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> has good arc extinguishing performance as a whole, its arc extinguishing mechanism in disconnect switches is still unclear. Therefore, in order to verify whether the gas mixture of C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N and CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> meets the breaking performance of the isolating switch, this article focuses on the simulation study of the breaking process of the gas mixture of C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N and CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, and analyses the breaking process of different types of small currents. In addition, this paper also conducts tests on disconnecting switches under different working conditions to break small currents, and it is verified through the tests that this mixed gas can meet all the requirements for disconnecting switches to break various small currents.

articleTitle: Development of an experimental setup to study temperature distribution of liquid natural cooled power transformers
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Knowing the temperature profile of a transformer is of great interest because the expected thermal lifetime of the transformer is mainly determined by the hotspot temperature in windings. Understanding the thermal behaviours of the transformer in different conditions facilitates better utilizing and managing transformer assets for a utility in the most optimum manner. Thermosiphon-driven liquid natural (ON/KN) cooled transformers are widely used in the electric grid as they generally require less maintenance compared to pump-driven liquid forced and directed (OD/KD) cooled transformers. Therefore, a complete-cooling-loop experimental setup is developed to study the parameters affecting the thermal behaviour of an ON/KN cooled transformer. The affecting parameters can be categorized into three categories: geometric characteristics, operational conditions and material properties. Geometric parameters include the transformer thermal head and the number of discs per pass for the winding model studied. Operational conditions are considered by different loading scenarios. The material properties refer to alternative insulating liquids. In this paper, the design and implementation of an experimental setup is presented which is used to study the effects of these parameters on the thermal behaviour of liquid natural cooled transformers.

articleTitle: Research on short-time withstand current test technology of main-branch of 500kV mechanical DC circuit breaker
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: This paper summarizes the system composition and working principle of 500kV mechanical DC circuit breaker applied in Zhangbei flexible DC power grid demonstration project. As an important part of DC circuit breaker, the main-branch circuit is mainly composed of multi breaking units of fast circuit breakers in series. It is used to make and break the DC system current, and to verify the capability of the main-branch to withstand short-time withstand current is an important assessment index. The short-time withstand current is divided into two stages. The first stage test current is the overload current of 4.5kA and lasts for 1 min. The second stage test current is the current under special working conditions required by technical specifications. In the second stage, the fast mechanical switchgear needs to be opened quickly in the 3ms, and the fast mechanical switchgear needs to be closed quickly at 11ms. It is required that after the short-time withstand current test of the main-branch, no component damage or failure is allowed. The existing test methods can not fully meet the requirements of the test for the main-branch of DC circuit breaker, so it is necessary to study a test method with high equivalence to meet the expected assessment index. In this paper, through calculation and simulation, under the condition that the integral value of square and time of test current is equivalent to the value required by technical specification, the short-time withstand current test of main-branch of 500kV mechanical DC circuit breaker is completed by using equivalent test circuit. It is proved that the test method is not only of high equivalence, but also feasible.

articleTitle: Analysis of the suppression effect of voltage transformer's neutral point capacitance on ferromagnetic resonance
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: With the continuous development of China's economic construction and high-tech product manufacturing technology, the requirements for power quality are getting higher and higher. The power supply stability and reliability of the distribution system that undertakes the last mile of power supply to users are important guarantees to ensure power quality. However, due to the complexity of the distribution network topology, load variability and the universality of the grid, the operation failure rate has been very high. Especially in the 10 kV distribution system, the ferromagnetic resonance accidents caused by the saturation of electromagnetic voltage transformer (VT) have occurred from time to time, and have not been resolved, which has great harm to the insulation of distribution equipment. In this paper, according to the topological structure characteristics of 10 kV neutral point ungrounded distribution network of power station, the harmonic elimination method of VT neutral point grounding by capacitor is analyzed in depth. Through the calculation and analysis, the effectiveness of VT neutral point capacitor harmonic elimination method is clarified, but it will cause the system neutral point potential offset. The research results have great significance for improving the operating reliability of low-voltage distribution networks and eliminating ferromagnetic resonance.

articleTitle: Effect of voltage and fog application on AC flashover characteristics of polymeric insulators under artificial clean fog test
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: One of the key-stage of a good insulator design is to test their performances under artificial pollution tests based (or not) on field monitoring. According to IEC 60-507, two methods are recommended for the clean fog test: (i) Method 1 is to apply to the insulator a reduced voltage under fog conditions until the leakage resistance drops to a minimum. At this moment, the full voltage ramp is applied until flashover (FOV). (ii) Method 2 is to apply the full voltage and after applying the fog, and waiting for a maximum of one hour for the occurrence or not of flashover. This paper deals with the comparison of both methods for selecting the adequate one in order to be much closer to the field conditions, especially for the design of leakage current monitoring. Three insulators were used: silicone rubber with 4 small sheds, silicone rubber with 4 large sheds, and EPDM with 5 alternate sheds. The results show that (i) FOV voltages of method 2 are lower than method 1 whatever the type of insulator, (ii) Dry bands dynamic and discharges activity, leakage current, leakage resistance, and average power are closely linked to the used method.

articleTitle: Fault analysis and comprehensive improvement of Xinjiang power grid transmission lines easy to ice
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Transmission lines are an open system. Due to their wide coverage, they often need to span multiple complex terrains and areas. In the ice-prone areas, transmission lines are prone to ice damage failures, and in severe cases, even tower collapse and disconnection accidents, which poses a severe test for the stability and continuity of transmission equipment operation. Therefore, based on the formation mechanism of transmission line ice coating and the characteristics of the fault area, this paper analyzes the cause of ice damage in detail by means of sag observation and wind load verification, and puts forward several effective anti-icing measures to ensure the safety of transmission line Stable operation, control the power grid and social and economic losses caused by ice damage failure to a minimum level.

articleTitle: Topological research on inductive pulsed power supply
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The application of pulse power technology in the industrial and military fields requires pulse power as a large current generator. The high energy storage density makes the inductive energy storage have a broader application prospect than the capacitive energy storage. In this paper, we choose the meat grinder topology as an example to examine the circuit structure, device selection and working principle of different topologies in detail. Three circuits, stretch meat grinder, meat grinder with SECT and meat grinder with CPFU, are chosen for simulation and comparison. On the premise of 1.763kJ initial energy storage, the electrical performance of the three topologies is compared. According to the theoretical analysis, it is found that the traditional inductive energy storage pulse power supply may produce a substantial residual current in the final stage, which will have a negative impact on the output current and energy transmission efficiency. In order to turn off the residual current, a new type of pulse power supply topology based on the SECT topology is proposed. The simulation result shows that it is profitable to turn off the load current within 30 μs.

articleTitle: An electro-thermal model for dielectric heating in silicone elastomers under harmonic distorted voltages
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The electro-thermal model to assess dielectric heating under harmonic distorted voltages is based on the superposition of two voltages with variable frequencies and involves the Multiphysics coupling of electrical and thermal interfaces. The dielectric parameters of the test samples are first determined at sinusoidal voltages. Based on the measured data, the dielectric loss as well as the dissipated heat in terms of the heat source density under harmonic distorted voltages can be calculated. To verify the model, the heat source density of the test samples are also determined experimentally. The results show that the heat source density increases with higher frequencies, but decreases with enhanced temperature due to a negative temperature coefficient of the dielectric properties. Nevertheless, harmonics-induced voltage distortion has a negligible effect on the dielectric heating of the tested silicone rubber due to insignificant temperature change. The calculated results are comparable to the measured data, which indicates that the applied methods are suitable to model a harmonic distorted voltage stress. The proposed model can serve as the basis for other materials. A promising next step would be to incorporate nonlinear materials in the presented model, with the field grading silicone being a material of interest.

articleTitle: Electric field simulation and partial discharge test of 10 kV cable terminationswith hole defects
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: 10 kV cables may have holes caused by making main insulation and installing terminations, which threatens the safe operation of cables. This paper makes a cable termination with a hole, the electric field distribution is simulated to study the law of electric field with the holes' axial position. A high-frequency current transformer is used to measure partial discharge on termination with a hole. The results show that the holes' axial position has a great influence on the termination electric field. If the hole does not exceed the fracture of the insulation shielding, the maximum electric field strength amplitude does not change much. If the hole exceeds the fracture of the insulation shielding, the maximum electric field strength decreases significantly as the distance away from the fracture. When the hole is located in the fracture of the insulation shielding, its maximum field strength amplitude reaches the maximum. In this paper, two partial discharge tests are carried out on the termination where the hole exceeds 6 mm of the fracture, and we compared the results of the two tests. It is found that there are certain differences in the value of partial discharge change rule and phase change rule between the two discharges.

articleTitle: Research on calculation methods of harmonic parameters of XLPE HVDC cable
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In this paper, aiming at electrical parameter calculation of XLPE HVDC cable, the series impedance matrix and shunt admittance matrix of XLPE cable based on HVDC transmission equation are theoretically analysed. The methods of the analytical calculation and numerical simulation are studied respectively, establishing the calculation models and methods on XLPE HVDC cables. In order to compare and analyse the applicability of these methods with two numerical simulations and an analytical calculation, the XLPE HVDC cables with three voltage levels of ±320/400/525kV are taken as examples to calculate their harmonic parameters and their change regularity under different harmonic frequencies, and providing a research reference for the design and characteristic analysis of XLPE HVDC cables in power transmission system

articleTitle: Dynamic analysis of DC GIL insulator surface charge accumulation based on COMSOL and MATLAB co-simulation
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Insulator surface charge accumulation is one of the main limiting factors of DC gas insulated pipeline transmission lines (DC-GIL). At present, the analysis of surface charge accumulation mostly uses the finite element analysis software to calculate directly, but there are some shortcomings such as slow simulation and poor data processing ability. Therefore, this paper proposes a method to calculate the gas side charge density based on time-varying power flow. Through the co-simulation of COMSOL and MATLAB, the fast calculation, flexible program call and data processing of partial differential equation are realized. The transient and steady-state characteristics of surface charge accumulation of DC GIL basin insulator under different solid conductivity are calculated. The influence of voltage and gas ion generation rate on the type, quantity and steady-state time of insulator surface charge accumulation are analyzed. Finally, based on the insulator structure in this paper, the limit solid conductivity of which the surface charge accumulation is not affected is calculated.

articleTitle: Influence of trace SF6 on streamer corona development in SF6/N2 mixtures under positive DC voltages
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>/N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> is a kind of binary gas mixtures with synergistic effects, that is, a small amount of SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> can make the gas mixtures maintain the useful characteristics of an electronegative gas. This paper focuses on the study of the influence of trace SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> on streamer corona development in SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>/N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> mixtures under positive DC voltages. A needle-to-plane electrode corona discharge experimental setup was set up. Considering that the streamer corona development was more significant at atmospheric pressure, the streamer corona light emission images under different SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> content at 0.1 MPa were given. The corona characteristics in SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>/N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> mixtures including corona onset characteristics and current pulse characteristics were compared between atmospheric pressure and high pressure (0.3 MPa). The experimental results have shown that both the length of streamer channel and the number of bifurcation at streamer head decrease with increasing SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> content. Within the experimental scope, with increasing SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> content, the pulse-time parameters decrease, while the positive corona onset voltage and pulse-repetition rate increase.

articleTitle: Impact of base oil composition and additives on gassing characteristics of oil-paper insulation
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Recent years, gassing characteristics of transformer oil have been studied. However, it is different with the actual working conditions, as oil-paper insulation in transformers rather than pure oil. Oils with metal deactivator can produce large number of hydrogen, but it is barely reported that the hydrogen over set standard during the actual transformer operation. In this paper, influences of aromatic content, additives including Dibutyl paractesol antioxidant and benzotriazole derivatives metal deactivator on gassing characteristics of oil-paper were studied, and mechanism of stray gassing in oil-paper insulation was discussed as well. 80mL oil and 10 pieces of insulation pressboards were placed into a glass syringe, capped and aged at 120° until the characteristic gassing reached a stable. Then the dissolved gas-in-oil analysis test were performed. The experimental results indicated that the dissolved gas in oil-paper insulation increased with the increase of aromatic content. Unlike the gassing characteristics of pure oil, the Dibutyl paractesol antioxidant had resulted in more CO and CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> dissolved gas of oil-paper system. The study showed that both base oil composition and additives were all important factors for gassing characteristics, while lower aromatic content, moderate antioxidant addition and no metal deactivator were beneficial to reduce the dissolved gases.

articleTitle: Improving the insulation performance of epoxy resin after damp by POSS modification
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Epoxy resin is widely used as a coating for metal film resistors due to its excellent insulation performance and good viscosity. However, the commonly used epoxy coatings have poor hydrophobicity, which will reduce the insulation performance of the coating and further affect the measurement accuracy. In order to improve the hydrophobic performance of epoxy coating materials for metal film resistors, polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxanes (POSS) is used to modify epoxy resin to obtain POSS-modified epoxy resin. test results show that after adding POSS to epoxy resin, The water absorption rate of epoxy resin was reduced by 14.99% and the contact angle at different temperatures is increased, resulting in a 4.51% reduction in the dielectric constant, 4.92% increase in breakdown strength. The improvement of hydrophobic performance and insulation performance is related to the Si-O-Si structure contained in epoxy resin.

articleTitle: Modeling and parameter study of electromagnetic launch system driven by inductive pulsed power supply
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Inductive energy storage pulsed power supply has great advantages in energy density and has great development potential in the field of pulsed power supply. The model and parameters of inductive pulsed power supply are studied in this paper. Inductive pulsed power supply XRAM based on series charging and parallel discharging has the advantages of simple structure and strong extensibility. To reduce the high voltage on the switch when the large current is turned off, inverse current commutation with semiconductor devices (ICCOS) is usually adopted. In this paper, the ICCOS counter-current process is numerically analysed, and the SIMULINK simulation model of a Megajoule level XRAM inductive pulsed power supply is established. Based on this model, the parameters of electromagnetic launch system driven by inductive pulsed power supply are studied, and the results show that the output current waveform parameters and the emission efficiency of the system are closely related to the parameters of inductor. In addition, the emission efficiency can be improved by increasing the charging current, power supply stages or changing the value of inductor.

articleTitle: Successive electromagnetic transient diagnosis using unsupervised circulation-learning strategy
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In this paper, we present an unsupervised learning diagnosis method for successive EMT. This method can not only segment these EMT but also diagnose them separately. In the method, a feature extractor constructed by CNN is to extract principal features. And then, a point-wise confidence interval is used to segment successive EMT and a Rule is made to determine the digital-labels of the EMT segments based on the principal features. Eventually, a correspondence Table of digital-label and type of EMT is built to achieve successive EMT diagnosis. To train the feature extractor in the method, an unsupervised circulation-learning strategy is also proposed. The strategy can utilize unlabelled EMT to update the CNN parameters in the feature extractor. Further, the proposed method is tested under a measured EMT dataset, which contains successive EMT. The favourable segmentation and diagnosis results of the EMT are obtained after parameters in the method are determined. Results show that the proposed method is effective and accurate in diagnosing successive EMT.

articleTitle: A self-consistent approach for modeling the transient ground resistance of rods
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: A formulation based on the energy balance between losses and ionization is proposed in this paper in order to model the transient performance of a ground rod submitted to impulses of current. The flow of high current in grounding electrodes buried in medium or high resistivity soils results in electric fields of sufficient intensity to ionize the nearby earth. The ionization mechanism in the soil around the ground electrode yields a time-dependent reduction of the transient resistance, which can be held for several tens of microseconds as observed experimentally. Laboratory measurements were performed on a ground rod scale model using different values of soil resistivity. The experimental results, obtained under well-controlled conditions in laboratory, show that energy is an important parameter in grounding systems. The dynamic resistance response can be explained by the energy required to place electrical charges around the electrode maintaining the flow of current in the non-ionized zone of the earth. A simple electro-kinetic model of the progression of discharge in soils, considering the overall energy balance was proposed by the authors in previous papers, but the total injected energy was required as an input data, so the knowledge of the voltage and current were necessary for simulations. This paper presents a self-consistent formulation, which can provide an estimate of the transient voltages on a ground rod, only from the current impulse waveform, soil resistivity and rod geometry.

articleTitle: A voltage measurement method based on pockels effect for UHV AC transmission line overvoltage monitoring
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The level of transient overvoltage caused by switching operation is a key factor to the insulation of the UHV AC transmission system, which requires to be monitored with accuracy. Traditional voltage measurement methods are designed for power frequency with poor high frequency performance, which cannot obtain the waveform of switching transient overvoltage precisely. There are some alternative solutions such as the capacitive divider at the bushing tap of the transformer. However, they are not installing friendly and have negative influence on the safety of the system. A non-contact sensor to monitor the transient voltage is proposed in this paper. Different voltage waveforms are used to verify the accuracy of the sensor. The real working condition is simulated by applying the real closing operation transient overvoltage wave recorded from a UHV AC project to the sensor. The proposed sensor and its measurement system can be used to the UHV AC transmission system to monitor the transient overvoltage.

articleTitle: The molecular weight and curing dynamics of bisphenol a expansion chain modified epoxy resin affect the physical and electrical properties of their curing materials
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The molecular weight and curing dynamics of epoxy resin have a great influence on the performance of epoxy composite materials. In this study, bisphenol A is used to expand the chain modification of low molecular weight epoxy resin, the infrared spectrum, molecular weight and distribution of epoxy resin after chain modification are explored. Through the study of the curing reaction dynamics of the expansion chain epoxy resin, evaluate the curing and heat release properties of the expansion chain epoxy resin. On this basis, the expanded-chain epoxy composite material is prepared, and the hydraulic characteristics and breakdown strength of the composite material are studied. The results show that the use of bisphenol A achieves the goal of chain modification of epoxy resin, increases the molecular weight of epoxy resin, and reduces the rate of epoxy curing and heat release. When the mass fraction of bisphenol A increases gradually, the impact strength of the expanded-chain epoxy composite material gradually increased, the tensile strength and bending strength showed the trend of first lifting and then decreasing, and the breakdown strength gradually increased.

articleTitle: A digital input electricity meter calibration system based on IEC 61850 standard
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The accuracy of the digital input electricity meter is a interest bridge between power suppliers and users. Generally, by calibration can ensure its accuracy, but the research of the digital input electricity meter calibration is remain in primary stage, the calibration results can not guarantee the stable operation of the digital input electricity meter in power grid. In this paper, we propose a digital input electricity meter calibration system which can improve the digital input electricity meter calibration level. The experiment have been done to analysis its performance, the result shows that the calibration system have high reliability. By applying the calibration system to test three 0.2S class digital input electricity meters from different manufacturers, we verified the feasibility and validity of the calibration system.

articleTitle: Research on the development of photoelectric signal during typical discharges in transformer main insulations
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The breakup of transformer oil tank was mainly caused by the localized high oil pressure coming from the high-energy flashover occurred in main insulations. The existing relay protection technologies mainly focus on passive protections of faults with high energy and large current, therefore they cannot distinguish the discharge faults in the initial stage. Similarly, the online monitoring devices cannot detect serious flashover faults which occur in short-term time scales. During the development of oil/pressboard discharges, simultaneously appeared optical signals have advantages of fast time respond and strong anti-interference ability. In this paper, a transformer model embedded with a Silicon photomultiplier (SiPM), is created for modelling typical discharge phenomena in transformer main insulations. By creating protrusions on the insulating structure and applying an AC voltage of about 70kV to the high-voltage bushing, a long-gap discharge situation that may cause the main insulation failure is simulated. Results indicate that the SiPM optical sensor has the advantages of high sensitivity and strong anti-electromagnetic interference ability, and it is suitable for oil-paper insulation discharge detection under AC voltage. When the fault is in different development stages, the photoelectric signal has the characteristics of different sequence distribution, which provides a new idea for the early detection of transformer insulation defects.

articleTitle: Molecular dynamics simulation of the destruction mechanism of polyester films by reactive species in plasma under corona discharge based on ReaxFF
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: PET has excellent electrical insulation performance, which is commonly used as inter-turn insulation material for transformers. In the long-term operation of high-frequency transformers, PET is generally exposed to pulse corona discharge. During the corona discharge, the reactive species bombard the surface of the insulating material and react with it, making it decompose and gasify. In positive DC corona discharge, the most obvious erosion effect is mainly H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup> and NO<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup>, while in negative DC corona discharge, the more active ones are O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup> and OH<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup>. In this paper, molecular dynamics simulation method based on reactive force field is used to investigate the destruction mechanism of PET by H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>, NO<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>, OH<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup> and O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup> in plasma formed during corona discharge. According simulation calculation, the bond breaking of the structure when reactive species bombarded PET is analysed, and the microscopic destruction mechanism of PET material is explored. The types and quantities of the main small molecular products are counted, and the mechanism of their production is analysed. This study reveals the microscopic mechanism of the destruction of PET by reactive species in corona discharge, which provides a theoretical basis for optimizing the design of polyester films and improving the performance of insulating materials.

articleTitle: Partial discharge analysis of power electronic transformer under high frequency pulse voltage
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Power electronic transformers (PETs) are becoming popular in modern DC distribution grid due to their high efficiency and flexibility. To increase the power density of PETs, high switching frequency would be adopted for the power switches. However, this may eventually increase the risk of partial discharge (PD) as the internal insulation space is reduced. In order to investigate PD characteristics in PETs under high frequency pulse voltage, an experimental platform was set up in the laboratory, in which a twisted pair of wires model was used to test the insulation failure between windings in PETs. The PD behaviour were thoroughly investigated in the frequency range of 50 Hz to 20 kHz by time-resolved partial discharge (TRPD). The results reveal that at high frequency, the initial discharge voltage decreases and discharge repetition would increase, while the PD amplitude decreases. Moreover, the PD pulses mainly occur at the field strength inversion of the rising and falling edges, the discharge time width tends to increase at high frequency. Under high frequency voltage, the total amplitude of PD is much higher than 50 Hz, which may be the main reason for high-frequency insulation failure prematurely.

articleTitle: Repetitive microsecond pulse flashover characteristics of switch stage insulators in SF6
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Recently multi-stage gas switch has developed a failure mode that mainly results from surface flashover of the stage insulators, so the performance of the overall switch is degraded. In the following, repetitive microsecond pulse (RMP) flashover characteristics were investigated based on a RMP generator in SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> and the groove structure was put forward to improve the surface insulation strength. The test sample was arranged between a couple of parallel plate electrodes in 0.05–0.4 MPa SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> to mimic the working condition of stage insulators. The relationship between flashover voltage, flashover time delay and surface insulation lifetime with electrode metal and insulator type were obtained. It is illustrated that the function of electrode metal has relationship with flashover voltage; the increase of groove depth makes contribution to improve flashover voltage and the grooves near the grounded electrode have the best effect; wave-grooved type insulators have more excellent surface insulation strength including 6.76% higher flashover voltage and an order of magnitude higher lifetime than that of rectangle-grooved type insulators.

articleTitle: The AC and DC resistance of metal shields in medium voltage XLPE cables
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: There is no universally accepted calculation and measuring methods for alternating current (AC) resistance of metal shields in medium voltage (MV) crosslinked polyethylene (XLPE) power cables. Direct current (DC) resistance of the metal shields is generally used instead of AC resistance for the determination of allowable cable current rating and other parameters. Whether the substitution is appropriate or not, and how much error will be brought in by this processing, are still unclear. In this paper, both the analytical calculation and numerical simulation method are applied to determine the AC and DC resistance of metal shields in medium voltage XLPE cables, together with the ratio of the two, and a method for measuring the AC resistance of metal shields is proposed. The results demonstrate that there is no significant difference between the AC resistance under operating frequency and DC resistance of metal shields. Thus, the DC resistance of metal shields can be applied to replace its AC resistance in the evaluation process of the current rating for medium voltage XLPE cables, without introducing a noticeable error. Besides, the analytical calculation method is proven applicable for the evaluation of the AC resistance of metal shields.

articleTitle: Risk assessment of ferroresonance in distribution network
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In the neutral ungrounded distribution network system, the risk of ferroresonance in distribution network is rising due to the larger size of system capacity and the increasing use of power cables. This paper utilized the example of a 35kV transformer substation and designed its system model based on EMTP. It evaluated the possibility of the risk of ferroresonance in future grid by considering the change of system equivalent capacitance to ground, the selection of PT inflection point and other different disturbance excitation are considered. The results contributed to the system stability of the power grid and improved the economic benefits of power system.

articleTitle: A degradation detection case of polarization-depolarization current on 110kV submarine cables
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The traditional partial discharge detection method cannot meet the application requirements of long-length cables under the development of new generation of smart grid for the defects of signal attenuation and low accuracy. This article applied a non-destructive testing methods, PDC method, to diagnose the operating status of a 110kV cross-linked polyethylene insulated submarine cable. Four phases submarine cable were tested. Three kinds of characteristic quantities for judging the overall insulation state of the submarine cable were obtained through the polarization depolarization current curve, including the DC conductivity, the depolarization dielectric loss factor and the asymmetry coefficient at a frequency of 0.1 Hz. The results showed that the electrical conductivity and asymmetry coefficient of the four cables were within the normal range, and the overall insulation state was normal. The analysis results were consistent with the operating time of the cable, and the asymmetry coefficient ranged in 0.85 to 1.05 according to the operating life. The results provide an effective basis for improving the status diagnosis capability and fault finding level of long-length submarine cables.

articleTitle: Design of a current sensor with hybrid integrator based on a new circuit topology
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Pulse current is one of the core parameters of pulse power device. In this paper, based on a new circuit topology, a current sensor with hybrid integrator is designed, which works in LR integral mode at high frequency and RC integral mode at low frequency. First, the coil inductance is simulated using ANSYS HFSS, and the exact inductance value of the coil is obtained by comparing with the measured results. In addition, a sampling branch with low inductance is designed based on PCB board and patch resistance. Finally, the square-wave response test of the current sensor shows that the current sensor has good performance and wide bandwidth. The quickest response is to ~3ns, and the wave flattening drop within 1 μs is very small. At the same time, the sensitivity and bandwidth of the current sensor are experimentally studied, and theoretical analysis is verified. This work has important reference significance for current sensor design and effectively expands its application range.

articleTitle: Space charge dynamic characteristics of epoxy material under extreme conditions
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Converter transformer valve side bushing as a key device for connecting converter transformer and converter valve tower, its insulation reliability is vital to DC transmission system. The main insulation material of the valve side bushing of converter transformer is epoxy impregnated paper composite material. Under extreme conditions such as high temperature and high electric field, a large amount of space charge will accumulate in the epoxy composite material, which will accelerate the insulation aging of the epoxy material. In this paper, the space charge transport model of epoxy materials under high temperature and high electric field is established based on bipolar carrier transport model. At the same time, the model is improved considering thermionic emission and extraction limitation. The dynamic change of space charge distribution in epoxy composites is simulated and calculated. The simulation results are as follows: first, the results based on the improved bipolar carrier model are in good agreement with the experimental results, which verifies the effectiveness of the model; then the space charge distribution in epoxy materials changes dynamically under extreme conditions; finally, the positive/negative charge injection/extraction and the different polarity charge accumulation of the two electrodes also have different changes at different temperatures. The epoxy material used in the valve side bushing of converter transformer is simulated under extreme conditions, which provides an important reference for a comprehensive understanding of the insulation properties of epoxy composite materials.

articleTitle: Intensive monitoring and disassembling analysis of an 1000kV shunt reactor with abnormal grounding current and dissolved gas in oil
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In this paper, a fault treatment process of a 1000kV ultra-high voltage (UHV) shunt reactor is introduced, which involves abnormal growth of grounding current and dissolved gas in oil. Firstly, the fault type was judged according to the online monitoring of dissolved gas in oil and grounding current, and a fault prediction method based on the growth trend of dissolved gas in oil was proposed, which could distinguish the fault mode at present situation and provide reference for outage maintenance plan making. Then, through the disassembling investigation and the material analysis of the defect parts, it was found that the upper magnetic shield of the UHV reactor moved and collided with the upper yoke to form a conductive channel, which eventually led to the heating and ablation of the silicon steel sheet and growth in dissolved gas in oil.

articleTitle: Mechanisms behind the transition of streamer propagation mode in natural ester around the acceleration voltage under lightning impulse voltages
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: It is well known that the streamer propagation in transformer liquids changes from slow 1st and 2nd mode to fast 3rd and 4th mode when the acceleration lightning impulse voltage is reached. Previous research indicates that the streamer structures around acceleration voltages is closely related to test conditions such as voltage polarities, liquid types and gap distances. However, the mechanisms responsible for the evolution of slow streamer to fast streamer when the overvoltage increases are still not clear. A comprehensive study on figuring out physical nature of streamers around acceleration voltage is necessary for understanding the phenomena of streamer mode transition. In this paper, streamer phenomena in a natural ester at 25mm need-to-plane gap under positive lightning impulse voltages is modelled by using COMSOL Multiphysics finite element software, with field ionization processes including charge generation, recombination, trapping and charge carrier transportation being considered. Voltage level applied on the high-voltage electrode is increased from streamer initiation level to overstressed level. The simulation results show that when the acceleration voltage is reached, the average propagation velocity of the streamer has a relatively obvious change. It is indicted that thermal process plays neglectable roles in the evolution of slow streamers to fast streamers around the acceleration voltage. The mechanism responsible for transition of streamer mode is the highly increased degree of field ionization.

articleTitle: A Convolutional neural network and sequence-to- sequence model based energy disaggregation algorithm for non-intrusive load monitoring
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: With the achievement of the sensing technology and communication network, the smart monitoring and computing equipment becomes more and more common, which generates the massive data of different types and sampling frequency. The detailed information in the collected electricity usage data shows the load features and residents' electricity utilizing style, and the achievement of artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms provide better ways for process and analysis. The appliance-level energy consumption information obtained by non-intrusive load monitoring is a great benefit for energy saving by scientific management. For this purpose, this paper adopted an energy disaggregation algorithm based on CNN and Seq2Seq model to analyse the appliances' energy consumption information. We use the local attention mechanism in decoding to process the information in the long source sequence, expected to reduce the information compression and computational complexity. The proposed method for non-intrusive load monitoring succeeds in disaggregation from the total power profiles to target appliance power profiles very close and provides more effective performance than the traditional CNN and LSTM method.

articleTitle: Phase-resolved cavity PD pattern time evolution characteristics in polyethylene insulation
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In the present work, the phase-resolved-pattern of cavity discharges in a polyethylene insulation are measured and analysed with regard to how the patterns change with time, from inception to complete failure. The findings are interpreted with reference to similar findings in the literature and the theory of PD phenomena. The test samples were prepared comprising of a cavity of punched through 0.2 mm thick polyethylene disc positioned in the middle of 2.2 mm discs sandwiched between two plane metallic electrodes. The phase-resolved partial discharge patterns obtained, indicate distinct changes in the ageing process with time until final breakdown. The possible PD mechanisms associated with the observed behaviour are discussed.

articleTitle: Nonlinear characteristics of highvoltage frequency domain spectroscopy of 500 kV submarine cable
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The nonlinear characteristics of high-voltage frequency domain spectroscopy under different voltage excitation is the important indicator to reflect the insulation state of submarine cable. In this paper, the high-voltage frequency domain spectroscopy (HV-FDS) of fresh and thermally aged AC 500 kV submarine cables are measured under different voltage excitations from 1 kV to 10 kV (RMS). The complex capacitance and dielectric loss of fresh and thermally aged AC 500 kV submarine cables are analysed under different voltage excitations. Finally, the nonlinear characteristics mechanism of HVFDS of AC 500 kV submarine cable is discussed in-depth under different voltage excitations. It is concluded that the micro particles which can act as moving charges and higher voltage excitation are the premise of nonlinear characteristics of HVFDS. The nonlinear characteristics of HV-FDS of fresh and aged AC 500 kV submarine cables are significantly different under different voltage excitations. This paper can provide technical support for the diagnosis and evaluation of the insulation state of AC 500 kV submarine cable.

articleTitle: Excellent varistor calcium copper titanate composites tailored by interface engineering
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In this work, based on former results, we extend on study of CaCu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Ti<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> based composites. Since yttrium doped CaCu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Ti<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> is able to enlarge the grain boundary resistance and suppress the dielectric loss simultaneously, Y is considered as an excellent doping element to develop optimized dielectric and electrical CCTO based ceramics. For 0.5Ca<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sub>Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.33</sub>Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Ti<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub>-0.5SrCu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Ti<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub>, breakdown field is as high as 35.82 kV·cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> and nonlinear coefficient is 14.65 in the current range of 0.1−1 mA. The withstand voltage of single grain boundary raises from 4 to 24 V with higher Y content. Moreover, relaxation process is systematically studied through electric modulus spectra and activation energy calculation. CaCu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Ti<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> composite system composed of Y-doped CaCu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Ti<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> and SrCu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Ti<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> is ascribed as a reasonable system to improve varistor properties via interface engineering.

articleTitle: Hydrophobicity and density measurements on new and field aged medium voltage composite insulators
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: This paper investigates the aging of the HTV silicone rubber with ATH filler housing of brand new and naturally field-aged medium voltage composite insulators. Three different tests were performed for the purpose of this investigation. Visual inspection, as well as hydrophobicity, according to the spray method of IEC 62073, and density measurements, according to method B of ISO 2781, were conducted. The composite insulators used for this research work were two new (unused) and six naturally aged line-post and suspension composite insulators, made by four different manufacturers. The results showed that visual inspection, in combination with measurement of hydrophobicity, can be a good indicator for the aging of composite insulators. In addition, it was concluded that density of the housing material does not seem to depend on the aging of the insulators, as well as on the part of the insulators from which the test piece is extracted. Finally, density can give a first indication about which material is used as housing for composite insulators.

articleTitle: Detection of dissolved acetylene in transformer oil based on photothermal interferometry spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Power transformers are important equipment in power system, which usually are oil immersed. When there are faults happening in the oil-immersed transformer, hydrocarbon gases will generate and dissolve in oil. Nowadays, the purpose of proposing high-sensitive and compact optical gas sensors for online monitoring has drawn much attention. In order to realise the purpose of trace acetylene detection, a novel gas sensor based on hollow core photonic crystal fiber (HC-PCF) and photothermal interferometry (PTI) spectroscopy are studied theoretically. A continuous laser, whose wavelength is around the P(9) absorption line of C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> at 1530.371 nm, is used in this paper to stimulate photothermal effect. A theoretical model is developed and used to simulate the temperature changes caused by photothermal effect and phase modulation in a one-meter-long HC-PCF filled with trace acetylene. The PTI phase modulation process for different laser duration, output power of the probe beam and pump beam are modelled. It is theoretically possible to achieve ppb level detection of C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> with a one-meter-long HC-PCF, and it provides an alternative method for transformer dissolved acetylene online monitoring

articleTitle: Short circuit protection of high-voltage high-power three-level inverter system
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The penetration level of high-voltage and high-power three-level inverter system in power electronic conversion system has been improved continuously because of its flexibility in power conversion. And it is widely used in renewable energy power supply system, flexible AC transmission system, uninterrupted emergency power supply, AC-DC-VVVF speed control and other fields. However, the short-circuit fault forms of three-level inverter system are various and the traditional protection methods do not have the characteristics of systematization and integrity. Aiming at the above problems, based on the analysis of the main circuit structure and working principle of the three-level inverter system, this paper divides the system into two parts: the front-end rectifier side and the inverter output side, and studies the various types of short-circuit faults existing in these two parts. The mechanism and characteristics of short-circuit current contributed by corresponding phase-shifting transformers, DC busbars and switching devices are analyzed. On the basis of the traditional protection principle, a multi-compound overcurrent protection method for short circuit fault of power switching devices, high-power transformers and AC/DC transmission lines is proposed. A complete short-circuit protection configuration scheme for three-level inverter system is constructed. Finally, a fault simulation model was built by Matlab /Simulink and a dynamic test was conducted to verify the feasibility of the protection principle presented in the paper.

articleTitle: The evaluation of the buffer layer chemical corrosion for HV XLPE insulated cable with corrugated aluminium sheath structure
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Aluminium (Al) corrugation is one of the mainstream sheath structures in high voltage cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) insulated cable in China, owing to its advantage of good bending performance. Recently, the reliability of the cable with such a corrugated Al sheath has been suspected, since the buffer layer ablation was found many times in the failure cables with such a sheath structure. This study attempts to investigate the underlying mechanism of such a buffer layer chemical corrosion phenomenon through reproducing the ablation in laboratory. For indication upon the relationship between ablation and corrosion, a corrosion device with sheath-buffer-layer model sample is designed and the similarity of the ablated samples from laboratory and failure cables is analysed by Optical-Microscopic (OM) and Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM), revealing corrosion is one of the causes of ablation. After reaction, the gas is pumped into Gas Chromatography (GC) Analyser and the reaction product is detected by X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS). The test results show that the H2 content in the gas after reaction is obviously higher than that in air and the composition of ablation product from laboratory and failure cables is similar, which provide proofs for chemical reaction.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the metal oxide surge arresters degradation based on the loss tangent
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Metal Oxide Surge Arresters (MOSAs) are equipment used to protect equipment of Electrical Power Systems (EPSs). In this work, a technique is proposed to assess the level of MOSAs degradation based on the loss tangent calculation. The degradation of surge arresters, as well as other electrical equipment, can also be assessed by means of the loss tangent that varies with the voltage and the level of degradation. Thus, its value tends to increase according to the time of use of the equipment. A high value of the loss tangent is indicative of a failure. For the development of the proposed technique, tests in a high voltage laboratory were carried out in order to build a database. In these tests, different operating conditions were simulated to verify the behavior of the loss tangent curve, considering the surge arrester as being in good and defective condition. Based on the values obtained in the tests, it was observed that for each operational state of the evaluated components, different curves of the loss tangent were obtained, in addition to verifying that the more degraded the surge arrester is, the greater the value of the loss tangent. Thus, the loss tangent can be used to assess the operational condition of the MOSAs.

articleTitle: Recognition of partial discharge of XLPE cable based on ResNets
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The most effective method for the defect detection of XLPE cable is to perform partial discharge detection. However, it is difficult to identify partial discharges induced by different types of faults in XLPE cables, especially for certain types of cable insulation faults with high similarity. In view of the common insulation faults and partial discharge characteristics of XLPE cables, four different models are designed and an experimental platform is built to collect partial discharge signals. Taking the partial discharge pulse waveform as a sample, a defect recognition method for XLPE cables based on an improved ResNets is designed. The experiment compares the recognition effect of the ResNets and the classification method based on timefrequency features and analyzes the applicability of the recognition method to various faults and the influence of the training sample size on the recognition model. The experimental results show that the recognition method based on the improved ResNets can deeply dig the effective features of the partial discharge pulse and the recognition accuracy is higher than that based on the time-frequency feature of the SVM and the BPNN neural network classification method and it is also higher than that based on the convolutional neural network. The recognition method has a good recognition effect for all four types of faults and the recognition accuracy and recognition efficiency are greatly improved with the increase of the training sample size.

articleTitle: The influence of impulse polarity on the degradation of varistors
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In order to explore the influence of the polarity of impulse current on the degradation of Zinc-oxide varistors, a test was performed on the same type of Zinc-oxide varistor samples by alternating positive and negative impulses during the impact process. The change trend of the three parameters of the samples under different impulse backgrounds was different. Under the action of 8/20μs, 3.5kA single positive polarity impulse, the leakage current exceeded 100μA after about 105 impacts. When the positive and negative polarity impulses alternated at 5/5, the impact life increased to about 215 times. And the speed of change of the three parameters slowed down. We find that the use of alternating positive and negative impulses can increase the number of impact resistance of the varistor. In addition, the life of varistors is prolonged with the increase in the number of negative impulses in each group of impacts and the increase in the alternating frequency of positive and negative impulses.

articleTitle: A hybrid analytical model for estimating the shielding effectiveness of an irregular cavity structure with aperture arrays
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: At present, the scale of Chinese power grid continues to expand and the transmission voltage level continues to improve, which leads to increasingly serious electromagnetic interference problems faced by some secondary equipments, especially the secondary protection devices and monitoring communication devices installed in UHV substation. In order to protect these secondary devices from the interference of external electromagnetic waves, metal shielding cavities are usually used to improve the shielding effect. However, considering the need of heat dissipation and ventilation, the shielding cavity has aperture arrays. In addition, the appearance of the cavity is not only a regular structure. According to the characteristics of an irregular cavity with an aperture array, a hybrid analytical model of the shielding effectiveness (SE) is established. Firstly, the equivalent circuit model is gained in the light of the cavity structure, in which the aperture array is regarded as admittance and the cavity is equivalent to a short-circuited waveguide. Then, the analytical expression of shielding effectiveness is derived. Finally, the results show that the analytical model is in good agreement with the CST simulation in typical cases under the dominant TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub> mode. Besides, as the height of the convexity structure increases, the resonant frequency of the cavity will shift; the lossy dielectric layer can enhance SE of the resonance point. This method provides an analytic approach for designers to speed up the design process of the irregular cavity structure with an aperture array.

articleTitle: Influence of aging on prebreakdown characteristics of ester liquids with experimental and statistical analysis
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: This study emphasizes the pre-breakdown phenomenon of low pour point synthetic esters with thermal degradation for potential usage in cold climatic regions. It is to be mentioned that two synthetic esters having a pour point less than -60°C are chosen for this work. The investigations are aimed at understanding the pre-breakdown behaviour of these very low pour point liquids at room temperature. The testing is performed using a point-plane electrode configuration under AC stress in a hermetically sealed test cell. To understand the influence of thermal degradation, the insulating liquids are subjected to a controlled thermal stressing under sealed conditions. The measurements are reported at different thermal aging duration (2 weeks, 4 weeks, and 6 weeks) at a tip of radius 5.46 μm and 10.75 μm with an inter-electrode distance of 10 mm. The measurements include partial discharge inception voltage, breakdown-streamer-inception voltage, and acidity of the liquids at different aging conditions. The influence of thermal degradation on the pre-breakdown characteristics of the fluids is reported. In addition, a two-way ANOVA (with interaction) statistical analysis has been performed on the experimental data.

articleTitle: Research on the thermal field distribution of the current-carrying fittings with different heat dissipation structure
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: In ultra-high voltage(UHV) power transmission, there are many types of current-carrying fittings in converter stations. Different types of electric power fittings are designed for different areas, and the number of them in service is relatively large. The heat caused by factors such as size and contact performance of fittings seriously affects the safety of power transmission. Accidents are prone to occur under hot temperatures and high electrical load in summer. In this paper, the electric-thermal field of the clamp-type fittings is calculated, and the influence of different heat dissipation structures on the temperature rise characteristics of the fittings is studied. The effects of clamp type and heat dissipation fins on heat dissipation area and heat dissipation performance are compared and analyzed. In addition, the influence of the material of the terminal board on the temperature distribution is studied. As the contact resistance increases, the temperature difference between clamp without heat dissipation fins and clamp with heat dissipation fins increases linearly. This research can provide reference for the structural design of electric power fittings, especially clamp-type fittings.

articleTitle: Research on the detection method of 500kV composite insulator's decay-like fracture
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Composite insulators play an essential role in insulation and load-bearing in transmission lines, and their operating status directly affects the safety and stability of the power grid. This paper uses an insulator of decay-like fracture to measure the temperature and discharge under different conditions by visual inspection, ultraviolet detection, infrared detection, and electric field detection. Detailed morphology of the insulator of decay-like fracture is obtained. The results show that the deterioration of the sheath is considerably related to the surface contamination or leakage current. It is an effective method to determine the deterioration of composite insulators when the temperature and temperature rise of composite insulators are abnormal (for example, T>50°C, ΔT>30°C). Under DC conditions, the temperature rise and discharge are much lower than those of AC, indicating that the temperature rise of the insulator is mainly generated by dielectric loss heating caused by the polarization effect of the insulating dielectric under the impact of the alternating electric field. The measurement results are significantly affected by the test conditions. It isn't easy to judge whether composite insulators are fractured or not by using electric field distribution and UV measurement on site.

articleTitle: Temperature dependency of the frequency response characteristic of high voltage inductive instrument transformers and RC dividers
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: This paper discusses the temperature dependency of the ratio error and phase displacement of the frequency response characteristic. The measurement of the frequency response is done by a Sweep Frequency Response Analysis (SFRA) device. Furthermore, a method called vector fitting is used to approximate the measured curve and model the temperature dependency. This done by introducing an electrical equivalent circuit of the inductive voltage transformer.

articleTitle: Variation of chemical bonds of oil-paper insulation in the process of thermal aging: A molecular simulation
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Molecular simulation is utilized to study the change in the number of chemical bonds of oil-paper insulation during thermal aging process. First, a molecular system of 80 hydrocarbon molecules including paraffin, naphthenes, aromatic hydrocarbons and cellobiose is constructed, and obtained a reasonable structure through system optimization. Subsequently, the pyrolysis process of the molecular system is simulated at the temperature of 1500 K, 1800 K and 2000 K respectively using the reactive force field ReaxFF. The simulation results demonstrate that at different temperatures, the number of various chemical bonds changes consistently with time, and the change in the number of chemical bonds will affect the absorption peaks of infrared spectrum of oil-impregnated paper in certain bands. The simulation results not only reveal the law of chemical bond changes during the aging process, but also validate the feasibility of infrared spectrum for the diagnosis of material aging.

articleTitle: Micro electric-field sensor based on converse piezoelectric effect
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The measurement of electric field has important value for power grid information measurement, equipment fault diagnosis, meteorological monitoring, etc. Meanwhile, electric field measurement can also be used for voltage measurement. Traditional electric field measurement methods, such as field mills, are bulky and costly, and will cause electric field distortion. Micro electric field sensors have advantages of low cost, small size and easy mass production. At the same time, miniature sensors can reduce electric field distortion. Therefore, micro electric field sensors can be used in the applications such as large-scale sensing arrays, internal measurement of equipment, etc. In this paper, we proposed a novel micro electric field sensor based on PVDF film and piezoresistive effect. The proposed sensor has the advantages of wide frequency bandwidth and wide measuring range. Through micro-fabrication, the sensor can be mass produced.

articleTitle: The role of filler dissipation in material properties of ethylene-propylene-dine monomer for cable insulation
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The flexible and torsion resistant cable needs to withstand high electric field and high torque operating conditions. In order to meet the requirements of insulating materials, some fillers are added to ethylene-propylene rubber, and it is necessary to study the effect of fillers on the electrical properties of ethylene-propylene rubber. In this paper, we studied the physical properties of substrate material, filler distribution, dielectric properties and cable pressure resistance and so on. It can be concluded that the segment length dispersion of the ethylene-propylene rubber base material affects the processing performance of the material, and the inorganic agglomeration and pores has impact on the dielectric performance of the material.

articleTitle: Research on vibration characteristics of dry-type air-core reactor under turn-to-turn short circuit fault
