publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: With the increasingly wide use of dry-type air-core reactor, the turn-to-turn short circuit fault of reactor is gathering more attention. Dry-type air-core reactor is in vibration state during the normal operation, and its vibration characteristics can reflect the state of the reactor. In order to further research the vibration characteristics of reactor under turn-to-turn short circuit fault, a reactor experimental platform based on laser doppler vibrometer is built to get the vibration distribution of dry-type air-core reactor under normal operation and turn-to-turn short circuit fault. The research results show that the vibration speed is proportionate to the square of current in reactor; the vibration distribution is affected by the reactor's structure and current frequency. The current distribution and vibration characteristics will greatly change when turn-to-turn short circuit fault occurs. The research reveals the vibration characteristics of reactor under turn-to-turn short circuit fault, which provides a reference for the research of reactor condition monitoring method based on vibration characteristics.

articleTitle: Prediction of pollution flashovervoltage based on multiple characteristics of leakage current
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: With the accumulation of dirt and chemicals from the environment, outdoor insulator pollution flashover accidents tend to occur, which are threatening the operation safety of the power system. In this paper, a model is presented to predict the pollution flashover voltage by analyzing multiple characteristics of leakage current under AC operating voltage. By means of setting different equivalent salt deposit density(ESDD) and non-soluble deposit density(NSDD), insulators could be tested under simulated environment. Then, leakage current flowing along the surface of composite material insulators(FXBW4-10/70) can be monitored when an increasing voltage is applied. According to the time and frequency domain analysis, different parameters, i.e. the root mean square(RMS), proportion of harmonics and so on can also be measured. Finally, by adopting the theory ofprincipal component analysis(PCA) and artificial neural network(ANN), the value of pollution flashover voltage is predictedaccurately with simplifying data sets. This model modifies traditional diagnostic patterns which are only connected with singlecharacteristic and it is expected to become a multi-characteristic method for the prediction of pollution flashover voltage in thepower system.

articleTitle: Analysis on the locomotion of cable tunnel inspection quadruped robot based on deep reinforcement learning
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: The quadruped robot applying the expert skill learning system can learn and generate adaptive skills from a group of representative expert skills, screen and master these combined skills through deep reinforcement learning, so as to select different skills in different environments to move in stranger environment. This approach leverages the advantages of trained expert skills and the fast online synthesis of adaptive policies to generate responsive motor skills during the changing tasks. The cable tunnel unmanned inspection quadruped robot is equipped with a 5-DOF mechanical arm with a sensor module on the top to realize the cable condition detection. The combination of the intelligent sensors can make the robot obtain the ability of environment perception similar to human beings, so that the quadruped robot can complete the instructions safely and accurately in the cable tunnel environment, collect and analyse the environment and cable condition parameters, find problems and give feedback in time.

articleTitle: Study on the partial discharge recognition for special-shaped voltage method
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: There is less research on partial discharge (PD) detection under special-shaped wave voltage and corresponding pattern recognition of insulation defects in the current literature. A special-shaped wave voltage method is proposed that is non-destructive testing characteristics, which can be applied to the PD detection of insulation defects. This paper investigates pattern recognition of insulation defects for the special-shaped wave voltage method. First, we analyzed the principle of PD pattern recognition, the PD pattern structure, feature extraction and classifier selection. Subsequently, by using the inherent pattern classification and noise suppression capabilities of the BP neural network, the extracted feature vectors are studied. Finally, the accuracy rate of pattern recognition of PD types of each defect is emphatically compared and analyzed. This study has shown that the pattern recognition algorithm of the BP neural network can be applied to the PD pattern recognition under special-shaped wave voltage of insulation defects, and the accuracy rate of pattern recognition under optimal special-shaped wave voltage is higher than under power frequency AC voltage. Therefore, the PD pattern recognition under special-shaped wave voltage has practical application value.

articleTitle: Signal attenuation and distortion in coaxial cables for high voltage measurements
publicationTitle: 22nd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2021)
abstract: Coaxial cables of about ten meters in length are commonly used in high voltage laboratories to interconnect high voltage lightning impulse dividers output to the digital recorder located in the control room. Common practice in testing laboratories is to check the characteristic impedance of the measuring coaxial cable to analyse if it is matched to the low voltage arm of the divider and to the measuring instrument. In addition, cable shielding must also be checked to proof immunity against interference signals, specially, when the disruptive a discharge occurs. Although it is not usual in testing to consider the signal attenuation caused by the measuring coaxial cable, it should be considered in calibration measurements or when the cable is too long (longer than 15 m). Effects caused by a measuring coaxial cable when a high voltage lightning impulse is measured can be determined by modelling.
